text: "Good night, Arueshalae."
"I hope you have a dream tonight. Any dream."
"It's so wonderful not to be alone anymore."
"Desna, patroness of travelers! I thank you for bringing our paths together."
"I still cannot dream, Desna. I have not earned the right. I have not solved your riddle."
"Well, I can at least stand watch over my friends and guard their slumber."
"What's this — a butterfly? How did it get here?"
"Could it be? Is the goddess watching over me?"
"When I feel like I'm struggling with the desire to do evil, I look at the stars or the clouds."
"I like it when clouds are in the shape of something else. Like a castle, a mountain... a fat, fluffy rabbit!"
"If you ever feel like the world outside the walls of your mansion is alien and incomprehensible, come and talk to me. I know all about deception and betrayal, I can protect you."
"You wish to be my friend? How charming... I would simply love to share girlish confidences with you... And hear all about the deep, dark secrets of your past."
"Am I imagining things, or did I see a vicious gleam in your eyes? Where did that come from?"
"You're mistaken. How could a young lady who has spent her life cloistered and wanting for nothing have even an ounce of viciousness in her?"
"Sometimes I watch you in combat and I get the impression that fighting demons brings you pleasure. Do you truly enjoy it?"
"Of course I do. I am defending my home, fulfilling my duty. I feel the thrill of righteousness. No need to fret over it, you wouldn't understand."
"The word 'friend' is so unfamiliar. There is no real friendship in the Abyss. I would love to call someone my friend..."
"We have so much in common, Arueshalae. I have spent my entire life in seclusion and have never had anyone to call a friend either. Not a single soul."
"Can shamans feel lonely? They are surrounded by spirits who wish to talk."
"Have you ever heard the expression 'lonely in a crowd'? It can be the same with spirits."
"Please, don't look at me like that. I can read your desires plainly on your face."
"Do you think your face does not betray your inner thoughts? A wolf can befriend a flock of sheep, but it will always see them as lumps of meat. Wouldn't you agree?"
"You must thank fate every day for blessing you with the celestial blood in your veins."
"Hardly. I stopped doing that when I was told for the thousandth time that I was a disgrace to my blood and my lineage."
"Daeran, I can't understand why blood makes some mortals better than others. What do a person's origins have to do with their worth?"

"Some people's ancestors simply had sharper elbows and better luck than others, and they codified a system whereby they and their descendants would rule over everyone else. Not that I'm complaining, of course."
"I have heard that human mothers love their children unconditionally and absolutely. Was your mother like that?"
"Consider this a free lesson in Golarion etiquette: we do not speak of other people's dead mothers unless we are sure our interlocutor will welcome it."
"It seems like you are deliberately goading me, trying to make me fall, Daeran. But why?"
"Because I am a terrible person, darling, haven't you realized that yet?"
"I've wanted to comb your hair for so long... but I'm afraid I might hurt you."
"Can you do a braid? If you know how, I'll endure it."
"After everything that happened to you, you could have become a very angry person... But you didn't. Where does all your compassion and love come from?"
"I don't know. What about you? You're very kind, even though a horrible thing was done to you: you were forced to be a demon."
"Another campsite where I will pray for Desna to send me a dream. And another disappointment when it doesn't come."
"I have scary dreams sometimes. Or sometimes I have good ones, but then I'm sad when I wake up and realize they're not real... Maybe having no dreams is better?"
"I think Soot likes me. Why do you think that is?"
"You're good and you have wings. She probably thinks you're a big, beautiful bird."
"Before, I lived as I had to, never thinking of how quickly time passes for mortals. Do you sense time the same way demons do?"
"Time is a strange thing for everybody... but I think bad things seem to last a long time for both demons and mortals, and good things are over in the blink of an eye."
"Why do mortals always leave the ones they love? Isn't being with the people you love the ultimate happiness?"
"Are we built to be happy? The way I see it, we're born so that we can spend our whole lives floundering and trying to loosen the garrote of unfulfilled desires that's wrapped around our throats."
"When you say that I'll never atone for what I've done, I think you're talking about yourself. It's your chance of redemption that you don't believe in. But I can change — so can you."
"Are you joking? Now a demon's trying to tell me how to live my life? I've never met a bigger bunch of moralizers!"
"I know you don't trust me, but... we're very similar. We're both strangers in this crusade."
"You got that right. A hired killer and a demon as the crusade's brightest hope. Whatever happened to the days when saving the world was left to righteous heroes?"
"You think that by trying to do what is right, I am lying to myself? You're wrong."
"Well, I could make an effort and join up with the paladins. The question is about when, not if, I'll get tired of pretending to be something I'm not."
"Why are you the person who trusts me least in this party, Greybor?"
"Because I know better than anyone the things miscreants say to avoid punishment — 'I want to change.' That's what they say."
"Despite their differences, your parents truly loved each other. How I wish I could experience that kind of love!"
"You don't know what you're wishing for. The best outcome from that kind of love is a good-looking child like me. The worst outcome... well, let's just say no love is worth that."
"Your people have suffered greatly, but they never forgot their mission. It is astonishing how strong mortals can be when they have hope!"
"My people would be surprised to hear you say that. Mongrels lost any hope they had a long time ago, they're just afraid to admit it."
"Lann, can you please explain why mortals insist on so many different forms of address? Sir, madam, my lord... I can barely keep track of them all."

"I ask myself that same question. I think it's just a stupid uplander custom. Sometimes I get the feeling that mortals make their language as complicated and confusing as possible to make outsiders easy to spot."
"There is something inside you, Lann. Something I have not seen in other mortals."
"My unparalleled beauty? I knew that's what you meant!"
"You were right when you said the starry sky was mesmerizing. It's like you're seeing myriad worlds at once!"
"If only somebody had found a way to sail across the night sky in a boat, from one star to another..."
"Sometimes I want to be like you, Nenio. I want to learn how to forget things I'd rather not think about. Some of my memories are a heavy burden to bear."
"In my expert opinion, you enjoy contemplating your past and the results of your actions, and conducting self-analysis. If you truly wanted to forget, you would have done it already."

"Nenio, you never ask me questions about the Abyss. Every crusader brave enough to talk to me asks me what it's like there, but you never do. I don't mind either way, but why doesn't the Abyss interest you?"
"My project is called the Encyclopedia GOLARIONNICA. The Abyss is not Golarion. That information is beyond the scope of my current research."
"Nenio, do your notes contain any mention of demons who have... changed?"
"I have come across no such evidence. But did you know that the promise of false redemption is number 17 in the list of most common ploys used by demons to trick gullible mortals?"
"You study the world around you with such dedication... you must truly love it."
"Love, hmm, love... you have reminded me of something, demon girl, but... ah, yes! I must finish writing my entry about the Wound's influence on ant reproduction!"
"You said you only forget things that are not important. But sometimes the importance of some things is not apparent right away."
"Perhaps I do forget some important things from time to time. Or perhaps I do not. I don't remember."
"I know you hate demons, but since we're fighting together, perhaps we could..."
"No. We could not."
"Men and women often look at me with lust in their eyes. But not you. I find being with you calming, surprising as that may sound."
"Unacceptable. A demon should feel fear when in proximity to a Hellknight."
"I'll stand watch while all of you rest."
"You think we're going to let you stand watch alone? We've still got some sense left in us."
"I know you do not believe that a demon can change their nature. But aren't you different from your own kind, Hellknight?"
"I do not engage in rhetorical games. He who enters into an argument with a demon as an equal has already lost."
"I do not flagellate myself like you do, but... deep in my soul, I am just as ruthless toward myself."
"If I were a demon, those words would immediately precede an attack on my intended Hellknight victim."
"All the paladins I've met before behaved very piously. They abhorred frivolity of any kind. You're not like that at all. You're not afraid to be yourself."
"The paladins you're talking about... they were easy to break, right? It's easy to break someone who's running from themselves."
"Do you really have faith in me, Seelah? But why? You're a paladin, can't you sense the evil in my heart?"
"You don't have to be without sin to be good, sister. And to start on the path to atonement, you first need to admit that you have something to atone for."
"But what if I once... killed one of your fellow paladins? Someone you knew?"
"Well, I won't lie, it would be a hard pill to swallow. But we'd just need to try even harder to honor your victim's memory."
"I like hearing stories of your adventures. You have helped so many people!"
"Do you know what the worst part is? It always seems like I could have helped more of them."
"You took a leap of faith when you accepted me, Seelah. Aren't you afraid I will lose control? Then you would feel even worse than if you had never trusted me."

"What would feel worse is if I had cut you down on the spot, and then spent the rest of my life tormented by the thought that I hadn't given you a chance when you sincerely wanted to change your nature."
"You're a good man, Sosiel. But I'm tormented by thoughts of how I would have broken you, how I would have destroyed you and mocked your goodness... I feel like I've wronged you."
"I know. The old Arueshalae would have done those things. But you are a different person. I can see that. I trust you."
"You show so much concern for me, Sosiel. Is that because my appearance is beautiful and your goddess teaches you to revere beauty?"
"Yes and no. You are beautiful, it's true, but not because of your appearance."
"You're much younger than me, but you seem so much wiser. Sometimes I feel like a child compared to you."
"Immortals mature differently than ordinary humans. Even Shelyn's views changed over time. It took her millennia to understand that true beauty is not on the outside, but within."
"You were right. When I pray for the souls of those I killed, I feel lighter afterward."
"The next step is to forgive yourself for being lost in darkness, there was nothing else you could have done. They say forgiving yourself is the hardest part."

"I never thought about the world around me before — all I thought about was finding my next victim. But now I'm starting to notice things, the way the grass moves in the breeze, the way sunlight glints on armor. It is beautiful."
"You see beauty in the small things. You would make a fine artist. Would you like me to teach you to paint?"
"My kind have treated you terribly. Allow me to make amends for them, if I can."
"What are you going to do? You can't turn back time. Stay out of my sight, if you want to help."
"Sosiel was so desperate to find you... I have never seen a love so pure and bright before. It was wonderful even to witness it from the outside."
"You don't understand, demon. Sometimes I think it would be better if he'd forgotten me and just lived his life. It would have spared him pain."
"Achoo! Aaaachoo! Ulbrig, what are you doing? What is that smelly powder?"
"Mustard seeds. Ground up and charmed on a stone at midnight. It's to stop you putting the evil eye on me, just in case. A great remedy against fey enchantments!"
"Your ancestors were the first crusaders who followed the Queen herself. Doesn't that make you proud?"
"I'm proud of the strength and the iron will they passed down to me. I couldn't care less who they followed."
"You were raised in a good family and lived among good people in your tribe. Why are you turning your back on everything they tried to teach you?"
"Because only idiots like you chase after the thing that makes them weaker."
"Perhaps when you learn more about the surface, you will change your opinion of people and want to be closer to them."
"People? Right now all I can see around me are slugs and trash."
"You lied to the only friend who trusted you unquestioningly. Is gaining power worth being so isolated?"
"Ask a different question — was the company of one pathetic wimp worth turning down a chance at power?"
"Life underground is tough, but on the surface you do not have to live by the same harsh rules. You could let your softer side show."
"And lose my advantage over these flabby saps who are used to having full bellies and sweet dreams? Yeah right."
"Sometimes you remind me of a child that's trying to act like an adult. It's as if something is stopping you from growing up."

"Lemme get this straight: you look at other people and it makes you wanna grab 'em and suck 'em dry, but you take one look at me and you wanna pat me on the head? I think I should be offended by that!"
"Why does your demonic heritage hold so much appeal for you? Isn't it enough to be mortal, to live among mortals, to be ordinary?"
"When you get to know people a little better, you'll see where I'm comin' from. You've got it into your head that bein' mortal's some great thing, but it ain't all it's cracked up to be!"
"You feel the pull of your heritage, it beckons to you, but take my advice: resist its call. You will find no happiness among demons."
"Oh yeah. Just like rich folk always told me there's more to life than money. It's all 'Do as I say, not as I do, Woljif' with you lot!"
"You say your life is hard, but I would happily trade my life for yours, even for a day. You have friends, a place in the mortal world, and dreams..."
"Are you offerin' me a deal? Is this some kind of demon trap? Are you gonna take over my body or somethin' like that? No way, sister, I ain't gonna fall for it!"
"Why are mortals always striving to become rich? Your world is so interesting, so full of things to dream of! But lots of people think only of money."
"You can dream about pies in the sky and it doesn't cost a thing. But if you want to make your dream come true, you need to put some money on the table!"
"What is it like, to kiss a lover and feel the strength leave his body, to feel his life slowly fade away, to feel his pleasure morph into pain..."
"It is horrific. And not at all as poetic as you make it sound."
"You've kept silent long enough. You must admit your evil deeds in order to make room for light in your heart. I want to help you! Let me be your confessor, and I shall help you unburden your soul."
"I'm grateful to you, Camellia. It truly is difficult to carry my memories inside. Well, if you're sure you're willing, I'll tell you... But please prepare yourself — my past is dark and sordid!"
"Sometimes I worry that demons could take advantage of my inexperience. I know nothing of life, I am ill-prepared for the temptations they might offer me. Will you tell me about them?"
"Don't think about it. You have a pure heart. It won't lead you astray."
"Why won't you grow out your hair? You look like a pageboy now, long hair would be much more attractive."
"I do not want to be more attractive, I want to learn who I really am."
"I am so pleased to know you, Arueshalae. It is always so delightful to sit with you by the fire, whispering and sharing secrets..."
"Really? I am so glad to hear it! Maybe you could tell me something of your childhood? I love sweet tales of childhood!"
"War, dirt, dust, smoke... swill instead of food. These horrible tents instead of a normal bedroom..."
"But then again, there are so many opportunities for fun!"
"Why do I have to do all the dirty work at the camp?"
"We have plenty of soldiers. Why don't we take a few along as servants?"
"The world must be cleansed."
"Starting with my immediate vicinity."
"My precious mirror..."
"As long as you keep showing me this beautiful face, I know fortune will continue to smile on me."
"There is a strange smell in the air today, it stirs the senses..."
"The spirits tell me someone will die. How... sad."
"I am so weary of carrying my pack... I wonder if some chivalrous fellow would deign to help me?"
"Most certainly. Wait just a moment while I fetch a commoner to carry it for you. We just so happen to have an overabundance of commoners in our party."
"Isn't it strange that we who move in the upper echelons of society have been obliged to mix with such diverse rabble?"
"Just look upon it as a trip to a menagerie, my kind lady. I personally plan to regale my acquaintances with tales of this folly for years to come."
"How does one who believes in no gods or spirits come to possess healing powers?"
"I suppose I must draw strength from my utter disinclination to be in debt to any god or spirit."
"You were observing me earlier whilst I was practicing with my rapier, Daeran. Did you find it a captivating sight?"

"Oh, indeed. As captivating as a dancing cobra, a rushing avalanche, or a raging thunderstorm. And just as with those natural phenomena, it is important to do two things: enjoy the view and keep one's distance."
"On quiet nights, the sound of laughter and merriment were sometimes carried across the river to me in my garden. Oh, how I dreamed of being in your merry boating party!"
"If I had but known of the beautiful captive of Gwerm manor, I would have dreamed of abandoning the boat and coming straight to your garden."
"Surely Kenabres has felt like a prison to you as well? A nobleman of your caliber stuck in such a shabby little place..."
"Perhaps it was fate that kept me there, so that I could one day meet you, Lady Camellia."
"Even so, Count, you find Mendev utterly unbearable and yet here you remain. Why? And please answer without any foolishness about our meeting being predestined."

"The heavy burden of the past and dark family secrets have kept me here, like a man weighed down by an anchor. And I would be happy to reveal those secrets, sweet Camellia, if you give me a few moments to think them up."
"You there, beggar! Would you like some fried meat? With crackling, just the way you like it. I'll keep watch to make sure it doesn't get burnt."
"Thank you, Camellia! But I don't like fried meat. You probably confused me with someone else!"
"Vagrant, you sleep on the street, wear rags, and all your friends are beggars. There's dirt and disease all around you. You belong in an infirmary."
"Thank you, Camellia! You're so caring!"
"You there, beggar girl! That filthy bird of yours has befouled my tent! Wash this at once."
"Washing... When I was little, I loved doing the laundry with my mom. We had so much fun... Thank you for reminding me of those days."
"I cannot imagine what type of person could listen to your muddled rambling and find any deeper truth in it."
"I don't know why people listen to me either. But I'd like to know... then I could help them more."
"If you bathed and brushed your hair, you may provoke slightly less revulsion in those around you, urchin."
"But some things never wash off, isn't that right? Like blood... It's always on your hands, even if you can't see it."
"I am glad I no longer need to spare your tender feelings! Perhaps we can be friends now."
"Why, of course, Cami... Wait, let us seal our friendship with a sisterly kiss!"
"Do you really think all the men around you will be yours just because you start speaking in that breathy voice? I see nothing alluring in it."
"Come with me somewhere private and I will show you something alluring."
"Do you claim not to take any pleasure in plunging your blade into your victim's flesh?"
"I take pleasure in depositing the client's fee in my coffers. The rest of it — that's just work."
"Life has handed down many harsh challenges to me already in my life. I need someone who can teach me how to kill my enemies."
"I don't usually offer lessons, but if we can agree on a price..."
"Sometimes I can't seem to fall asleep. Every time I close my eyes, I see demons spurting blood, I hear the screams of the dying... I've never felt like this before..."
"If it's sympathy you're after, then all I can say is that everything passes — even these dreams will pass. If you're looking for someone to cheer you up, then you're looking in the wrong place."
"Some people find me arrogant because I tell them the truth about their deformities or their poverty. Yet people find you a pleasant fellow, even though you are a hired killer. The irony!"
"Manners are one of the best diversionary tactics."
"Are you sure you are not overstating the value of your services? Can killing truly be such challenging work?"
"Some of my colleagues accept low rates because their work is a 'passion' for them. But they do not guarantee quality, unlike me."
"I remember my father once scolded me for bringing my puppy to the table and letting it eat from its own plate..."
"What does a poor mongrel have to do to get luxuries like separate plates? I've been eating off yours for a month!"
"You know, Lann, you're almost half cute. I can only imagine what the knife of an experienced surgeon could do for you..."
"That's a great idea. If we find one, we'll also get him to shorten that tongue of yours, and take out your poison glands."
"If I were to bisect you right there, where your human and lizard halves meet, it would look quite... ridiculous."
"If you did that, then each half would grow into a whole new Lann and the two of them would give you a double beating. That's mongrel magic for you."
"Even your ugly kin from your ugly underground village rejected you. And that is why you so eagerly scurried up to the surface after us."
"I should've left you in Neathholm. A couple of days with you and my kin would be scrambling to get to the surface too."
"Which do you prefer, Lann? Being a filthy mongrel under the ground, or being a filthy crusader on the surface?"
"I like being a filthy crusader. Speaking of which, after a week on the march, you don't look much better."
"Nenio. Don't you fear death?"
"I fear nothing, for fear is the enemy of experimentation. But everyone in the world should fear my death — coming to terms with such a loss will be arduous indeed."
"I say, Nenio, why do you speak to me so rarely? I could tell you much that would interest you. We could be friends."
"Your intellect is lower than the intellect of the average citizen, rich girl. Your knowledge and views are of no interest to the world."
"I'm certain that your past isn't as simple as you say. There must be some dreadful secret that you couldn't bear to live with and chose to forget..."
"You're mistaken, rich girl. I am a researcher, and I would never choose to forget something significant and mysterious, no matter what discomfort such knowledge might bring me."
"You are so absorbed in your research... No doubt you are also well versed in vivisection."

"Naturally, rich girl. And very soon I will be starting a new absorbing project in this field — the practical excision of carnivorous ooze. You can be of assistance — you can serve as bait to catch the ooze and hold it in place while I work!"
"So you have forgotten everything... but why are you so certain there are no dark, horrifying secrets lurking in your past?"
"Certain? No, I am not certain, but hypothetical horrifying secrets have absolutely no bearing on my current research."
"You wield your weapon well. Watching you in battle is a pleasure."
"Combat is not a circus. You should watch me less, and watch our enemies more."
"You're a good fighter, Regill, but you're unbearably boring after the battle is done. It's probably because you're bleaching."
"I'm not here for your entertainment."
"I've heard that the more intense a gnome's Bleaching, the more his thoughts become distorted and hazy."
"My thoughts have always been crystal clear. The Bleaching has had no effect on them."
"It would be interesting to know what you did before joining the Hellknights. One does not make such a decision apropos of nothing."
"Made a great many decisions shut up in your mansion, then, did you, girl?"
"A gnome Hellknight... You must have had to fight long and hard to win the respect of others."

"Various incidents took place, of course. Especially when I was a young recruit among other young recruits. But I saw the mockery as just another trial to be overcome. Like fighting a devil... but worse."
"Seelah, a ball gown would suit you very nicely. Or any dress."
"Are you kidding? All that lace on me? It'd be like putting a saddle on a sow. It'd be enough to make the cats laugh!"
"Ouch! I broke a nail! It must be nice to be a knight like you. You can clip your nails short and not wear any makeup — and no one says a thing."
"So what would happen if you didn't wear any makeup? Would the demons refuse to die because you're not looking the part?"
"I do like how spic and span you keep all your things. Your armor is so polished, I could powder my nose without needing a mirror."
"Well, I live in hope of the day when you can see me as a person, and not just a convenient reflective surface."
"Have you never wondered why the gods do not simply solve all of the world's ills themselves, without paladins and crusades?"
"Some gods would be eager to solve mortals' problems for them. Rovagug, for instance. But we wouldn't like the result."
"Come now, Seelah. Don't be such a sourpuss. I am trying earnestly to be a good comrade! I would dearly like to chat with you..."
"You are a strange girl, Cami. Always so pleasant, like a chirruping bird... but strange, nonetheless."
"Today was a long day. I can barely stay standing, I'm so tired... And I still have to wash the dishes."
"Go get some sleep. Don't worry about the dishes, I'll wash them for you."
"What will you do when the war is over? I'd like to return to my manor and put it to rights... You could help me make a garden around it!"
"Tempting... But I too want to return home. You should see the gardens we have in Andoran!"
"You say the priests of Shelyn revere beauty, but not once have you asked to paint my portrait. Why?"
"I made several attempts, but none of my sketches were satisfactory. There is something in you that eludes my brush."
"It is so gratifying to have a kind and genteel fellow in the party. I feel so peaceful when you are near."
"If you had more faith in your heart, you could find peace wherever you went. But I am glad I can bring you solace."
"Do they truly drink tea made from rose petals in the temples of Shelyn? I should like to try it one day."
"Where I'm from, we use rose petals to make jam. I received a jar from the temple only recently, I would happily share it with you!"
"It is good to see someone with a penchant for fighting, and not preaching, in this party."
"I don't waste words on pointless niceties. If you need something — say it. If you don't — leave me be."
"Seeing how furiously you destroy your opponent makes my head spin. It's like you are a hurricane, not a man."
"A man can be stopped. A hurricane cannot. I want to be a man."
"When you extend your talons, the sight of them strikes such fear in me. So long, so sharp... A single move, and someone could be disemboweled."
"Don't be afraid of my talons — they're for enemies only. If I gut someone, then it's for good reason."
"If I am forced to eat food prepared by your hands one more time, arachnid, I shall go on hunger strike!"
"Hunger strike? What would you know of real hunger, you pampered little princess?"
"Do you really think that any strong female warrior must eschew bathing and grooming entirely? A thin excuse for primitive habits."

"Oh no. A warrior must always smell of flowers and toss out fancy surface words! It doesn't matter. You'll remember this conversation when you're begging for scraps at the foot of my giant throne. We'll see how pretty you look then."
"The men down in the caves are so hideous... Doesn't their appearance simply snuff out any carnal desire?"
"You think the face has anything to do with it? Your face, for instance — the day I touch it is the day I squeeze the life out of you."
"I am curious, Wenduag, about how you treat your lovers. I should not be surprised to learn you bite off their heads after the deed is done..."
"I don't. Do you?"
"Don't you ever tire of groveling all the time? It seems so false."
"You understand nothing. The weak must show their submission to the strong. Only then will the strong tolerate the weak."

"You're right. I shall never understand what it's like to grow up on the street. My papa gave me everything I could ever wish for. But I perfectly understand what it's like to be raised by a hard, heartless woman. Your old granny isn't the only one of her kind."
"Oh no, poor little Princess Gwerm! Now tell me how you'd cry into your supper, your pretty tears falling onto your fancy silver dishes!"
"Do you know who your ancestor was, tiefling? Was it a mephit, perhaps?"
"Well, if it turns out I'm the by-blow of some lord of the Abyss, won't you be sorry! By then it'll be too late!"
"A thief once broke into our house. His hands were cut off in punishment for his audacity. And quite rightly too, I think."
"Don't get your hopes up, lady. Even if they cut me hands off, I'll be picking coin pouches with me teeth."
"It is too bad you never tried to get your hands on the treasures of the Gwerms, thief."
"Do I look like an idiot to you? Everybody knew about your house, it was infamous: you go into Gwerm manor, you don't come back out again!"
"I notice that you cozy up to anyone with even the smallest amount of wealth or power. But not to me. Why is that?"
"Y'know somethin', your ladyship, there's some boots even I won't lick!"

"It's so touching, Arueshalae, the way you're drawn to people. I struggle not to respond in kind to your vulnerability and openness. I struggle not to drown in the depths of your beseeching eyes. That is how a succubus's enticement is supposed to work, yes? By luring the victim in... so he forgets to be vigilant, and so you can feast on his life force."
"Please, stop! That's not what I want at all... I didn't mean to..."
"I've heard that succubi can take on any guise, male or female. Does that mean that you prefer to appear as a woman?"
"To achieve my ends, I became what people wished me to be, but I've never considered what I might wish myself to be. You have given me food for thought. Thank you."

"It must be quite a diverting game to think of yourself as good. Right, Arueshalae? And the most delicious part is that it's all just pretend — at any moment you can slip back into your role of hunter and killer."
"You see everything as a game. But my decision to change means everything to me, more than life itself."
"What do you see when you look at people, I wonder? A succulent piece of meat? Or, perhaps, a decadent dessert?"
"I see them like... like a person dying of thirst sees a creek running with clear water. But I would rather die than drink a single drop."

"Shall I grant you a little honesty, Arueshalae? I am an oracle, which means that one day a great external force changed my life, without asking permission. Desna did the same to you — does that not bother you? Not even a little bit?"
"Desna opened my eyes, she did not force me to do anything. But I understand why you see a similarity. I never considered that you and I had anything in common before now."
"Camellia, allow me to attend to you and ease, if I can, the travails of the crusade. As a lady accustomed to comfort, this all must be quite trying for you."
"You are the picture of chivalry, Count. But I grew up in far less luxurious and pleasure-filled conditions than you. I am no stranger to sufferance."
"But why did your dear papa conceal you from society for so long, Lady Camellia? It's an outrage!"
"Isn't it obvious, Count? He was protecting me from the likes of you. My father has always been wary of little boys who climb into other peoples' gardens."
"I am trying to discover even the slightest flaw in you, Lady Camellia, but I cannot. Confess now, you must have one imperfection?"
"Just the one, but I take great pains to conceal it, Count. Perhaps we should take a walk together some time and I shall tell you about it... away from listening ears."
"If I were a shaman, I would do something utterly unthinkable and then tell everyone the spirits put me up to it."
"That would be quite audacious... I would never dare risk telling such an outrageous lie."

"Wouldn't it be wonderful if we had been friends as children, Camellia? We would have played hide-and-seek throughout the marble halls, ridden ponies through green meadows, flung bowls of ice cream from the garden walls onto unsuspecting passers-by."
"The thought is far from tempting, Count. If you had been my friend in childhood, you would have been a terrible influence on me."
"Steady on, Daeran, they are perfectly ordinary mosquitos. They are not spreading disease."
"And they will not bite you on the face. They wouldn't dare!"
"Hmm, everyone looks rather busy. And yet there's nothing for me to do to help the crusade? What a pity!"
"I suppose being bone-idle is also an important task. By right of blood, I claim this duty as my own."

"I cannot help but think that everything happening right now will one day end up in the history books. And under the stern gaze of the schoolmaster, little Mendevians will read: 'On such and such a day, the heroes stopped to camp here and there...'"

"And the little blighters will be thoroughly bored, and so they will begin doodling in the margins, and the only picture of yours truly in the book will be adorned with a mustache. So much for the rewards of heroism!"

"I read in a book by one great thinker that the further we are from civilization, the less civilized we become. As though stone walls, law scrolls, and the expectation to eat at a table laid with a tablecloth are all that stands between us and barbarism."
"If that is true, I am reluctant to see a more feral Daeran Arendae!"
"The Worldwound is an abomination, but still..."

"It is giving birth to new things — plants, creatures, natural phenomena. Life. Unfettered, strange, incomprehensible to us, but utterly unique life alien to both Golarion and the Abyss. I find the notion... fascinating."
"If you're so good at healing other people, how come you don't heal yourself?"
"Of what? There's nothing wrong with me!"
"I used to see you preaching in the square, Ember. Didn't your past teach you to be wary of crowds? Fanatics are dangerous whether they're taking up arms against you or hanging on your every word."
"I didn't preach, I just talked. And I didn't see any fanatics there, just good people. Why would they want to hurt me?"
"Just looking at you pains me, Ember. Why don't I do something about your appearance? What do you say to a bath, some new clothes, and a comb for that hair?"
"Thank you, but I like the way I look. Why don't I do something to your appearance? How about I use soot to blacken your hair? It will be great!"

"Ember, if you think that life is suffering and there is no hope, then why do you bother to heal all these people? If I were you, I'd take myself off to the nearest tavern and raise a large mug of milk to their soon-to-be-departed souls."
"If death came quickly to all, like a dream, that would be good. But they are not dying, they are fighting to live, so I need to help them."
"How is it that I never set eyes on you in any of my strolls around Kenabres, Ember? You are an amusing little thing!"
"You set eyes on me. But you didn't see me."
"I like seeing you as you are now — mask torn away, no longer pretending. Of course, 'like' is not quite the term I should use when describing my feelings toward a demon."
"So, you're not pining for the sweet, meek, wounded Arueshalae? You prefer the dangerous predator? How very reckless of you, Daeran. One day your recklessness will be your downfall."
"Tell me something, Arueshalae — were you pretending to repent, were you sincere, or was it all just Desna getting inside your head and seizing the reins?"
"I think it was the last one. The power of the gods is mighty. Mighty enough to dupe even demons with false visions."
"Out of curiosity, Greybor... how much do you charge for your services?"
"A lot. But if my prospective client washes my dishes at the campsite and budges up to give me a dry spot for my tent, I can offer a discount."
"You know, Greybor, you fuss over your name and reputation so much, you could give some of my fellow nobles a run for their money."
"As well I should. For a lord, a name is a pretty bauble, but my name is a tool. It's my bread and butter."
"Greybor, name your price: I want you to take my place on sentry duty today."
"I'm not doing that no matter how much you pay me. I appreciate your offer, Count, but I appreciate the chance to sleep before battle with you standing guard even more."

"Hired assassins go out of their way to please their clients. They are shunned in high society, but people in my circles often make use of their services, paying incredible sums for the privilege. Your kind are rather like courtesans, are they not?"
"Is that your roundabout way of calling me a whore, Count? Watch yourself — I may not like working for free, but that doesn't mean I can't kill a man just because I want to."
"I am astounded by your rates, sir. On what do you spend all your lucre? Hardly tobacco."
"You underestimate the quality of my tobacco, Count. When it comes to my few pleasures, I spare no expense."
"But really, what's it like? Like an ordinary human organ? Or is it like a lizard's? Is it forked? By my reckoning, it should at the very least be longer than a normal human's."
"All right, all right. Give over, you've won. There, look. Happy now? A perfectly normal human tongue."
"What a revolting sight. Lann, what is this slimy thing swimming about in my bowl? Are we having some prized mongrel dish today?"
"You are. The rest of them are having regular old stew. But I wanted to rustle up something extra special just for you."
"Lann, satisfy my curiosity — has anyone ever mistaken you for an animal?"
"No. What about you?"
"I am not surprised you do not know how to enjoy yourself, but how you have never played a ball game before is beyond my comprehension. Shall I give you a lesson?"
"Run around and kick the bull's bladder stuffed with hay? I think I've got it. When we get back to Drezen, we'll see who needs lessons!"
"I once ordered three wheels of a most excellent blue cheese, but they delivered three hundred by mistake. I lived off the stuff for two weeks, but a man can only take so much mold..."
"I once lived off mold for two weeks too. Just mold, mind you, no cheese."
"I say, Nenio, have you heard that there is a dinosaur living in the sewers beneath Drezen?"

"This claim is so popular that every tenth crusader keeps rushing to tell me of it. Having spent three nights in the cesspits of Drezen, I can confidently say that the claim is a baseless rumor and nothing more."
"My dear Nenio, did you know that the best folk remedy for snoring is a pillow pressed to the face of the snorer? Give it a try tonight if you hear anyone start to snore."
"How very interesting, thank you for the tip! The next person to snore will be subject to immediate experimental healing! This will be fascinating!"
"Nenio, tell me, do you truly not understand that I am... well, mocking you when I suggest all these madcap experiments?"
"Mocking me? I've never thought about it in that way. It makes no difference to me. Your ideas are tremendously useful, aasimar boy."
"The mystery woman without a past... It is rather tantalizing."
"Oh, you fall into the one percent of those surveyed who find amnesia sexually arousing. Thank you, your contribution to my data is much appreciated!"
"What do you think would happen, Nenio, if you tied two babaus together by the tail and suspended them above a hole filled with acid?"
"I have already conducted that experiment, aasimar boy. Demons are quite resistant to acid, and their tails are difficult to knot securely."
"I say, I do believe your Bleaching has progressed since yesterday. As your healer, I'm prescribing a trip to the nearest brothel. The experience will add at least ten years to your life."
"Naked people are of no interest to me. People faking desire for me — even less so."
"Regill, if your commander ordered you to, say, get drunk on wine and proposition a pretty squire... would you, as a loyal soldier, be duty-bound to carry out the order? Without a second thought?"

"I would be duty-bound to report the commander, arrest him and deliver him to be tried in a court martial. We already had an incident where infiltrators were masquerading as our soldiers, we have a procedure for unmasking saboteurs."

"I do not understand you Hellknights. Your life is nothing but restrictions, prohibitions, regulations... I see sticks a plenty, but where, pray tell, are the carrots? What are you doing all this for?"
"Our 'carrot' is our sense of inner satisfaction and knowledge that what we are doing is right. As regards the stick... That's always necessary."
"Why do you always go around with such a dour countenance, Paralictor? Is it required by your order's charter? Or is it merely the latest Chelaxian fashion?"
"Do you see any cause for merriment here? I do not."

"Every living soul, in a moment of weakness, reaches for something — a purpose, a dream, happiness or hatred. What do you reach for in those moments, Regill? You, who claim to be unhindered by emotion?"
"What I 'reach for' in such moments is discipline, and the stark awareness of all that will be lost if I surrender to weakness."
"You know, you're not that bad for a paladin. Not as much of a self-righteous bore as the others."
"You're also not as much of a jerk as I thought... for an arrogant, immature, self-absorbed man-child, of course."
"Another stopping place, another troubled sleep interrupted by the snores of my adored companions. Seelah, could you perhaps sleep a little farther away from me? A mile should do it."
"Yeah right. The snores of a paladin possess the magical ability to ward off all fiends, didn't you know? My snores are doing you a favor, pal!"
"Seelah, my dear, won't you tell me again how sinful and morally bankrupt my lifestyle is and how I must see the error of my ways? Your lectures always send me straight to sleep."
"Yeah right. Today your path to repentance is silent prayer and self-reflection."
"You are shivering from the cold, Seelah. It makes you look so girlish, and I find it thoroughly charming."
"Seelah the Shivering, charming counts with her girlish trembling, ha! But seriously, if I'm shivering, it's because I don't like being near you. You give me the creeps."
"I am willing to bet that you have never heard this one before. This was told to me only yesterday. So, a glabrezu, a lilitu, and a succubus walk into a tavern in Drezen..."
"...and the tavern keeper says, 'Pick your poison. Or do you want the Commander to kill you personally?' Who do you think came up with that one, Daeran?"
"I wish to make my confession, Sosiel. On one occasion I spent a rather steamy night with a trio of Osirian crocodile hunters. Their enormous, bronzed..."

"...muscles shone with oil, their bodies were temptation made flesh, and so on, and so forth. Do you really think you're the first person who's tried to turn confession into a joke? It's an old trick."
"It pains me to think that any living creature could be so dull and predictable. Tell me, Sosiel, do you have even the smallest secret? Something unusual that you keep private from the world?"
"The only thing I hide from the world is my fear, and my desire to throw up my hands and say, 'Someone else can do this.' I am not ashamed to admit it. Now it's your turn."
"Shelyn teaches you to worship beauty, but your worship does not seem to extend to myself. You have wounded me, sir!"
"Shelyn also teaches that beauty comes from within. I look inside you and... there's very little to admire there at present."
"You were probably seen as quite the catch in your village, eh, Sosiel? A handsome cleric in a sea of farm boys stinking of sheep's wool and manure."
"I was fortunate to be born in a wonderful place where the people are beautiful in body and soul. I am no better and no worse than anyone else there."

"I have frequently riled up clerics of Iomedae and Erastil, but I have on occasion vexed priests of Sarenrae, Asmodeus, and Gorum. Should I turn my unholy crusade against the Shelynites now? What will it take to ruffle their feathers?"
"You want my advice? Well... simply behave as you usually do in my presence."
"You have traveled a long road. From paladin to Hellknight, from Hellknight to a jester for demons."
"Whereas you started out as a jester. Where will your road take you, aristocrat?"
"I nurse a naive hope that the elder Vaenic brother will prove more interesting than the younger."
"You are just a drunken lordling, what's interesting about that? People like you are ten to a dozen in high society anywhere."
"Look here, Ulbrig, this is a fork. Did you have these in Sarkoris?"
"In Sarkoris we had honor. We had loyalty. We had warm-hearted families. We had love. As for forks, yep, we had them too — and we knew where to stick 'em!"

"If I had an estate to spare, I'd bequeath it to you, Wenduag. Hundreds of bachelors seeking a rich wife would serenade you with songs of your unparalleled beauty! It would be like something straight from the stage."

"Are you mocking my beauty? Even if it fades, I will still have plenty to take pride in. But what will you do if I cut up your handsome face? Will you lock yourself away in a tower and wallow in self-pity?"
"Your confidence, your unequaled talent for temptation... You were considered the most beautiful girl in the tribe, if I'm not mistaken?"
"Yes. And the healthiest, for that matter. I could bear many beautiful and strong children, increasing the strength of the tribe."
"For a troglodyte, you show no fear of the sky or open space... or are you simply good at hiding your fear?"
"I don't waste time looking about me. I only look for whatever it is I want to kill, eat, or fuck. And once I've found my target, it's the only thing I see."

"Do you know, my dear, I believe I am starting to become inured to you? Your glowing eyes when you watch me sleep, your fur in the food whenever you cook... I would miss all those things if they stopped."
"That was not my fur. Can't you tell the difference between my fur and rat fur? There were some rat bones in the pot, too, cut up nice and small. I hope you enjoyed them."
"I am so fortunate to have met you. We both know what it is like to be beautiful and desired in our own milieu."
"Before, my beauty meant something. But not now. Now I seek only power."

"Perhaps, if we survive this, I shall invite you to one of my soirees. We can devise an exotic backstory for you and everyone will lose their heads over you, literally licking up to you, ignorant all the while that you are but a petty thief from Kenabres. It will be a riot!"
"Then I wanna to be the Prince of Garund! Or maybe the King? It's a tough choice!"
"I cannot stand demons. If I didn't already know your grandfather was one, I should never have sensed the demon blood in you. You're much too... unremarkable."
"And you come from aasimar stock, your excellency, but I'd say we're each about as angelic as the other."
"I wonder, if I tossed some coins on the ground and told you to bark like a dog, would you?"
"Well... maybe I would, y'know. But I won't forget this."
"If you dressed up a little and scrounged up some saucy impudence, you could be a kept man in some noble's house. Easy work with very little risk. I hear they pay a premium for curls."
"What's that, sit in a house all day waitin' for the lord or lady to swan in? No way! I may be a cur, but I ain't house-broken!"
"Wait, did I hear you correctly: you are charging me one hundred coins for this potion? Me, your comrade? Our fellowship will not withstand such a trial, believe you me."
"All right, fifty! Maybe there's some gang of aasimars you can join? From what I see, you get a kick outta fleecin' honest folk!"
"Don't you miss the Abyss at all? Even a bad home is still a home. That's what I think. A home lives in your heart."
"Trust me, there's nothing worth missing. And I am trying to rip that 'home' out of my heart so I never think of it again."
"You're so pretty. But I'll never be like that. It's a little sad, I guess."
"For anyone with a heart, you will always be far more beautiful than me, little one."
"What would you like your first dream to be?"
"I don't even know. I think once I'm able to imagine it, that's when I'll be ready to accept Desna's gift."
"Your wing makes the perfect umbrella! Thank you for keeping me dry when it rains."
"And if I fold my wing like this, it makes a little shelter."
"Don't you miss the demons you knew, the ones you left behind?"
"I left no one behind. It was more like... I ran away from them. No one in the Abyss will be missing me, so I have no one to miss either."
"I heard you talking to your invisible friends. You know, I have a friend too..."
"I can't imagine what spirit would talk to a guttersnipe like you — and I don't want to."
"You're so beautiful and kind... But I think you're sad all the time. Why is that?"
"Those who stick their snotty noses in other people's business can get very sad themselves."
"It's sad that your mom died. But it's good that she didn't see the terrible things you were forced to live through. Every cloud has a silver lining, doesn't it?"
"It does indeed. For instance, when you die, the world will be free of one hideous, foolish girl."
"Your house is so pretty! But I always thought it seemed very cold, no matter the time of year."
"Paupers are destined to criticize that which they have never had or will have."
"I hear you moaning sometimes in your sleep, it sounds so sad... Do you have bad dreams?"
"Firstly, don't you dare eavesdrop on me while I'm sleeping ever again, and secondly, don't even think of pitying me!"
"You say you love to have fun, but your eyes don't look happy at all. Why are you lying?"
"Oh, seer, you have glimpsed my secret sorrow! I admit it! I have the ability to feel more than one emotion at any given moment!"
"You're great at healing people. Maybe you could help out in an infirmary."
"Plumping pillows for wounded paladins is one thing, but constantly wading through the gore and stench? Not a chance."
"You have such pretty golden hair... When I look at it, I always think of the sun, angels, fresh bread, and all sorts of good things."
"Fresh bread, you say? Poor hungry child, I hope you won't try to eat me while I sleep."
"It's sad when you're surrounded by people but none of them are your friends, isn't it?"
"I don't have the slightest idea what you're on about. I could fill the main square of Kenabres with all my friends. And Prelate Hulrun, if he were here, would add, 'And burn them all.'"
"Once in the River City, I found a jug and drank from it. It turned out to be wine. Wine is very strange. It makes you think everything's really funny, even when it's really not."
"'Everything's really funny, although it's really not' is the perfect description of the crusades. No wine necessary!"
"La-la-la..."
"Na-na-hmm..."
"One more day, and I'm still alive."
"Everyone dies, and I don't even get sick... Why is that?"
"Auntie Magpie baked a bad pie, dropped it flat, made the sky cry..."
"...dropped the second, made the rivers dry, dropped the third, now we all die."
"The water is bubbling in the pot and the little bubbles are rising up from the bottom, quickly, like there's something interesting at the top."
"They live on the surface for a moment, and then — pop! — they're gone! It reminds me of something..."
"Good Sooty, lovely birdie..."
"Do you like being with me? Maybe you'd rather be flying about the River City with your crow friends?"
"I miss you very much, Arueshalae. I'm sad we won't be able to play together anymore! I really, really loved you Arueshalae, really! I'll always wait for you."
"Don't talk about me as if I'm not here, little girl! I am here, right in front of you!"
"You are so unfortunate: you drink and drink another's life force, but your thirst is never satisfied. You did this to yourself."
"Me? Unfortunate? I was unfortunate when I tried to go against my own nature. Now... now everything is completely different!"
"Greybor, are you there? I was sent to tell you that supper's ready... Why are you looking at me like that? Are you sick? Does something hurt?"
"Run along, Morah... I mean, Ember, go on. I... I'll be there now."
"We're all sitting around a warm fire, we have yummy food, the night is quiet, and nobody is trying to kill us... It's nice, isn't it?"
"We're sitting round a fire that is visible for miles, we're too tired to fight, and it's gone too quiet, almost like someone is watching us. But, do you know what? It's not all that bad."

"...I totally forgot the song... what did papa sing again? The little lamb ran away, lost in the lowlands a night and a day, tell me where my little lamb's gone, and I will lead him all the way home..."

"The next part is something about how there's water and hay waiting for the lamb back on the farm. I once had to sing about that blasted lamb twenty times in a row... and she still wouldn't fall asleep. No, she didn't... she just kept watching me and laughing..."

"Sometimes I think... it's good my father died. He thought the crusades were something different to what they were. He had such a beautiful dream — but he would have been disappointed in the reality."
"Disappointment is not the same as the inquisitor's pyre, little one. Disappointment can be survived. I know there's someone he would not have been disappointed by, and that's his daughter."
"You love traveling... but why do you have to kill people? Can't you just go traveling without that part?"

"It's more interesting my way. I get bored of sightseeing very quickly, I'm not interested in foreign food, every tavern is the same as the next. But killing is different every time — it's the most enjoyable part of the trip."
"Why did your tribe hide under the ground? If you came up to the surface, would the good people really turn you away?"
"Why did you live on the street? If you entered a wealthy home, would the good people not allow you to stay there?"
"Too bad I didn't know about your village. My friends and I could have left the streets and lived with you like a family!"
"I'm afraid you wouldn't be welcome there either. You think too kindly of us. Even our tribe had its castoffs and pariahs."
"How are you able to think of jokes so quickly? I can't make jokes at all."
"You've seen how fast a paladin can bring their shield up to fend off a blow? It's the same thing — takes years of practice."
"Knock knock. Who's there? Para. Para who? Paralictor Regill."
"No, you're supposed to say 'knock knock' and I'm supposed to say 'Who's there?' and then you reply. Go on, try again."
"Look, I found some feathers. But they're all black, so I guess you won't want them for your arrows."
"When I was underground, I had to use the wings of big beetles as flight feathers. I'm not picky."
"You're afraid you're running out of time because mongrels don't live long. But ordinary people, and even elves, think the same. Everybody thinks the time given to them is too short."
"Huh... So do you think I could make a list 'Fifty Things to Do Before I Die'? Fine, I'll be realistic: 'Thirty Things.'"
"Nenio! I like your tail!"
"Really? But it serves no practical purpose and hinders rather than facilitates my movement. However, I cannot deny that beholding it does bring a certain aesthetic pleasure."
"Nenio, give me a pen! I want to draw too!"

"I am not drawing, burned girl, I am producing a detailed sketch. Take a pen and some paper. Today we are going to create an optimal layout for the sleeping rolls and other areas of the camp, taking into account wind direction, heat distribution from the fire, and the position of individuals who are prone to snoring."
"Nenio, why are you trying to calculate the speed of a crowd of peasants chasing after a thief who stole a goose and two apples? Who needs to know that?"
"Oh, it is very important information. If I had known it at the beginning of the experiment, I would have abandoned the heavy goose right away."
"Nenio, are you injured? I'll heal you right away! Don't move your fingers, all right? Otherwise, they'll set like that and look like a chicken's foot."
"Would it be possible to break all the bones and heal them in such a way as to give my body additional advantages? Girl, wait, hold your magic! I want to try to lengthen my finger bones..."
"The paper was white, then it turned blue even though you dipped it in red blood! What magic is this?"
"Girl, this is called my 'experiment to determine the acidity of demon blood.' I can explain the basis of the experiment. First, we take a perfectly ordinary piece of paper..."
"You care about your soldiers. Lots of people don't like you, but I know you are a kind man."
"Of course I care about them. Their combat effectiveness is my responsibility."
"A gnome used to live on the street with us — he was gray and pale, just like you. He would get in tavern brawls all the time — to live longer, he said. But he got killed in one of those fights."
"Only cowards run from death. You can't escape it, no matter what. It's better to face it than let it stab you in the back."
"Regill, have you ever seen a real devil? What did he look like?"
"A weakling that folded after the first hit."
"Hell is a very sad place. People are in so much pain there, they forget everything good about their past life. Why do Hellknights want everyone to be like that?"
"Hellknights do not want Hell's torment, but Hell's discipline. However, if sufficient discipline is impossible without suffering, then so be it."
"There probably are Hellknights in your unit who really love you."
"Respect for one's commander and mentor is to be expected among Hellknights. But 'love' is beyond remit."
"You fight demons with such joy. Do you really enjoy their suffering?"
"Pfff. Shove that somewhere else. Demons are demons, why are you sympathizing with them?"
"You have the power to heal and the power to maim. Don't you regret that your goddess made you a killer?"
"I only regret that the Goddess didn't grant me the power to silence unwanted noises!"
"When Iomedae became a goddess, her friends probably missed her a lot, huh?"
"They would have been happy for her, silly. She turned into a goddess! It's not like she moved to Garund!"
"Your hope and bravery call to people, Seelah. But if their hopes don't come true and their fates don't change for the better, what can you give them instead?"
"If I give someone hope, that's enough — it means I'm making a difference. Without hope, there is only death. There is no changing things for the better if you're already dead."

"You refuse to admit that life is ruled by despair, and that hope only deceives people. But despair is what led you to Iomedae. Isn't that true? If you had just hoped for the best, you would still be a thief."
"Don't preach your silly ideas to me. I didn't wallow in despair, I did the right thing. That's totally different."
"We've met before! You never shooed me from the temple steps, and once you gave me a whole loaf of bread!"
"And I let you keep sleeping on the street... Forgive me, Ember, I did nothing for you when you needed my help!"
"I used to have many friends in the River City, but then all of them died. Now I have new friends... They aren't going to die, are they?"
"No, Ember. We won't let any of our friends die. We studied healing magic for a reason, didn't we?"
"Shelyn teaches us to see beauty in everything... Does that include people's disfigurements, when they are chopped up in war?"
"Enjoying wounds is not Shelyn's but Zon-Kuthon's teaching. Wounds need to be healed or prevented. And sometimes beauty needs to be protected with weapons."
"I found your sketching chalk. Well, half of it. Soot ate the other half, but don't scold her, please."
"I hope that snack didn't do her any harm. Next time I will leave some breadcrumbs outside my tent, so she isn't tempted to rummage through my things."
"If you draw everything beautiful, how come you never draw yourself?"
"I've tried, but every time embarrassment gets the better of me. I see so many flaws in myself... No, sorry, it's difficult for me to answer this question."
"You never give in, do you? You and Sosiel are very alike. He never gives in either, no matter how hard it is."
"You think I'm like my brother... Thank you, little girl. There is no higher praise."
"You're sleeping poorly: you toss and turn and moan. If you want, I can sing you a lullaby? I know lots of lullabies — maybe I know the one your mother used to sing to you."
"No. If I hear that song, I'll think of home. I don't want to reopen that wound."
"You're always looking at me with an angry face. But I don't understand — why? Did I do something bad to you?"
"Hmph... You, girl, might not have done anything to me — yet. But it's because of people like you that Sarkoris perished. How else should I look at you?"
"It must be a lot of fun living in a tribe. Like one big family."
"People watching your every move, sticking their noses into your business, telling you how to live... Yes, it was fun, fun, fun."
"It's easy to do tricks like me: first you need to think of something good, about how you want to help somebody, and then... poof! Try it, it'll work for you too!"
"I find it easier to imagine the bodies of my enemies, laid out all around me. Will that do?"
"Did you have any songs down in the caves? Life without songs would be sad."

"When I was a runt, I once started whistling a tune out of boredom... But then a carnivorous snake slithered up behind me and wrapped itself around my throat. I stabbed it with my knife, and then I sank my teeth into it and chewed. Ever since then, I haven't liked music... But I do like snake meat."
"Let's play hide and seek! Wait, what am I saying? You'll just find me right away."
"You want to learn to hunt, is that it? All right, I'll hide. I will try to remember that it is a game, and not a real ambush."
"You really are very beautiful! Your eyes are so yellow and bright, your teeth are so straight. And your hair sticks out really scarily!"

"Envious, girl? Not everyone can be beautiful and healthy like me! But it doesn't matter, you are tenacious, cunning, and you know how to survive. You will be fine, even with your ugliness and your injuries."
"So, your auntie Hepzamirah is a cow, your great-grandfather Baphomet is a goat... so how come you're a little lamb?"
"Huh? Whaddaya... ah, the horns, gotcha. I dunno, but I hope to all the gods the story doesn't start 'One day Baphomet was walking through a pasture...'"
"You shouldn't be angry that you're a tiefling. Tieflings are made when a human and a demon love each other so, so much that they become a mommy and a daddy."

"I dunno what the deal was with granny and ol' granddaddy, some creepy ritual or pure animal... lust — bleugh — or whatever those cultists call it, but I can tell you now there was no love, or talk of mommies and daddies."

"Do you know what would be nice? If we didn't die in the crusade. After, yes, if we win. But if we die before that... that would be bad. You will try not to die, won't you? Although I suppose it will be hard."
"Sometimes I'm more afraid of you than Baphomet."
"Do your tiefling friends tease you about your Shadow? I remember how upset you used to get when you were little..."
"Stop acting like we know each other! Only a pathetic idiot would be friends with a crazy beggar, you got it? That ain't me!"
"When you were little, you had the funniest little stubby horns! Did it hurt when they started growing?"
"...damn things itched like crazy."
"You always have so many curious things in your bag! I've never seen anything like them. Can I touch them?"
"Sure, why not. But I'm watchin' you!"
"I saw your grandmother before Deskari attacked the River City. But she didn't recognize me. I don't think she recognized anyone."
"That's because you didn't owe her any money. If you'd been in her debt, she'd remember you till the day she died!"
"Do you see me as a rival, Camellia? How sad. We could have been something truly great..."
"I am under no illusions. The only thing I could be for you is a meal."
"Camellia, my friend... If you let the call of the Abyss into your heart, then after you die you could become one of us, a succubus."
"I should want to become an idiotic, insatiable, gluttonous fiend? That is what you think of me, 'friend.'"
"I know you think about me, Daeran. About what it would be like to be with me. Where is your sense of adventure now? Will you let fear keep you from experiencing pleasure?"

"What of you, Arueshalae? Do you think about me? About what it would be like to be with me? About how much life there is within me, and the ecstasy it would bring to drink mouthful after mouthful? Can you picture it clearly? Good, you can choke on it. You picked the wrong prey, my lovely."
"You enjoyed teasing me before. But now... you're afraid. Admit it. You know I won't hold back if I get my hands on you."
"I enjoyed teasing you because I wanted to see the moment when the little white lamb turned into a slavering wolf. Now that I've seen it, there's no point in continuing."
"Stop giving me that pitying look! You're spoiling my appetite!"
"I'm sorry, but it's just so sad. I lost my friend."
"My little sweet, I have decided to return to the path of redemption. Let's hug and be friends again! Come on, come to me..."
"Poor Arueshalae... You're in so much pain, but there's nothing I can do!"
"Desna... your sweet shrines, your holy singing priests... one day I will return to you..."
"...to hunt my fill."
"That foolish attempt to redeem myself taught me a great deal."
"For instance, I learned how mortals fall over themselves in the face of naivety and helplessness. I will use that."
"You always insisted that I couldn't redeem myself, that it was just an act. Are you satisfied now?"
"Of course, I am. My instincts were right. I cannot say the same for my comrades, alas."
"What is she like, your wife? Hmm, Greybor? What was so sweet, so tempting about her, that you decided to give up the assassin's life on the road, if only for a time?"
"You wouldn't understand, even if I told you everything I remember. But I won't."

"My closeness bothers you, doesn't it, Lann? You keep your distance, hiding behind cutting jokes... and all because you enjoyed taking pity on the poor, meek succubus, but you can't feel like a knight in shining armor around the real me, can you?"
"The real you? There's nothing real about you."
"I don't care one bit what you look like, Lann. Isn't that wonderful? You have always dreamed of meeting a woman like me!"
"I'm surprised you even remember my name. A hunter doesn't often bother to name its prey."
"You forgot your past... With me, you will forget your future..."

"Thus the succubus begins to stalk her prey, verbally attacking the target, trying to persuade or hypnotize... Wait, are you trying to persuade me or hypnotize me? It's important. Let us try that again."
"Your ability to change form and deceive is similar to mine, Nenio, wouldn't you agree?"
"What an interesting observation, demon girl! We should conduct a series of parallel transformations and carefully compare our processes."
"Poor Kiranda. She fell into your clutches and paid for it with her life. You've turned out to be more treacherous than a demon, Regill Derenge. What does that say about you?"
"That I do my duty well. If you give me even the slightest cause to suspect you of treachery — you'll soon be joining your succubus friend. Think on that."
"You, gnome, I wouldn't even deign to kiss. When the time comes, I will rip your heart straight out of your chest!"
"I have been expecting your attack since the moment you were rashly accepted into our party. And since that moment, I have been preparing for it."
"Poor Seelah, you were so hopeful that I would join the light and that we would fervently pray to our goddesses side by side! It's so charming to see you try to hide your disappointment!"
"I am not trying to hide anything."
"Fighting against yourself is so wearing, but freedom is so uplifting... Let us be free together, Seelah."
"You're incapable of being 'together' with anyone."
"Don't turn away, Sosiel. Look me in the eye. You will find no repentance there, so do not look for it, my sweet."
"I am sorry I failed to help you. I could have tried harder... I should have!"
"You arrogant little priestling... Did you really think you could save me? Helping a demon become good — they would have made you a saint for such a miracle!"
"I only wanted to be your friend. I'm sorry you have already forgotten what that is."
"You spent too long in the Abyss. You will never stop hearing its call."
"Right now all I hear is the voice of a predator ready to strike."
"You want to forget everything that happened to you? I can give you the gift of oblivion to wash it all away... You will be cleansed."
"You? Cleanse me? I'll bathe in your blood, demon. Then I'll be cleansed!"
"Since I changed, you've been acting so strangely, Wenduag, it's amusing... I thought you would try to kill me out of envy."
"You became strong, dangerous! I do not want to be at odds with you... for now. And if I do attack, it will be when you least expect it."

"Aren't you afraid of me, Wenduag? Before, you took every chance you could to give me a tongue-lashing. What if I want to get my revenge? Now that all that Desna nonsense is no longer holding me back."
"Didn't my jeers help you give up on all that 'Desna nonsense'? Forget it, let's find someone we can hunt together instead."
"You're always slinking around me, but the moment I look at you, you run off... Tell me, ringlets, is little sister Arueshalae really so terrifying?"
"Yeah, you are... I don't fancy my first time bein' my last time!"
"You are the spawn of a powerful demon... it will be all the sweeter to drink your strength. I will crush you in my embrace and you will give me everything, down to the last drop."
"What do I look like to you, an orange? I ain't made to be squeezed!"

"'I want,' 'I can' — it's all just talk. Even if by some miracle you don't go back to your own kind with your tail between your legs and you keep hanging about with mortals, they'll never accept you. No one will ever want to live side by side with a demon."
"I hope I can earn the trust of mortals. I will try hard."
"You put on a good show, but... we'll never believe your supposed change of heart."
"But if I was still the old Arueshalae, you would believe it. Oh, you would have believed anything I wanted you to... Your doubts only prove my honesty."
"I heard you praying to Desna the other night, asking her to send you a dream. I look forward to the day when I finally put you to sleep. What a sweet dream that will be."
"I don't entirely understand your meaning... But I sense your hostility and the threat in your words. I'm sorry you see me as an enemy."
"People don't change. If an inveterate liar or a fugitive looks you in the eye and asks forgiveness for past wrongs — look for the dagger behind his back."
"People change, and often beyond recognition. But sadly, I have witnessed more people turn into liars and criminals than the opposite."
"I once saw a notorious scoundrel and thief who announced he was going to live a righteous life. He looked like a caged beast. I see the same despair in your eyes that I saw in his."
"What matters is I am no longer making other people miserable. As for myself... I have never been truly happy. Perhaps the goddess will one day send me that feeling."
"Plenty of people ask me about my work, but none with as much interest as you. Why's a sheltered girl like you so interested in murder?"
"My interest lies in daring man who aren't afraid to get their hands dirty."
"You show no fear of violence or blood. Such mettle is quite unusual in the daughter of an aristocrat who grew up in seclusion."
"Or perhaps I am simply naive and do not fully understand what is occurring around me. If I did, I would not doubt fall over in a dead faint."
"People say that nobles always have a hidden agenda. You can never take any of them at face value."
"I grew up in seclusion and never learned the art of intrigue, Greybor. I am exactly who I appear to be and nothing more."
"You are so polite to me and so brusque with other commoners... What is it you want from me?"
"I am polite to those who deserve my politeness. There are not many such people in the crusade."
"A noblewoman who knows how to cook over an open fire. You truly are a lady of many talents, Camellia."
"Do not try to spare my feelings. I saw you pour out your stew behind that rock over there."
"I'm surprised an odious little lordling like yourself hasn't earned himself a swathe of serious enemies."
"Only people who do things earn themselves enemies. Whereas I, for the most part, simply enjoy myself."
"It seems to me, Count, that you are overly concerned with how your deeds will affect your family name."
"For generations my family strove to build its perfect reputation! One black sheep such as myself can't possible tear it all down... no?"
"I wonder if you were the son of a humble innkeeper in Absalom, and not the son of a count, would you be just as unbearable?"
"I haven't the faintest clue. But I do know that I probably wouldn't be an orphan whose entire family had been wiped out by demons."
"Some people believe in gods, some believe in prosperity. But as a nobleman, Count, I suppose you believe you were born to rule."
"I believe the social structure of Mendev has given me wealth and privilege from birth. I was born a squalling, naked creature, just like the infant of any peasant or city drunkard."
"Speaking strictly hypothetically, Count, if you could kill anyone in Mendev, who would it be?"
"Boredom. Or sanctimony. I would annihilate them in this wretched country if I could, but alas, there is no assassin capable of dealing with such monsters."
"Why do you always end up in the thick of things, girl? I know you're not stupid and you understand the risk involved."
"I just want to protect you and the others. Don't worry, you don't need to watch over me — I have my grandmother, after all."
"Little one... what are you doing in the middle of this war? The battlefield is no place for children."
"It's no place for anyone. But I've already had a longer life than many. So if I get killed, it doesn't really matter."
"Why are you looking at me like that? Do I frighten you? Don't be afraid, I won't hurt you."
"No, I'm not scared of you at all. You just look... lost. Like you went for a walk and forgot the way back home. But you're going to have to remember it."
"I can't believe there is no beggars' guild in Kenabres. Didn't they demand a cut for letting you operate in their territory?"

"Sometimes I was approached by healthy people who pretended to be poor and sickly, and they said that I owed them some kind of 'cut.' I gave them coins. If they are willing to be miserable all their lives for the sake of coins, that means they need them more than me."

"You're willing to give away everything you have to other people, girl. But people will get used to it, and they will keep asking, and when the time comes that you can't give them anymore — they'll start demanding."
"And rightly so. I'll be very upset if I have nothing to give them."
"Ignoring the fact that you want to drink my life force, I do prefer you this way. You always know what you're getting with succubi, but penitent sinners are much more unpredictable and dangerous."
"Take a closer look and you will start to like me even more. I am a slow-acting poison, but one without an antidote."
"I'm sorry, darling, but I've been around long enough to know better than to be tempted by a pretty face. Don't even try it."
"Fine, you avaricious dwarf, I suppose I cannot turn myself into a pouch of gold coins to tempt you. But you still won't escape me."
"The demons just seem to keep coming and coming recently, like there's no end to them."
"If things keep going this way, the Queen will have to gift me a tract of land because there won't be enough gold in the country's coffers to pay for my services rendered."

"I've traveled some distance, fulfilling this contract... But it's still better than doing a job for some jealous cuckold of a grocer whose wife's been a little too neighborly with the fellow next door."
"What? Sure, I took jobs like that when I was green. A man's got to start somewhere."
"Greybor, old boy, who have you got yourself tangled up in this time? The way you're going, soon you'll be a dyed-in-the-wool crusader, singing hymns and giving alms to the poor."
"And even — oh gods, the thought makes me shudder — killing for free!"
"I was thinking of making a deposit in a trustworthy temple of Abadar — just in case of an emergency."
"But every minute we spend in the Wound is an emergency. I think it's more prudent to invest in better gear..."
"Many of my fellow professionals prefer to work for one client as they get older instead of a string of different ones."
"What they want is a nice little setup as the court assassin for a monarch or duke, not the carnage of the war against the demons."

"I like your take on things. You don't make a big tragedy out of the fact that you're going to die someday. You live each day as it comes, accepting the inevitable. You would have done well in my profession."
"We're all going to die someday, it's just that there's less time between me and that unpleasant event than there is for most people. If Pharasma lets me, I'll send you a postcard."
"Lad, I know you grew up in caves, but... you need to work on how you present yourself to the world. Strangers are going to judge you on things like that."
"Do you think if I dress myself up and learn how to give a graceful bow, I can stop people from noticing that I'm half lizard?"
"You were asking me about the most remarkable place I've ever been to. It's got to be Absalom, center of the world. People of all stripes, from hundreds of different cultures, living side by side."
"Really? Huh... Maybe even my face wouldn't stand out in a crowd that big. I wouldn't mind seeing the place someday!"
"I'm beginning to think I'm a bad storyteller. You were practically snoring when I was telling you about my last mission before I came to Mendev."
