"I like hearing about your travels in distant lands, but you always describe towns as a list of places to ambush a target. Why do I need to know that some such alley in some such town has exits to the street where the nobility's carriages go past, and where the best hiding spots are in the slums?"
"Here's my advice to you, Lann: if you want to stop coming across as a savage, stop eating every meal with your knife. Other cutlery is available, you know."
"The next time I find myself at a royal reception, I'll remember that, Greybor. The Queen probably has thirteen different forks for one main course."
"Nenio, out of interest, whose head is worth more — Queen Galfrey's or the Commander's? What does your science tell you?"
"The Queen's, most certainly. Although, if we consider the developing trends, the price for the Commander's head could exceed that for the Queen's in approximately eight months and four days' time."
"The most important thing is to make the right shape with your lips and tongue, and to exhale just right."
"Dwarf boy, your skill at creating smoke rings is worthy of accolades. Tell me, can you hit the Commander's head with a smoke ring from here?"
"Why are my boots wet and slimy? They were dry when I left them here a moment ago, and oddly enough, I prefer them that way."
"I conducted an experiment. Did you know that footwear is completely unusable as a foodstuff, even footwear made from high-quality leather?"
"You created an anatomical atlas of weak points for every creature on Golarion? A useful document."
"The atlas is not yet complete. All my attempts to pinch a dragon's tail have been unsuccessful so far."
"If one of your experiments kills you, all your work will die with you. You should make sure it is preserved."

"There are many ways to recreate my Encyclopedia in the event of my death. For example, summoning my spirit. Yes, it would be quite good if someone did that! Then I could continue my research without any distractions!"
"I don't mean anything in particular by this, but in my circles your skills would be highly prized. Perhaps even more highly than in the Hellknights."
"My blade belongs to the order. It is not for sale. Nor am I."
"What do you make of this ridiculous fad for carrying a knife up your sleeve?"
"Like you, I am vehemently opposed. The arms are too easily blocked at the beginning of combat. Carrying a knife in the leg of one's boot is much more practical."
"You know, Regill, you are much more imposing and commanding than any gnome I've ever met."
"You are not the most typical example of your kind either, Greybor. It is our work that defines us far more than our blood or origin."
"I've heard the heads of the noble houses of Cheliax don't tend to last long. Perhaps you know if they have need of... reliable contractors?"
"You do realize you have just asked a Hellknight how you can best go about your illegal activity?"
"Since we've been adventuring together, I think your hair has become a little less colorless than it was when we met."
"The chaos at work in the ranks of the Mendevian army sometimes shocks me more than I care to admit. This, paradoxically, staves off the Bleaching."
"Quit scowling at me. Let's drink — I have a flask of excellent liquor, strong enough to break the ice between us."
"I could accept your offer, I suppose, but... I have a rule — I don't drink in the company of poisoners, cheaters, or assassins."
"I can't help noticing how impressive your fighting skills are. It's not just good training I can see, you've got talent and a tactical mind too."
"Well, if we're swapping compliments, you're not a bad fighter yourself. But that does nothing to change the fact that you're a worthless, murdering scumbag, albeit a competent one."
"Why are you staring at me like that? I'm just relaxing after a long day, smoking my pipe, not bothering anyone..."
"All I see is a hardened killer relaxing, a hardened killer smoking his pipe, and a hardened killer 'not bothering anyone.' It's obvious you're up to something!"
"Of course paladins deserve respect. They are professional soldiers who have the support and endorsement of the gods. But your condescension to others is tiresome."
"Excuse me? The condescension of paladins? Taken a look in the mirror recently, Mr. Big Bad Assassin? Have you heard the way you go on and on about your 'Reputation' with a capital 'R'?"

"It seems to me that in the First Crusade there was more space for paladins and less for hired killers. However, there is a limited supply of do-gooders and fighters of conscience. And that supply is used up quickly."
"Faith, hope, and love are what hold the world together, Greybor. The only people who talk about the power of money are those who have no faith, no hope, and no love. I know from my own experience."
"Be honest, lad, you wanted to find your brother alive and well or not at all. Nobody wants a broken man."
"You're wrong. I want to get Trever back no matter what state he is in. I am ready to help him carry any burden."
"You boy, what the hell do you think you're doing? This war isn't yours to fight, anyone can see that. You should be a painter, a gardener, anything you want, but not a soldier."
"You've got it wrong. The world would be a much better place if all the soldiers were like me, and all the people like you were gardeners and painters."
"Quit bothering me with your sermons, priest! You can see I'm happy with my life, I'm doing fine, so what's your problem?"
"On the outside — yes, you look fine. But I can also see the injuries you have done to your soul. Don't lie to me or yourself and pretend they don't hurt."
"I once met a gnome who had a little stand in the middle of a room with some wrapping paper on it, and he called it art. Is Shelyn the patroness of that, too?"

"I think the beauty of that work of art lies in the philosophical idea behind it. If the gnome was truly inspired, that means the goddess was with him. And if he was a charlatan — well, that is on his own conscience!"
"Sometimes it feels like I don't have one cleric following me, but a whole temple of Shelyn constantly nagging me to repent."

"I am sorry, I did not mean to be such a nuisance. I can see that you have not been entirely corrupted by evil and that you are willing to heed the words of a friend. I struggle to stop myself reminding you what it is like to live a life of faith."
"I feel sorry for what you've been through, Trever. You could have been a strong fighter and comrade. But slavery among the demons can only break a man."
"I did not break. I survived and kept my mind whole. The ones who lost themselves, they are the ones who broke."
"I see nothing wrong with gladiator fights if people take part in them willingly."
"No. Killing for entertainment is a dark business. Even if you win, you are still killing yourself."
"You could comb your beard, at least. Your whole head's as wild as a bird's nest."
"And you remember what a bird's nest looks like, do you, you wit of a townsman? Somehow I doubt it."
"Up here on the surface, it's not enough to be a good hunter, unless you live in the middle of nowhere, of course. You need a trade. Have you considered what you might like to turn your hand to?"
"If I turn my hand to murder, all paths will be open to me."
"Mongrels are stronger, faster, and tougher than humans — so why do they live such harsh lives in the caves? Do your lot have a weakness?"
"If we did, I wouldn't tell you. Toughness and the ability to survive are useless if you haven't got brains to back it up."
"I like your style, but if you want to make a living out of this, try to work more cleanly. You won't get too many repeat customers if you turn every murder scene into a bloodbath."
"You, dwarf, have already forgotten how to take pleasure in killing. The carnage is the best part!"

"Of course, what matters most in an assassin is results. But if you want to earn good money for getting those results, you need to learn how to present yourself. Your appearance needs to inspire confidence in the client."
"The Commander knows what I am capable of. Anyone else can take their opinions and choke on them."
"I like the way you stalk your target and blend effortlessly with the shadows. I may be wrong, but you even seem to stop breathing."
"Oh yes, I know how to be patient. The prey or the enemy may be stronger, but a strike dealt at the perfect moment is enough to ensure supremacy in any encounter."
"You don't see anything shameful in running away? What about the damage it does to your reputation? Your name?"
"Big deal! I'm a thief, ain't I? If I damage my name, I'll just swipe myself a new one!"
"You say you despise the notion of family, but you call your fellow thieflings brother and sister, and you even call me 'Uncle Greybor' sometimes. Don't you see the contradiction there?"
"People like it when you talk to them like you're old pals. Like if I say 'uncle' enough times, maybe you'll have mercy on me and decide not to murder me in my sleep."
"Tell me, Woljif, what's the word on the street in Kenabres about why Kerismei Valensis was named head of the thieflings?"
"Word is that she got the job because brother One-horn had himself a little accid... hang on a sec!"
"Still, what do you personally prefer — blades or magic? What I'm asking is, which is more to your taste?"
"I prefer my demons dead so they can't try to bite my tail off. I'll sing ditties and walk on my head if that's what it takes to kill 'em!"
"The longer I listen to you, the more convinced I am that you're ridiculously lucky. If I were you, I'd make a sacrifice to Norgorber as a sign of my thanks."

"Hey, hey, you can stop right there, ol' fella. Us Mendev types, we love our Iomedae, we don't know no Norgorber... Uh, what size of a sacrifice are we talkin' here, a big 'un? What? I'm just curious."
"I think you must be the only demon who's decided to be good. Is it really so hard for your kind?"
"I guess most demons don't even consider the possibility."
"Hey, so what's it like — being immortal? Knowing that if you're lucky your time is never going to run out?"
"It's not a great as you might think. I know plenty who were driven mad by the idea of eternity, the immensity of it. Living too long is as much a curse as dying too soon."

"So, the point of their jokes is that I'm half lizard, half man. Like I have two natures. That's why all the jokes play on words involving the number two — two-faced, two's company, in two minds. Get it?"
"Ah, I think I understand. This is what mortals call a double entendre, yes?"
"Sorry, but you've got no chance. There's no way you'll last longer than me. I'm just more experienced, you have to accept it."
"No, wait. It looks so easy! You take a spoon... hang it off the tip of your nose... I don't understand, why does it always fall off?"
"The succubi we've met didn't seem all that tempting to me. Maybe because they all wanted to kill me."
"We... I mean, they would use spells if they truly wanted to tempt you."
"A camellia is a plant, right? Something like water hemlock?"
"And Lann is some specimen of underground fauna? Like a horned toad?"
"If people's appearance reflected their inner life, no one would leave the house without a mask. And nobles wouldn't leave without a cloak concealing their entire body!"
"I wouldn't say your appearance reflects your mind. If that were true, you'd be the size of a mouse."
"Mmm, smells good. What is it?"
"I accidentally threw a moldy log on the fire..."
"I think you're the type of person who could strip the flesh from my face in the night, and then in the morning blame it on a pack of wild dogs."
"I would never in a million years come near your face. And I am sure the wild dogs would also lose their appetite."

"Do you know what your problem is? You're caught between two worlds, just like me. One half of you is a lady with a lace handkerchief and all the airs and graces you'd expect, but the other half is a brutal killer who revels in the carnage of battle. You need to choose who you are."
"I am but a young, gentle lady who has been forced to pick up a weapon to defend my home. There is no duality in me, mongrel."
"Well, what's it like to sleep on the ground and subsist on rations? It must seem like torture to you — nobles wouldn't normally sink so low."
"Hardly. Do you know how my antecedents amassed all the wealth I now enjoy? They slept on the ground and subsisted on rations until they got what they wanted."

"I have an idea for a new pastime for you and your little friends: picnics mongrel style. Rat-tail soup, salad made from suspect mutated mushrooms, and constant attacks from cave monsters on all sides while you eat."
"That sounds... like it will be all the rage next season!"
"You pride yourself on being a rake and a libertine, but could you ever bring yourself to sleep with a mongrel? I bet you'd toss your cookies at the first whiff of one."
"If this is you propositioning me, then I'm game. Now, how much would you care to bet?"
"I wonder, are you always such a nightmare, or are you making an exception for us rabble? You probably act differently around highborn folk."
"You're quite mistaken, my scaled friend. I don't treat people like dirt because they are of a lower station than I am. I simply treat people like dirt. All of them."
"Here comes Count Arendae, now intimately familiar with all the delights of life on the march! Well, Count? How are you finding answering nature's call in the bushes?"
"It is all a matter of degree, my scaled friend. I feel quite well disposed toward the bushes, when they are not trying to eat me, that is."
"I can't imagine what you're actually like, deep down. If someone cracked open your golden shell and left you to fend for yourself in the world, what would happen, Count?"

"I do not know, but it would be amusing to swap places with you for a day. What do you say, Lann? How would it feel to inhabit my 'golden shell' in a world of plots, prejudice, and high expectations?"
"I wish your father was still alive — I'd shake some sense into him! What was he thinking, dragging a child into war?"
"Yes... I'd like for my dad to be alive too."
"People excel at forgetting their own. Forgetting people like us under the ground. Or you, freezing outside their window..."
"It's not their fault. Who can think of another's pain when they're hurting and afraid all the time?"
"When the war is over, we could take you to Kyonin, to your mother."
"My mama is an elf, she can wait for me however long it takes. But your mama can't wait that long. Maybe you'd better hurry back to her?"
"I'm starting to think you talk in riddles just so you can watch the other person try to look smart when they don't have a clue what you mean."
"I just talk about things as they are. It's other people who make riddles out of what I say."
"How come you eat so little? The hungry times are over for you now, you can eat as much as you need."
"Don't worry about me, I take as much as I need. And that's not much at all."
"What's it like, renouncing all your vows? Does it weigh on your conscience? Oh right, you demons don't have one of those."
"You want to know what it's like? It's like throwing off heavy shackles, like eating my fill for the first time after a long fast."
"Is it just me, or have you lost your sense of humor? The Arueshalae I knew smiled a lot more than you do."
"It takes a lot to make me smile. Many people see it only once in their life — when I'm about to take that life."
"You've traveled all over but never found anywhere to settle down. So, is wanderlust really as powerful as they say?"

"Wandering is destiny. You don't choose the road — it chooses you. And even if you lock yourself away behind a dozen barred doors, eventually something will lure you out of your hole again. And that's when you'll realize your traveling bag has been waiting packed the whole time."

"I'm struggling to adapt to how you do things on the surface. Below, our tribes only fight over food, and then we go our separate ways again. No mongrel would ever think of sending killers to murder his neighbors."
"Trust me, if you had an excess of food, people, and free time, you'd quickly start thinking of more sophisticated ways of killing each other."
"Do surface assassins have any hobbies? Knitting? Embroidery? Pottery?"
"Interesting question, lad. I tie strong knots and snares that tighten in an instant. I suppose you'd call that... macramé?"

"Maybe I should take up smoking too? I could get a pipe, grow a long curly mustache, brush it with a special little brush... Nah, it wouldn't work. I'd only be able to grow a one-sided mustache. The smoking plan is off."
"Tobacco could shorten your already shortened life. But personally, it's made my life a little more pleasant."

"It doesn't sit right with me, that killing has become a trade like any other. 'Hey man, I just heard about a great cobbler that's set up shop in town, and an assassin with a great reputation's just moved into my street!'"
"You probably spoke without thinking, but killing has been a profession for a long time. And it's not just people like me who kill for money, but soldiers, mercenaries, and politicians as well."
"It's not that I miss the creatures from my old hunting grounds in the caves..."
"But back there, if a beast didn't eat you for lunch, you could eat it instead. It doesn't work like that with demons."
"You can get used to anything. To monsters, to demons, to war, even to peace."
"But the huge sky overhead... Every time I look up, it sends a shiver down my spine."
"Scoot over, I want my scaly side facing the fire."
"My lizard side always gets colder than my warm-blooded side."
"Time for my daily assimilation training."
"The sun is not dangerous, Lann. It will not burn your skin. It will not blind you if you look at it. Love the sun! The sun is good!"
"Would you look at that? I've made it through another day without being killed or eaten, and without looking any more decrepit than I did yesterday."
"Not too shabby for a mongrel!"
"How could you forget your family, Nenio? Your roots, your ancestors, your heritage. I don't understand you!"
"Are there people of historical significance among your ancestors? Did your forebears invent something great? Then I don't understand why you remember them."
"Leave me alone, Nenio. Please, just give it up already."
"But I absolutely must sketch you for my addendum to the Encyclopedia. Now remove your clothes!"
"Your book is going to be no good to anyone. You think somebody being chased by an axe beak is going to get out your encyclopedia to find out how fast the thing can run?"

"I would hope that they would consult the Encyclopedia beforehand. But if the reader is already fleeing from an axe beak, then... Their friends will appreciate the addendum describing the burial customs particular to that region."
"Can you just leave me alone? Experiment on yourself, I'm not some lab animal!"
"Despite the conditions in which the subject came to maturity, it can compose intelligent sentences. Fascinating..."

"I've seen plenty of people who don't care about anyone else, but you're the first person I've met who doesn't care about themselves. You'd chop your own head off for the sake of science if you had to."
"But not any time soon. Experiments to investigate the reanimation of a severed head will require an assistant and a laboratory!"
"I noticed a small gap in your guard. When you strike to the side, you leave your shoulder open for a counter strike."
"Really? I never noticed. Get yourself a practice stick and show me."

"You know, Regill, when you joined, I thought you wouldn't do any good in our little squad. I always thought officers preferred giving orders to crawling in the mud, spending nights out in the open, and actually doing some fighting. I'm glad I was wrong."
"I used to be a part of a similar team. We went scouting, ran sabotage missions... As you can see, I didn't lose my skills while leading the chapter."
"I used to think that even in the Hellknights the smooth talkers would be the ones to make commander, not war dogs like you."
"My usefulness as a paralictor was self-evident."

"You would've liked being in my tribe: strict rules you have to follow if you want to survive, nice quiet environment, nothing to distract you from your thoughts... It's like a dream come true for a Hellknight!"
"Survival without a greater goal is meaningless. But you are right, mongrels live more sensibly than many other peoples."
"Your Bleaching creeps me out. I wouldn't want to live life frantically seeking out new experiences."
"It is surprising how few people understand this. Being in thrall to one's emotions is no better than being in thrall to Numerian narcotics."
"You aren't from a noble family, right? You were taught to fight and read prayers, but I can pick a street rat out of a crowd of aristocrats!"
"Right, and they keep looking at me like I'm about to blow my nose on the curtains. Especially the ones whose knightly services don't go any further than marching in parades."
"Did you break another one of the straps on your armor? Here, let me show you another knot... It's just as good but it won't fray so quickly."
"Whoa! Thanks! Show me that again."
"I don't know how I lived without beer up to now! Beer alone was worth coming up to the surface for."
"And you still haven't tried good wine!"
"I don't understand you paladins. Well, really it's that I don't understand the huge, clanking suits of armor you wear... Watch out, here comes Sir Clanks-a-Lot, everybody!"
"So what? This way everybody knows that good is on its way to beat down evil!"
"You think there's no glory without risk... but why do you want glory? So you can fight off crowds of admirers?"
"Glory is nice to have, but you can't let it go to your head. When I was a street thief, I lived for pulling reckless stunts, to see the way the other street kids looked at me afterward."
"Hey, Sosiel! If you paint my portrait, will your goddess curse you for blasphemy?"
"How could a portrait of a friend be blasphemy? If you truly want me to, I'd be glad to paint you."
"We have our own craftsmen. They weave cords, carve bone, make figurines out of mud... Your goddess probably wouldn't even look at garbage like that, would she?"
"Why not? I think she'd be glad that even in such terrible circumstances, you never stopped longing for beauty."
"If I ever find myself in a temple of Shelyn, which side should I turn to face the altar so I don't offend her?"
"Face her with your heart."
"Have you ever thought of giving it all up and going home? The crusade doesn't sound like a place where a priest of love and beauty will be very happy."
"I am not here for my own happiness. Spirits are low among the crusaders, and I want to remind them that love and beauty still exist in this world."
"Do you Shelynites ever argue about what's beautiful and what's not? Do you gather in basements at night and hold bare-knuckle brawls to decide which paintings are worthy of Shelyn?"
"If such a thing is happening, then I am not being invited to them. But throwing teacups? That, unfortunately, I have seen."
"You're lucky to have your brother. Don't make him worry like that ever again. If I'd been in his place, I would have shoved that Shelynite glaive so far up your—"
"I swear I will never hurt him again. Never."
"Apologies in advance if I make jokes about things you don't find funny. It's my way of avoiding confrontation. Sometimes I forget that it doesn't work on everyone."
"Do you think I'm some delicate flower? We had a guy in our unit who was left without arms or legs, but he survived. So we called him 'Lucky.' Ha. It's still funny."
"Warm-blooded game was hard to come by underground, but we had giant spiders galore. How about Sarkoris — did you have to deal with critters like that?"

"Well, in a lean time, you'd be glad of a spider to eat, no doubt... But on the whole, many-legged beasties weren't high on our list of delicacies. Except for bees, o' course — folks in every village kept beehives!"
"So, Wenduag, how are you settling in? Found any new friends to stab in the back?"
"You have so little trust in others, Lann. Especially for someone who sees himself as a goody-goody."
"Stop saying you're loyal to the Commander. I don't believe a single word that comes out of your mouth."
"Then you stop talking about how hideous you are. Or else I'll start thinking you're fishing for compliments."
"Don't even think of coming near my tent, unless you want an arrow between the eyes."
"Subtle... Are you sure it's hatred that's provoking such a strong reaction in you, Lann?"
"Wow, you're still here and you haven't even slit anybody's throat yet!"
"You're starting to repeat yourself. Running out of clever jibes, Lann?"
"You think you can seduce anyone up on the surface? We're monsters to the uplanders, Wendu."
"I'll do and be whatever I want. But you don't understand that, Lann — you have always cared too much about what others think of you."
"You know, you lucked out with your horns. At least yours don't tear a hole in every hood you wear. But we'd be even luckier if..."
"...we never had the damn things in the first place."
"You blame your troubles on everybody else, but you always claim the credit for anything that goes right. Is that really any way to live?"
"See, the human side of your mouth is flappin', but all I hear is a lizardy hiss."
"If you're so afraid of going near the enemy, I can teach you how to shoot from a bow. True, it's pretty tough to aim when you're running away from the battlefield."
"Whenever you decide to finally kick the bucket, give me fair warnin', is all I ask — if I'm gonna be eatin' cave slime at your wake, I need to line my stomach good and proper first."
"In our tribe, stealing was more trouble than it was worth. Thieves were severely punished. But up on the surface, you can rise quite high by robbing other people, I've learned."
"It's called si-vil-i-zay-shon, geddit?"
"It must be a pain, having to cut a hole in every pair of pants for your tail. For once I actually feel lucky compared to somebody else."
"It ain't just a case of makin' a hole — I need to stitch it so the whole seam doesn't split. That's why I learned to sew, my tail's a blessing in disguise!"
"I analyzed the aerodynamic properties of your wings, demon girl. My conclusion: they are incapable of flight."
"And yet, they do fly. I hope this isn't the only time I manage to violate the laws of the universe."
"Statistics indicate the girl demon will be attractive to 82 percent of female individuals on Golarion and 97 percent of male individuals."
"Oh... I... I'm flattered. Thank you. But let's not bring this up again."
"Demon girl, I need you to kiss me. This is motivated by scientific, rather than romantic, interest. Just let me get my chronometer and we can begin."
"You're insane! What are you planning to measure — the time it takes for me to kill you with a kiss? Don't ever ask me to do anything like that ever again!"
"If abrikandilus hate all that is beautiful, how do they fight on the same side as succubi?"
"Succubi are only beautiful on the outside, inside they are nothing but hunger and ugliness. Maybe even abrikandilus can sense it?"
"Horn length — check. Now let's measure your wingspan... please spread your wings out fully."
"I can't stretch them out any further... I'm trying..."
"By the way, did you know that the amount of money in an individual's possession is directly proportional to the weight of the secrets that individual is hiding?"
"And did you know that the length of an individual's tongue is inversely proportional to the length of their life?"

"Rich girl, my answer to the question you ask me every day is not going to change. I truly do not remember where I was born or how I came to be in Absalom. It was useless information that I preferred to forget."
"You're hiding something, my friend. It's quite unbecoming! Let's share confidences! Here, I'll tell you my darkest secret — I am a glutton for chocolate. Now tell me yours."
"Rich girl, I want to know more about your childhood. I am composing an addendum about the lives of illegitimate children of noble families in Avistan. Or is 'bastards' the correct term?"

"Why you... Never mind, taking offense at your lack of manners would be foolish. But one day we shall take a walk somewhere free from listening ears, and I shall tell you everything... more than you could hope for."
"Rich girl, quick question: what do you see in this picture?"
"Just some ink blots... It looks like a heart lying in a pool of blood. Why are you showing me something so vile?"
"Rich girl, did you know that, statistically, half-elves live longer than ordinary people, although they are twice as likely to die of food poisoning?"
"Let me guess, all those half-elves tried your experimental concoctions?"
"By the way, did you know that the amount of money in an individual's possession is directly proportional to the number of secrets that individual is hiding?"
"A most intriguing observation! I say, let's try to guess the secrets my cousin Galfrey is hiding!"

"Hey, aasimar boy. I calculated the number of sexual encounters you've had in your life, considering the young age at which you presumably became sexually active, and your lack of general moral principles. The total was 2184."
"Let's look at your workings. Hmm, so, three times a week, twice on each occasion, for seven years. Ah, there's your error — I go three rounds on Sundays. If we recalculate, that gives us... 2548!"
"Aasimar boy, you so eagerly suggest ideas for new experiments. You clearly have an interest in the natural sciences. You could be my assistant."
"Alas, my dear fellow scientist, we work in different fields. I'm not interested in taking part in your experiments, and you, perhaps, would not agree to take part in mine."
"Let's see if aasimars truly possess superior memory recall to humans! Please list all your ancestors going back to the founder of your line."
"Father, mother, grandfather, grandmother, my other grandfather, my other grandmother, four great-grandfathers, four great-grandmothers, my great-great-grandfather — what?"

"Hypothesis: the party's sexual interest in me surged when it became known that I am a kitsune. I am going to survey my comrades in order to confirm my hypothesis. Aasimar boy, what is it about foxes you find sexually appealing? Be precise."
"So, you did not even consider the possibility that I do not find — oh, dash it all... The tail, obviously."
"...to the far south of Garund, at the very limits of the civilized word, lies the Mwangi Expanse. This land is inhabited by dinosaurs, huge lizards whose every step makes the earth tremble."
"I like that one! Tell me another fairy tale, please, please, please!"
"The burned girl's injuries can be healed, but the treatment will not be cheap. As regards her mental wounds, I am not sure that science is yet advanced enough to help her."
"What? I need to be healed? But Nenio, I'm not even sick!"
"I performed some calculations and now I can predict the probability that your sermons will be successful. The current probability is one-hundredth of a percent..."
"That's good! I thought you were going to tell me I had no chance at all."
"Interesting fact: on average, the elves of Kyonin permit 7.5 humans to enter their lands each year."
"But... what do they need half a person for?"
"When you returned to the Abyss, demon girl, did your powers increase or decrease? How did your protracted starvation affect them?"
"I think of it as a diet. It made me even more beautiful and... gave me new ideas."
"How quickly can you extract the life force from a living creature? I would like to conduct an experiment. Let's start with this rat. Begin."
"Kiss a rat? I can, of course... but I'd rather you brought me something tastier."
"...thus, to remove the skin of the dead dragon without damaging it, you must first lift the scales at the neck, and then make a careful incision between them..."
"The cut needs to be made with a red-hot knife, if circumstances allow. Don't forget to write that down, it's important!"
"I calculated the estimated remaining lifespan of the dwarf boy, based on statistics and the danger of his current work. The result was five months, nineteen days."
"Ha. Come back and tell me that in six months."
"Dwarf boy, tell me more about the place where you learned to kill people. You called it Hawk's Nest?"
"If I told you, they'd hunt you down... Wait, you look like the prospect appeals to you. Forget it, you shouldn't even joke about it. There's no getting away from Daggermark assassins."
"According to my calculations, accumulation of wealth is pointless — at a certain stage, expenses increase exponentially, exceeding income."
"I can easily believe that some wastrels spend all their wealth on girls and card games. But a businessman knows how to handle his money. Your calculations are only correct for a certain population."
"Here's an interesting fact: to dissolve a body in acid cheaply and without the use of magic, you simply need to..."
"Go slower, please. It looks like it's my turn to start making note of interesting facts."
"Thus I have scientifically proven that the maximum distance an arrow can travel is achieved when it is released from a bow at an angle of forty-five degrees from the horizon."
"What? You've done it already? Did you consider wind speed and direction? Then go and run the numbers again. I'll just nap here. Your mumbling about calculations is relaxing."
"Just think about the contribution you could make to society, mongrel boy! So please set aside your emotions and consider my proposal rationally!"
"No, no, and did I mention no? I do not give you permission to dissect my body after my death in the 'interests of science'!"
"You believe that the mutations and high mortality of mongrels are a product of demonic influence, however, you cannot discount the possibility of interbreeding. I will show you in a graph!"
"I hope that thick red line going sharply downward means something good."
"Your right side reacts more vigorously to temperature changes than your left side. I wonder what will happen if we freeze your right side and set your left side on fire..."
"Demons are always trying to do that to me — guess how their experiments ended."
"...as such, the genetic predisposition of an individual for magical abilities is not an overriding factor in the manifestation of said abilities in said individual!"
"Hello, have you all fallen asleep?"
"I wonder if a ringing effect similar to a bell is produced inside the helmet of Iomedae's herald when the phrase 'In the name of Iomedae' is exclaimed?"
"This hypothesis requires its own experiment. I need a bucket."
"Final check. Knee pads in place, pillow in case of spontaneous collapse in place, chronometer in place and running."
"I hereby commence the experiment! Today we will learn if members of my race are capable of sleeping standing up."
"Foxes are incredibly intelligent and quick-witted. They are also noted for their high fluffiness quotient and their aesthetically pleasing hue."
"Yes, I think that is a sufficiently objective description."
"Every scientist thinks their field research is going to continue forever!"
"But as the saying goes — at the end of the day, we all must compile our bibliography and references..."
"Did you know that..."
"We don't know and we prefer not to find out. I am certain that whatever you say will be of no value whatsoever."

"Did you know that, despite the censure of many developed countries, the mass public executions carried out by the orders of Hellknights have put a stop to many individuals who are a danger to society?"
"Your approval means nothing, individual who is a danger to society."
"Could you bleach a little in front of me, gnome boy? I would like to conduct a personal observation of this process."
"Could you slowly die in front of me? I wouldn't mind seeing that for myself either."
"Gnome boy, please complete this brief questionnaire on the Bleaching. You are willing to do your part for science, aren't you?"
"What you do is not science. There is no system or sense to it."
"Here is a curious fact about Cheliax: the 'White Plague' is not a disease at all, but a series of murders and suicides orchestrated by cultists."
"You have just told me a fact that every five-year-old child in Cheliax knows, and you did not even stop to think before doing so. Your mind cannot keep up with your tongue."
"I am continuing my efforts to identify and record paladin curse words. Hey, paladin girl! I covered your armor with soot!"
"You're like a little kid. I can't get upset with you, let alone swear at you. Come over here, help me clean this armor."

"I am continuing my efforts to identify and record paladin curse words. Hey, paladin girl! I covered your armor with soot again, and I slashed your cloak and spat in your soup. Well, I think it was your soup, I can't be one-hundred percent certain."
"Nenio. Fine, but just for you. Are you listening? Are you ready? Bull-Shit! Feel better now?"
"No, you're wrong. There are treants in the desert too! Garundis call them tobongos."
"You're kidding me! Fine, I lose, which means I drink. Next... I bet that in all of Golarion a sentient slime has never held any government post!"
"Here's an interesting fact: the second arms of glabrezus grow where nipples grow on humans. Could human nipples evolve into an extra pair of limbs over time?"
"Sorry, I'm not drunk enough for this conversation."
"How evil does a person have to be for a paladin to be able to detect the evil within them? Can a paladin use their magic to sense, for instance, minor irritation or a latent sympathy for demons?"
"Uh. I don't know what to tell you, friend, but... I think everybody can sense when another person is irritated. Everybody except you, that is."

"I am continuing my research into the paladin girl's addiction to experiment participation. Today's objective is to survey the subject! Paladin girl, when did you first feel the urge to get involved in scientific research?"

"The day I made friends with a science-obsessed weirdo by the name of Nenio! Listen... science is great and all, but I'm not helping you out of any kind of 'addiction,' I'm doing it just to, you know, help. Understand?"

"A brother is a person who has similar genes to you. His personality, behavior, and moral principles are distinct. Losing him means eliminating the need to cooperate with a person imposed on you by your family."
"If you thought speaking of this in such blunt terms would shock me into discussion, you were wrong."
"Setting aside the aesthetic pleasure of beholding paintings, what practical purpose do they serve?"
"What makes you think that aesthetics isn't practical? Beauty commands attention and can convey ideas that would go unnoticed otherwise. And also, paintings can cover an unsightly spot on a wall."
"Now I will try to determine the best strategy for extinguishing a tent on fire, where the attempt must be made from inside the burning tent."

"Hey! Don't even think of it! It's not only dangerous for you, it's dangerous for the rest of us! Don't you remember that I asked you not to conduct any more experiments involving fire and our possessions... No, of course you don't!"
"Yes, cleric boy, the weather graph for the Wound looks exactly as I described — excellent work. But what informational value do the flowers and little people add?"
"They are allegorical depictions of the times of year and the cardinal directions. Sometimes symbols tell us more than numbers alone."
"I estimated the probability of meeting a cleric of Shelyn on the front line in the Worldwound. You have confounded my calculations, cleric boy."
"Is that your way of saying, 'What are you doing here?' Even you doubt me, I see..."
"As a human who has spent a long time among demons, you could write a treatise on the subject. Even though you aren't a scholar, it will be a valuable source for future research."
"No. What's done is done. I do not want to remember it."
"There is a striking similarity between you and the cleric boy. Is he your son?"
"Captivity did not do my appearance any favors, but I don't think I look that old..."
"You have a most fascinating head shape, bearded boy. If you'll allow, I will measure the prominence of your brow ridge—"
"Why don't I count your teeth instead? After I knock 'em out of your skull. What do you think of that for an experiment, sorceress?"
"Hey, mongrel girl. Tell me what mongrels eat in the catacombs. It's for my Encyclopedia."
"Other mongrels, obviously. Why else would we have such short lives?"
"Just think about the contribution you could make to society, mongrel girl! So please set aside your emotions and consider my proposal rationally!"
"I don't care what happens to my body after I'm dead. But you'll die long before I do, trust me."
"Mongrel girl, your account contradicts what other people have told me. Are you sure?"
"Absolutely. You probably talked to some liars who've never even seen a cave lizard before! They are actually very friendly creatures and they love to be petted."
"The facts you tell me about mongrel life do not always correspond to the reality. I think I need a larger sample."
"Ha ha ha, you finally realized, did you? I've been feeding you nonsense this whole time! And you believed it like a gullible child!"
"Mongrel girl, what other spider parts do you have apart from your appendages? Silk glands? A chitin shell?"
"The ability to do away with annoying flies like you."
"Tiefling boy, are you certain that setting fire to the temple in Drezen will bring about a sudden downpour?"

"Yep, yep, that's how it works. The gods protect the temple against all fires, or somethin' like that. But let me know when you're about to start. You can bet everyone will panic when they see the flames, chucking out all their worldly possessions — some upstanding citizen's gotta keep an eye on 'em."

"Due to the proximity to the Worldwound, many inhabitants of Kenabres are suspicious of tieflings. Tiefling boy, tell me, what are tieflings doing to change public opinion? How are they dealing with this problem?"
"Uhh, we pinch stuff from people who really don't like us. We rob other people too, but we don't clean 'em out in the same way. That's like justice, right?"

"Tiefling physiology has been a topic of only cursory scientific study. Since I have the good fortune of having a test subject on hand, I would like to deepen my knowledge and conduct a few experiments."
"What do you say to this brave challenge: 'How many cherry rolls can the average tiefling eat before he gets sick?'"
"...and therefore we can conclude that the atmospheric front moving from the west to the east will bring only minor precipitation, but there will be a heavy downpour in Nerosyan!"
"All I said was, 'Nice day, ain't it?'"
"Stand still, boy. I want to determine how many balls of mud can be speared on the horn of a tiefling."
"Uh, listen, Nenio! How 'bout we swap out the mud for nice freshly baked rolls? It'll make the experiment more interestin', and I promise to stand very, very still!"
"A demon cannot repent and fight in the crusade against demons. It is absurd."
"Desna granted me a miracle, and miracles are always absurd."
"Don't stray from the camp fire. If you do, I will consider it an attempt to flee."
"I don't have anywhere to run to. But... I don't want to cause you unnecessary alarm."
"Before we eat, I need to test the food for poison or sedative."
"Why am I not surprised that you say that while looking directly at me?"
"You are not the first and you will not be the last succubus to wear faith as a disguise. By your falseness you entrap the righteous."
"It is not false. It is the first true and honest thing I have done in my life. Although I doubt you will believe that."

"I have heard accounts of supernatural creatures changing their nature and becoming something different. But these cases are so rare that it would be absurd to see them as justification for trusting any demon claiming repentance."
"Thank you for reminding me that I am not the only one to have traveled this path. If there is a chance I will succeed, even one in a million, I will not give up."
"I hope you keep that spirit of yours under control. I wouldn't want it attacking us in the middle of battle."
"There are some forces you can't rein in. Unfortunate, isn't it? But don't worry, my spirit isn't going to betray me."
"I know people like you. Bored aristocrats who think that war is another diversion, like hunting. They usually get killed, and they get their allies killed too."
"Oh well! At least I'm not going to die of boredom."
"A sheltered noblewoman able to wield a blade with deadly skill. Highly suspect. What are you hiding?"
"You're always keeping such a close eye on me, Paralictor. Tread carefully, or else I'll think you've developed a tendre for me."
"Many aristocrats possess an unfounded pride in themselves. But you are not even an aristocrat, just the illegitimate daughter of one. So how do you explain your pridefulness?"
"What is it you call pridefulness, Hellknight? A sense of one's own dignity?"
"Shamans are not to be trusted. Any of them could be possessed by a spirit without warning."
"You fear that which you do not understand. Therefore, you cannot judge the merit of your comrades or your enemies."
"If you weren't an able healer, noble, I would vote to have you expelled from the party."
"Fortunately, no one is holding such a vote."
"Such power, and it is bestowed upon an undisciplined whelp. I cannot abide waste."
"Quite right. I am too good for this little world. Thank you for noticing."
"You expend too much effort trying to rile the aristocracy. The expedient thing would be to renounce your title and exit this fight."
"And miss out on the greatest diversion of my life? I think not!"
"You are the perfect illustration of the problems that arise in societies where titles and power are inherited rather than earned."

"Oh, I wholeheartedly agree! And I daresay even the most diehard royalists of Mendev agree with you. They look at me and think, 'How can that walking heresy be anywhere higher than dead last in the order of succession?'"

"It is interesting how differently people understand the term 'scum.' In that category, I would include those who spend their lives in idleness, like plants, capable of only drawing moisture from the soil and bathing in the rays of the sun."

"Why did you take such a circuitous route just to call me a useless piece of rubbish? I have no qualms about calling you an uptight, malicious automaton who is patently avoiding acknowledging his own hubris. So, please, do not hold back on my account."
"You waste too much effort on those who are unworthy."
"How would I know who is worthy and who isn't? I just help whoever I can."
"You've been through more than most in the crusade army, and you remain unbroken. If there were two hundred people like you in Kenabres, the city would never have fallen."
"In truth, I'm just like everyone else. Everyone else is just like me."
"You have a strong character. That always attracts weak people who need to latch on to someone else. Don't do them any favors and don't seek them out."
"Me? Strong? Oh no, that's not right, I find it hard to even lift a bucket of water."
"Your body also has a limited amount of strength. You must develop it if you do not wish to die an inglorious death."
"I burned and I did not die. I am protected by good people, like Soot and grandma!"
"Saints typically die a most painful death. Are you prepared to accept that, in order for people to follow your teachings?"
"Dying isn't hard at all. But after I'm dead, I won't be able to help anyone! Sooner or later I will have to die, but until then I'm going to try to live."
"Do you think the crusade will benefit you? Your standing in the Abyss? No. You are a mere tool."
"What does that make you, Hellknight?"

"In a way, I am glad that fate brought us together, succubus. I hope your story will spread far and wide and become a cautionary tale of what happens when one trusts the 'good intentions' of a demon."
"I will be famous, then! What an entertaining idea. A hundred years after your Bleaching has reduced you to ash, mortals will still tremble at the sound of my name and say, 'It's Arueshalae...'"
"It is more efficient to slit a throat from right to left: that way the larynx is immediately severed and the target cannot raise the alarm."
"I've always done it left to right, and I plan to keep doing it that way. Otherwise, the blood from the jugular will splash onto my sleeve, and the guards might get suspicious."
"You are trustworthy, Greybor. I could recommend you for induction into the Order of the Scar... Those worthy Hellknights hunt down killers. Your skills and experience would prove useful to them."
"Thank you, but I'm done taking orders and listening to lectures about discipline. I got enough of that during my training. I prefer to answer to no one but myself."
"You are a skilled tactician, Greybor. You should be serving as an officer, not fighting in the vanguard."
"No, commanding isn't for me. I can't help it, I just love working with my hands!"

"I value you greatly as a comrade-in-arms, Greybor, but I also serve the law. It is highly likely that one day your profession will see you dragged up on the scaffold, and I will be there as one of the executioners or guards."
"I understand full well that such an end is more than likely for me. Well... if I am to die on the scaffold, at least I'll see a familiar face before I go."
"Working with demons does not disgust you. Why?"
"For the same reason that some priests will deign to heal their enemies: relations between the warring sides may change, but the essence of my work will remain the same."
"You're a true warrior. You have what matters most — backbone. Unyielding, like a rod of iron."
"If hard iron in your body is what makes a true warrior, then my bow turns enemies into true warriors every battle!"
"You are a skilled archer but you sometimes lack discipline."
"Please, if I get any more disciplined, I'll have ask the Commander's permission to sneeze."

"Listen, Lann. Do not take offense at my words, they are well intended: ambivalence and regret are like poison to a soldier's morale. You must put aside your grudge against fate and your fear of death, before it's too late."
"I get it. You're talking based on experience. But be honest — you had a choice, to fight against the Bleaching or to accept it. I never had a choice — I'm going to die soon no matter what I do."
"The crusades do not need one-off feats of heroism. What they need are regular, reliable victories."
"I wouldn't say no to regular, reliable victuals. The cooking pot's been standing empty all day, not so much as a fly has gone in it!"
"You could become a Hellknight, but you are a loner. You do not understand why we organize ourselves in orders."
"I just think you can enforce order without wearing spiky armor. Of course, it doesn't hurt."
"Come at me with scissors again and it may be the last thing you do."

"I don't quite understand what you mean, gnome boy — reformulate your proposition about the possibility of my death more clearly. And turn around — I need to cut off a lock of your bleached hair, to compare it to the unbleached sample."
"I'm watching you, Nenio. When you make one wrong move, I'll be right there to see it. But just know that I've got my eye on you, always."
"Well, then, you can swat the flies away while I sleep."
"You are dangerous, out of control, and unteachable. Your experiments are reckless. People like you should be locked up or tossed straight on the pyre. You are an Areelu Vorlesh in the making."
"Thank you for the compliment, gnome boy. In truth, I have a long way to go to match the great Lady Vorlesh, but your comparison has filled me with renewed zeal!"
"Either you have not even considered what will happen if your notes fall into the enemy's hands, or you have considered it... because you are a spy."
"I am not spying for anyone! It would distract me from my scholarly observation of crusader behavior!"
"In my opinion, you are far too captivated by the criminal Areelu Vorlesh."
"Oh, she is a great scientist, indeed. I have a list of questions I will ask her when we have an opportunity to talk. It is quite a long list — I expect our colloquium will take two to three days."
"They say the worthiest fighters become devils in Hell. If it's true, it's only fair."
"Lazy fighters can retire. But for true warriors, death is no reason to shirk one's duty."
"My fingers are getting white... How much more time do I have? Twenty years? Ten? One?"
"I do not fear death. But what if the Bleaching makes me lazy and undisciplined? I hope I don't live to see such a disgrace."
"No discipline, no chain of command, a queen who trusts anyone off the street — this is a circus, not a crusade."
"It is an enigma to me how Mendev has functioned up till now."
"I cannot decide if I am pleased or displeased by the need to temporarily give up command of my Hellknight unit."
"I have invested a great deal of effort in training my junior officers. We will see how they handle this test on their own."
"It has been so long since I was last in Cheliax, I am no longer sure I can call it my home."
"But a Hellknight does not need a home. My order and my purpose are enough."
"Sometimes victory requires you to do things for which the gods will strip a paladin of her powers. You need more weapons training, or you'll be helpless in such a situation."
"Are you serious? Training for failure? For that alone, the goddess would strip me of my powers — and she would be right to!"
"Suffering develops character and hardens the soul."
"Like hell it does. Suffering maims and kills. Only crazy people like you see something good in it!"
"If you want to survive, you need to hone your self-control. I can offer you some advice."
"A Hellknight teaching a paladin? Sounds like the start of a bad joke."
"Your flexible morals and open acceptance are difficult to understand. You are happy to defend a confirmed thief, yet you do not see me as a worthy ally."

"My code says, 'my strength is not in my sword, but in my heart.' Winning the war is not enough, we must still have our humanity by the end of it. You do not understand this or agree with it, and that's the trouble."
"My methods vex you. But you have never been a commander. You do not know what it means to be responsible for achieving a goal, to be responsible for the lives of others."
"You're right, I haven't. But I know what it's like to be responsible for the lives of my comrades. Every paladin of Iomedae knows that."
"You're not a fighter, you're a gardener. I suppose you're a decent enough healer, but you have the soul of a civilian. What are you doing in this war?"
"What you say is true — and praise Shelyn for it. You could say I'm just here to protect my garden from vermin."
"You're making the same mistakes many clerics make. You think that the ability to wear armor makes you invincible. Keep away from the front lines or you'll leave our party without a healer."
"Thank you for your valuable advice, and your touching concern for my safety."
"You think it is a disgrace to be a Hellknight. I think it is a disgrace to be anything else in this war. It is the only logical position."
"But at what cost to your soul?"
"You must say your prayers with greater force and precision in battle. You are lacking in proficiency."
"I am not a Numerian automaton, no matter how much you wish I were. But I will try..."
"Shelyn has the capacity to be a formidable goddess. But it seems her followers do not understand what their glaives are for."
"Glaives are there to be used only when there is no other option."
"You have grown stronger, but your mind is damaged. You are suited to being a gladiator now, but you will never again be a warrior."

"I can't be a Hellknight ever again, that is true. But if the only warriors you recognize are those who wear black armor like you — you're wrong. Anyone who simply wants to defend their friends and their home is a true warrior."

"I have considered the matter and decided that the fault for what happened to you lies partly with the Orders. You never should have been accepted into our ranks — it would have solved many problems before they arose."
"Are you insulting me or pitying me? Or both at once?"
"We do not abide weaklings. The character of every knight is forged by a succession of privations and torments."
"You lot must lead a sweet life indeed, if you have to rustle up privation and torment specially. For us folks in villages, those things happened all on their own."

"Constantly shifting allegiance, latching onto whoever seems likely to be victorious... it seems like a winning strategy, but war consists of many battles where either side can win. You are not so good a strategist as to be able to predict the outcome of the war."
"I'm a good enough strategist to know that victory always goes to the strongest."
"You are relatively effective in combat, but you lack a true soldier's understanding of service. You only follow rules and commands when you are being watched."
"You follow my every move, so how would you know what I do when you're not watching me?"
"Your skills are impressive, but effectiveness in battle is but the smallest part of what being a Hellknight requires."
"I see you. You people on the surface think you're better than everyone else! If you tried to live underground, you'd soon shut up about requirements."
"This 'power' you so desperately seek, do you even know what it is?"
"I do not need to know, I can feel it inside. I am drawn to it like the roots of a plant reach out for water."
"Once a traitor, always a traitor. Treachery is feebleness of purpose. It is in the blood."
"You still think you can judge me, when I have the Commander's trust? You have gone too far, gnome."
"Your place is on a gallows, thief, and not in a company of crusaders."
"Oh, going for the gallows today? Very nice. Did you get lucky last night or summat? Usually you're threatenin' me with a pyre."
"No."
"I didn't even ask you nothin'!"
"Your shadow. Why did the inquisitors of Kenabres not investigate you?"
"The paladins told 'em there was no problem. And while the two lots of 'em were havin' a barney over it, I took off. Sorry to disappoint, Reggie."
"How is it the Kenabres inquisition never punished your family for its demonic links? Such a crime carries a death sentence in wartime."
"Who said we weren't punished, eh? Gran did her time in the torture chamber, all right, that's where she gave birth to my mom. She never did tell me how she got outta there..."
"You should face a tribunal for your desertion during the gargoyle attack."
"What business is it of yours, huh? You ain't my commander! And I thank all the gods for that every single day."
"Hey, sister! Are you moping again? Snap out of it, come over here and have a drink with me!"
"I can't get drunk from your alcohol, but the offer of company is very nice. Thank you... sister."
"What's with the gloomy face? Did somebody say something to you? If somebody's been bothering you, you just point him out to me and I'll smash his face in..."
"No, Seelah, everything's fine. I was just thinking about... the past. It's too bad you can't beat that into submission for me."
"Let me teach you a good Golarion song. You know, where I come from there's a saying: if you want to understand a foreign people, learn their songs."
"That is... surprising. Yes, I'd like to try. Go on."
"Don't listen to people who say you can't atone for past wrongs. If people can fall, they can also rise. If they can't, that means evil is stronger."
"Sometimes I fear that evil truly is stronger. But then I remember how beautiful the light can be, and those thoughts retreat."
"Maybe you don't believe it yourself sometimes, but take it from someone who knows: you are good. And you are doing the right thing."
"Please, Seelah, believe in me! Sometimes I really need to hear that..."
"You shamans are strange. It's like you wield magic like clerics, but with strange spirits instead of gods... It makes me uneasy."
"What does it matter where the power comes from? What matters is it's on our side."
"I can feel evil lurking in you. But you act like a normal person and a good comrade..."
"How should I know what your goddess considers evil? Maybe I wasn't polite enough to my servants? Or didn't give enough coins to beggars in the street?"
"You know, I hope this war at least teaches you how to talk to get along with your comrades-in-arms. I think we've got a decent party here — you could find yourself some friends."
"I'm not here to make friends. I'm here to kill."
"Maybe you can start pitching in a little at the camp? Getting your hands dirty isn't as terrifying as you think."
"Getting one's hands dirty — I thought that was only used to describe some grisly act. I certainly would not wish to do anything like that."
"I have no idea why you're even with us on the crusade. No offense, but you could be swanning around a ballroom somewhere, not dodging demon traps."
"Balls are hectic affairs, and I cannot abide crowds. Traveling with friends and fighting for a common cause is more to my liking."
"You know, you could at least try to look like you give a damn about anyone but yourself!"
"Do my ears deceive me? Is a paladin of Iomedae encouraging me to lie?"
"You're a master at drinking and having a good time — have you never thought of putting all that to good use? By throwing a charity banquet or something?"
"My mother used to do such things. But I... I... I don't have time for such deathly dullness. Next you'll be suggesting I traipse around the homes of deserving poor, basket in arm!"
"A hedgehog has spikes to protect its soft underbelly. What about you? Come on, you can admit it — you lash out at anyone who gets close to you because you're afraid of intimacy, right?"

"My carefully crafted facade lies in tatters! You have unmasked me! I am tormented by my comfortable, luxurious, golden solitude! Incidentally, comparing me to a hedgehog was rather charming. From now on, you can call me that if you like."
"Maybe if you pray to Iomedae, even just once, a miracle will happen. How do you know it won't?"
"I think if I begin to pray, Iomedae herself will be so astonished she will descend from Heaven to find out what calamity has occurred."
"I'll never understand why people enjoy mocking others, even those we don't like."
"I do not understand why I enjoy it so much either. I simply do it and it brings me pleasure."
"Your sermons are so annoying! You're going to preach to the wrong person one day and get a beating for your troubles!"
"Let them beat me if that's what they want, but... wouldn't you protect me?"
"You feel sorry for the cultists? What about the demons? Do you pity them as much as their victims?"
"How can you not feel sorry for anyone? Is there anyone in this world who isn't suffering?"
"Can you move faster and stop goggling around you like a fool all the time?"
"But I don't know if I'll ever see these places again. It will be awful if I can't remember anything interesting before I die."

"All right, Ember. I'll try to explain it one more time. Imagine the gods are your best friends. One of them even helped you out in a difficult situation, saved you like that knight who pulled you out of the pyre. Now imagine that somebody is always going around insulting your friends..."
"But gods aren't your friends. And they never will be. They don't save anyone, all they do is lie."
"I fed your crow. The way she was hopping around my bag of food, you'd think she hadn't eaten for a month."
"Oh... don't believe her, Soot is clever and is just pretending to be hungry! I fed her only half an hour ago."
"Even seeing what you've become, I still think I did the right thing by supporting you. You could have changed, Arueshalae. You just... fell early, like a bird struck down in midair. I'm sorry."
"Not calling me sister anymore, is that right, Seelah? Well, I will keep calling you sister. So that you always remember that little birds die."
"So, what are you going to do now? Go back to the Abyss? There's nobody waiting for you there either."
"I don't see anyone trying to get rid of me. I will be here to get on your nerves for a long while yet!"
"You're proud of what you do — almost as if it was a respectable profession."
"Whereas you think the only honorable killing is killing in the name of a god. That's a zealot's reasoning."
"If you revealed the names of your clients to your victims, that at least would be more honest."
"Do you think your victims accept death more easily because it was technically ordered by Iomedae?"
"I refused to drink with a cold-blooded killer. It's bad enough I have to fight alongside you."
"What'll you say tomorrow if the cold-blooded killer is feeling generous and offers to pay for the first round?"
"Have you heard the saying about there being no pockets in a shroud?"
"I'm not planning to wear a shroud any time soon. My current clothes suit me well, and they just so happen to have plenty of pockets."
"Even you must believe in something apart from gold. Don't deny it."
"Of course I do. I believe in Norgorber. I assume my answer has not improved your opinion of me."
"What's the alcohol situation underground? Do you have anything to drown your sorrows in?"
"You bet! Mold brew is a gourmet's dream. And tourists from Absalom used to come to us for our mushroom infusion!"
"Hmm, it'll be tough getting a helmet to fit you, but we can't leave your head unprotected."
"Just as long as it doesn't have a visor — or else how am I meant to scare the enemy?"
"I get it and all, but why a pirate? Why didn't you dream of being a regular, honest sailor?"
"Come on, I wasn't serious about it — the stories I heard as a kid just stuck in my head, I guess... There are plenty of stories about pirates, but about honest working folk? Meh, not so much."

"I've traveled across almost an entire continent, but I never met a mongrel until you. But I have heard about similar beings that appeared in other parts of the world as a result of other cataclysms, not just the Worldwound."
"Really? So we're not the only lucky ones, then? I didn't know that. Nobody in our tribe knew either, it seems."

"So how have you described paladins in this Encyclopedia of yours, Nenio? I bet it's something like 'bull-headed and boring warriors fixated on the principles of goodness and fairness'? That's how the world sees us, right?"

"My definition is something like 'noble warriors, defenders of the dejected and the downtrodden, who display an aversion to evil in all its manifestations.' But your version is also good. I'll add it in."
"Nenio, I'm amazed by your energy and zest for life. Every time I look at you, you're running around, noting something down, spouting one new idea after another. How do you manage it?"
"I simply enjoy what I do. If life's not like that for you, perhaps you're in the wrong line of work?"
"If you don't manage to kill yourself doing one of your experiments, somebody else will definitely do it for you."

"You are sorely mistaken! My scientific undertaking will be universally applicable and useful to everyone, so it is not in the interests of any of Golarion's inhabitants to hinder my work... This is clear to everyone, yes?"
"How many volumes are there going to be in your Encyclopedia? I bet if you stack them one on top of the other, they'd be as tall as a tower!"
"An excellent question, paladin girl! First, we need to decide which tower we are using as a comparator!"

"I've had enough of a break now, so I'm ready to help you with more crazy stun— I mean, experiments! What's on the agenda for today? Will we be standing on our heads? Reading dirty limericks backward?"

"Note to self: it is possible the paladin girl has developed an addiction to participating in scientific experiments as a subject. I must study this phenomenon and include it as a separate entry in the Encyclopedia."
"Tell me, Regill, back when you were a regular soldier, did you get whipped a lot?"
"Just the right amount to make me a decent fighter."
"The only thing you Hellknights are good for is killing their own. How many Hellknights die in peacetime at the hands of their officers?"
"Peacetime? What is that?"
"To hear you Hellknights talk, it's like you think everywhere should be run like things are in Hell."
"Hell is the ideal we are striving for. Being similar to Cheliax would be an acceptable intermediate stage."
"Right, let's try again. In your order, you follow five deities, including Iomedae and Asmodeus, but you do not follow them in general, only the parts of their faith that you like most?"
"That is correct. It means that you and I are more alike than you would care to think, paladin — I recognize the Inheritor's many achievements and I salute them."
"I refuse to believe it — nobody can actually be that joyless! Have you ever laughed, even once?"
"I have. Four times, in fact."
"Oh Light of the Sword, Iomedae, forgive me my sins and do not leave me in the darkness."
"I am weak and undeserving of your grace, and still you grant it to me. And that means I still have something to hope for."
"Hey-ho the derry-o... With his cheeks aflame and his trews down low..."
"Ugh! I can't get that tune out of my head! Damn tavern songs!"
"My sword is an extension of my arm, my sword is an extension of my arm..."
"So, is my plumage an extension of my head? Focus, Seelah..."
"If I lose my sword, I have lost a tool. If I betray my heart, I have died."
"The words of our code never fail to amaze me. It's like I always knew them in my heart, long before I found my faith in Iomedae."
"I will guard the honor of my fellows, both thought and deed, and I will have faith in them."

"The code is simple, really, but it is faith in one's fellows that is most frequently tested. Things would be a lot simpler if I could just cut down demons, without having doubts or thinking about anything at all."
"I haven't made a confession for a long time. Of course, we have different goddesses, but still.... Could you listen to my confession?"
"Of course. Let's go somewhere we won't be overheard."
"So many years wasted, so many good people perished... And there's still no end to this war."
"Praise the Goddess, we'll end it. Once and for all."
"I'm always surprised to see a follower of Shelyn on the battlefield — a place where there is no beauty or peace."
"Shelyn has been forced to raise a blade against her brother. She knows better than anyone the importance of sacrifice."

"What do you do when it looks like everything's going to hell in a handbasket and prayers aren't helping? I take myself off somewhere quiet and just hack and slash with my sword until I can't stand anymore!"
"I know the feeling. When I need to clear my thoughts, it is not a sword I reach for, but a brush."
"You made me look gorgeous. Somebody in Drezen said some paladin of Shelyn wanted to meet me. He'll be disappointed if he ever does!"
"I do not think he would be disappointed. Not at all."
"I know people who can't ever go back to 'normal' after fighting — they think there are demons everywhere."
"Maybe they are right. I know I can never drop my guard."
"I have a weird question to ask you, Trever. Which would you undo if you could — being held captive by the demons, or becoming a Hellknight?"
"You want to know what is more terrifying — evil that's done to you, or evil you do to others? I don't have an answer to that. I'm in no place to make that call."
"Tell me about your homeland, Ulbrig. What was Sarkoris like? Beautiful, I bet?"
"Stunning. Forests and fields, and rivers, and everything in bloom... When we win, you'll see for yourself."
"I know why you want to become stronger. You were scared of your weakness and helplessness as a child and you vowed to eliminate it. You're still being driven by this childhood fear."
"The only thing I feared as a child was dying of hunger in a damp cave, without ever achieving anything. I had to become better to survive."
"You look at me like you want to eat me. Take it easy — food's almost ready."
"Don't worry, paladin, I'd never eat you. I might take a bite out of you, though..."
"Do you think talking about how strong you are all the time makes you strong? It doesn't. It just shows that you constantly need to remind yourself."
"Maybe I say it to remind you of that fact, to get you to stop acting like you're smarter than me? Draw your sword!"
"I stay out of your way, and you stay out of mine. If we do that, we'll get along just fine. Agreed?"
"Keep away from me. We don't have to touch hands — that's for weaklings. If you have a problem with me, grab your sword and try to get rid of me. I can tell you want to, so come on!"
"Stop staring at me all the time. It's creepy, you know?"
"If you want me to obey — make me. Or are you afraid I'll beat you and you'll have to do what I say?"
"Running from the law, cutting purses, breaking into other peoples' houses... Is that really all you want out of life?"
"Oh sister, I remember a priest of Iomedae asking me the exact same thing when I was about ten or so, using the exact same words. Do you guys have a script you have to follow or somethin'?"
"You're not bad at spellcasting. Where did you study?"
"Here and there... but I'd give up all my lessons to be able to drink the way you do and not end up under the table."
"You'd like Solku. Caravans, traders from all over Golarion, the city's always noisy, with people speaking in a dozen different languages..."
"And you traded it all in for some armor and the Worldwound? You paladin types are an odd bunch, and no mistake."
"Do you know why you have no stamina? Because as soon as we stop anywhere, instead of helping to set up camp, you just drop like a rock."
"Nah, I drop like a rock because I've got no stamina!"
"Maybe if you stopped careening around like a runaway cart, and just sat down and thought about things, you'd figure out how to change your life."
"I've already done a stretch behind bars, thank you very much! I'm not going to sit around thinkin' while I'm free. I reckon I've earned myself five years of no thinkin' at all!"
"Your spirit is exceptionally strong. You not only recognized your deeds, you tried to atone for them. That warrants respect."
"I always just want to abandon it all and run away, back to my old life. But that's not possible. I can only move forward."
"If you wish to convert to the church of Shelyn, it would bring the goddess and me great pleasure."
"Desna showed me the path out of the Abyss, and I cannot abandon her. But... you are the first person to say I would be welcome anywhere. Thank you."
"Have you thought about what you're going to do after the war?"
"Demons don't know what peace is. I am still trying to grasp the idea that evil and suffering can come to an end."
"I am glad to have met you, Arueshalae. For me, you are proof that miracles can happen even in the darkest times."
"I will try not to let you down. I promise."
"Even if you stray from the path of righteousness, you will have a long time to conquer yourself and find your way again."
"No. I know that once I step off this path, I can never come back."
"You are so gentle, so fragile. It pains me to see you in the carnage of battle."
"Yes, all this blood and pain is difficult to endure... But I'm willing to bear it for the sake of my friends."
"Your face was made to be painted."
"Thank you. But you know, I think internal beauty is the most important thing in a person."
"If you should ever wish to confess your sins, I will always be willing to listen."
"I don't suffer any woman to listen in on my private conversations with a man. Not even Shelyn."
"It is possible that... if you were a little more polite to people, they would treat you differently too."
"Do not take this the wrong way, but being polite does not seem to have helped you much. People simply do not appreciate good manners!"
"I can only hope the spirits' voices do not drown out the voice of faith within you."
"Let us not speak of personal matters like faith. Such discussions can drive a wedge between the best of friends, and I cannot bear the thought of falling out with you, Sosiel."
"I'm glad you are with us, Daeran. Not because you are a good person, but because these events might prompt you to consider things."
"I'm sorry, did you say something? I was distracted by your lips. You have a beautiful mouth, but all I ever hear from it is claptrap."
"It brings me much sorrow to see such a gifted and, I suppose, worthy person as yourself give so little thought to his deeds and life, Daeran. It is such... a waste."
"You spend too much time thinking about life. Whereas I'm busy living it."
"Though you are a... complicated person, Daeran, I do respect you for your healing talent. Anyone who eases another's suffering cannot be entirely hopeless."
"You may want to recall the circumstances in which I received my healer's gift. Here's a hint — it wasn't of my own choosing. I would have rather avoided that episode in my life."
"I am almost inured to your blasphemous jokes by now. I understand you are just teasing me."
"Are you quite sure about that? You do not wish to retract that statement? Because once I change my target from the gods to your pious self, it will be too late."
"What did that look mean, Daeran?"
"It meant: 'nice sketch, I quite like it.' Yes, would you believe it, I am capable of not spitting poison every time I open my mouth. I am actually quite well disposed toward works of art, in fact."
"You are a child. You don't belong in this war."
"So you're an adult? War doesn't pick and choose its victims."
"Do your scars hurt? Maybe I can help with a spell or some medicine..."
"What can be healed, doesn't hurt. And what hurts, no one can heal."
"You've carried such suffering around your whole life. I think if you opened your heart to a kind deity, you would feel better."
"Really? You think I'd feel better if I had to care about what a deity wants me to do? Would my pack be lighter if I carried a horse?"
"You need to take better care of yourself, Ember."
"But then I'll be less able to take care of other people."
"Ember, I noticed your hair keeps getting in your eyes... This is just a little thing, something I whittled when we stopped on the journey... I hope they will help you."
"They're hair sticks... the kind real ladies have! But can I wear them even though I'm not a lady? Can I, Sosiel?"

"Listen, Ember... I respect your passion for making the world a better place, but some of your ideas are... too radical. Particularly the way you try to turn people away from worshiping the good deities."
"I simply say what is true. Are you upset that people are listening to me? Please, don't be upset!"
"It's difficult for me to believe that you are the same Arueshalae I knew before..."
"Why is it difficult to believe? Is it because you failed to see my true face, that you behaved like a naive, gullible fool?"
"You have gone astray, Arueshalae. But I will pray for your soul."
"Why don't I pray to the lords of the Abyss for your soul, sweet Sosiel? You are caught in a spider's web of foolish ideas and taboos. Perhaps I can free you from it all?"
"Have you ever considered confessing your sins to someone? It may ease your burden."

"If I did decide to make a confession — which will never happen, by the way — I'd pick an old military chaplain for the job, somebody who knows what I'm talking about. Not a young lad whose worst sin is sleeping through morning prayers."
"You must have seen and done many horrific things in your line of work. You have my sympathy. I'm sure your dreams are haunted by the dead."
