"No, actually, I sleep like a baby. Nightmares, fits of conscience, and all that — that's for amateurs. A professional has got to be able to do the job without taking it to heart."
"How about some tea, Greybor?"
"Hold on, did you just offer me some tea? Without forcing me to listen to a three-hour sermon on my wayward life? You're learning, lad. Of course I'll have some."
"In your place, I would pray more fervently than anyone, for how else could you atone for your crimes?"
"I pray regularly. To Norgorber, it's true, to ensure that he looks favorably upon me and helps me kill another couple of people."
"If you ever need to talk to someone, just know that I am always here."
"I don't know what we would even talk about. The price of wine and grapes?"
"I know you've been through a lot. If you ever need to talk, to relieve your soul..."
"If I need to relieve myself, I'll find some bushes. No need to help."
"I'm sorry about what happened to you..."
"What happened? What are you talking about? Oh, right — I was born a monster! Thanks for reminding me!"
"I'd like to show you a sketch. Tell me what you think."
"It's not bad, but if you ask me, I think you've made it too flattering. It's too bad you can't redraw my ugly mug for real to make me look like this handsome guy."
"Talking to you confuses me sometimes. It seems like every word out of my mouth offends you."
"How about this for a great idea, then: maybe you should just stop talking?"
"I would like to bring you to a temple of Shelyn one day, to make you understand that we accept everyone."
"Do you think after I'm chased out of the temple by glaive-wielding clerics, we'll just laugh it off as a misunderstanding and go and drink some tea?"

"Family is sacred. Your family are the people who are closest to you. Life has its ups and downs, loved ones argue and part ways, but they never forget one another. I'll never understand how could you forget your family, Nenio!"
"Are there people of historical significance among your ancestors? Did your forebears invent something great? Then I don't understand why you remember them."
"Nenio, your experiments are dangerous — for you most of all. You need to be more careful. I won't always be at hand to help."
"Science demands sacrifice! And because of you, boy, we failed to learn an individual's chances of survival after falling under the wheels of a cart rolling down an inclined plane."
"Don't you realize how dangerous it was to jump off that cliff? You could have been killed!"
"But how else would we have learned whether the amulet of levitation sold to me by that malodorous boy wearing the false beard in that alley was authentic?"
"Have you considered that some of your experiments could have hurt other people? Not everyone is willing to sacrifice themselves for science."
"Apologies, cleric boy, what did you just ask me? I wasn't listening — I was busy mixing experimental acids in the communal cooking pot!"
"You remember nothing... but what if you have a family waiting for you somewhere, or someone you need to take care of?"
"Observation no. 250: the cleric boy is once again demonstrating typical projection of his anxieties onto others. It would appear to be a defense mechanism. I will continue to observe."
"Hellknights have no dignity. You're just slaves, happy to serve your masters."
"Dignity is the ability to perform your duty in your assigned place. And it doesn't matter if it's the place of a slave or a ruler."
"You don't value the lives of your soldiers at all. You'd send a fighter to certain death without a second thought!"
"Your job is to heal, not give advice. I hope I don't live to see the day I take lessons from winemakers, tavern keepers, and tailors."
"I never thought I'd find myself fighting shoulder to shoulder with a Hellknight. To be honest, I'd avoid it if I could."
"You lack foresight. A skilled healer and a skilled fighter is an effective combination."
"Some people use times of war as an excuse for cruelty. But you Hellknights are just as cruel in peacetime. It is horrifying."
"It seems horrifying right up until the moment when you need to ask us for protection. Then all our methods are met with approval."
"I am certain Cheliax is not a lost cause. Despite everything, some people there pray to the good deities. That means that one day light will dispel the darkness."
"Calling things you find unpleasant or in conflict with your beliefs 'darkness' is a cheap rhetorical device. And one widely used by clerics who think themselves especially righteous."
"Those who perished in Kenabres... I still dream about them. Sometimes I see their faces in a crowd. Tell me... This will never be over, will it?"
"No. The ones we lost... They'll be with us forever."
"I saw a knight... A young woman, younger than me. But gray-haired, and with a fixed gaze... And I realized: she's not going to return from this war. Even if she survives."
"Neither are we, Sosiel. Not you. Not me. But at least we'll be able to put an end to this war, so no one else will have to go through this."
"I'm sure Acemi would have been proud of you."
"Don't speak for the long departed. I've done a lot of things that Acemi would not give me a pat on the head for."
"To be honest, I never thought I could have fun and feel so at ease with a paladin of Iomedae. The ones I've met before were very severe..."
"And I never thought I'd see a cleric of Shelyn on this crusade willing to risk everything. The goddesses brought us together for a reason — they wanted to rid us of our prejudices."
"It makes my heart sing to see that ordinary life goes on even on the crusade: people are enjoying themselves, making friends, falling in love, getting married..."
"Somebody may laugh at all this and say those people just think they're going to live forever. But I think that's the very reason why people are stronger in spirit than they seem."
"Must be nice back home now. I bet my niece is growing so big..."
"My family, I miss all of them so much!"
"Brother, where are you? What if you bravely fought here, right where I'm walking?"
"Or what if I passed your grave and never noticed? No, no... That can't be true!"
"Sometimes I'm afraid that Trever's face is slipping away in my memories."
"But my hands, my artist's hands, they remember."
"This land has suffered so terribly under the demons..."
"I will try to paint it as it was before the invasion. Beautiful, the way it will be again after we win."
"I can't help asking myself if I am in the right place in this war? Perhaps I should have just stayed among those peaceful vineyards and smiling peasants?"
"Am I truly needed here? Or is my naivety merely a hindrance to others? Questions, questions..."
"I can't believe it... We're sitting around a campfire together again like we used to. At long last."
"Except you're not a kid anymore. And I'm not someone you idolize. We're equals now."
"I'll never leave you again. I'll stay with you no matter what."
"No. You have your own life. Make more of yours than I did mine."
"I see that you are carrying a great burden. Pain, loss, guilt... If you wish to ease your soul, I am here to help, always."
"Ha. Lad, if I laid even a quarter of my burden on your dainty shoulders, you'd be crushed."
"What are you going to do when the crusade is over? Have you thought about living a peaceful life?"
"A peaceful life? The thought makes me sick. But there are always wars going on up here on the surface, so I won't miss the crusade for long."
"There is unique beauty in you. If only your features weren't eternally set in that harsh expression..."
"Do you really think that, priest? Oh, woe is me, let me just go have a little cry in my tent."
"Could you please keep your distance when I am hearing confessions? Confession is a private sacrament."
"Ah, you want to use their secrets yourself? You're far more cunning than I gave you credit for, priest."
"Forgive me, but we have nothing to talk about. I cannot see how I could be of any help to you."

"Stop stalling and start your sermon already, the one about the beauty of the soul and love for your fellow man. I burst out laughing every time you get to the part where you say that all mortals are worthy of compassion!"
"You have joined a group of people who are on a righteous mission, Wenduag. But are you capable of committing to this path? I would like to think so."
"I have joined a group of strong people. If you want to talk about 'righteous missions,' save it for your prattling priest friends."
"You don't have to talk constantly to please people. When you are silent and lost in thought, your face sometimes takes on a most intriguing and appealing expression."
"That... that's gotta be the floweriest way to tell somebody to shut their trap."
"Shelyn teaches us to only draw our weapons against those who will never choose to surrender."
"Good to know! So I don't need to worry about paladins of Shelyn, since I'm always ready to surrender!"
"How beautiful is the unspoiled countryside that has escaped the taint of the Worldwound! It is only in these places that you start to appreciate the beauty of nature."

"Uh-huh, I see what you're gettin' at! I'm a city lad, me, and I just love seein' the sun gildin' the roofs, the glitter of the nightsoil as people empty their chamberpots out through the windows, the pigeons gnawin' on one of their dead pigeon pals... s'enough to bring a tear to your eye!"
"You've moved again. Please, just sit still for just one minute!"
"What, not even move my tail? No, no, I've changed my mind, I don't want you to draw me anymore!"
"The crusade is harsh, but for those cast aside by fate, it is a chance for a new life."
"'Cast aside by fate'... well, now! Has a better ring to it than 'dirty crook'!"
"Don't come any closer, demon. Any talk between us won't last long."
"I just wanted to say... I'm sorry for what happened to you. That's all."
"You want to change, is that it? It won't work! The burden of your sins will always weigh on you. Only death will wash them away."
"People have tried to kill me many times, but the goddess must want me to live. I won't let her blessing be for naught."
"Sosiel doesn't like being on his own. I'm glad he has a friend here."
"Sosiel is the only person who understands the desire to just trust someone and reveal everything that is in your heart..."
"A person can be freed from captivity. But changing what's taken root in your head... that's where the real prison is."
"That's not true for me at all! I was free the moment I stepped over the threshold, and I am not looking back."
"Soldiers in the crusade are shedding their blood to give you a peaceful life in Kenabres. Show some respect!"
"Of late it is I who has been shedding both blood and sweat, heroically crusading for my homeland both in the Worldwound and even in the Abyss. Where is your respect for that, Trever, hmm?"
"Do you think my brother's faith is funny? It is his life."
"Incorrect: it is what is walling Sosiel off from life. Oh, I would hate to be nearby when his dark night of the soul comes. It will be a pitiful spectacle! But an enlightening one."
"Keep away from me in battle, little one. I could hurt you by accident."
"I know you'll never hurt me. Even by accident."
"You should come and visit us. Our family will fatten you up. A child should never be allowed to go hungry, all skin and bone."
"You should be with them, everything is good there. But my place is here, where everything is bad for everyone."
"I'll kill you if you come any closer."
"The rabid dog barks... but I know you're afraid. I can smell it on you!"
"Stay back. We have nothing to talk about."
"Trever, Trever, look at me... Don't I look like your sweet Marenta? Close your eyes and I'll reunite you with her..."
"If you can return to your family, to your home — do it."
"Home isn't a place, it's people who are waiting for you. No one's been waiting for me for a long time."
"So the demons paid you, and you served them. How are you any better than a cultist? Why shouldn't I kill you on the spot?"
"I didn't serve anyone, I did my job. There's a world of difference between the two."
"You're a good kid. Honest. Loyal. Not many like you these days."
"It seems like honesty and loyalty grow well in the cold, dark conditions typically found in caves."
"Don't talk yourself down. Girls don't just go after pretty boys."
"Nobody mistakes me for a demon in dim lighting anymore. That's one thing. But girls... that's still a work in progress. Slow progress."
"You don't even notice danger. You walk headlong into everything."

"There are no situations where danger is entirely null. For instance, there is a one-thousandth of a percent chance that tomorrow you will not wake up. It sounds like a threat. But it is actually only a fact."
"Don't come near me with your book. I don't want to talk about what happened. And I'm not a test subject."
"The subject's capacity for socialization and communication has suffered somewhat after the trials he has endured. The 'polite' phase has ended, now we move on to the next phase — 'provocation'!"
"I've heard of you, Paralictor Derenge. Some good, some bad."
"And I have heard plenty about you, Trever Vaenic, while traveling with your brother..."
"Will you tell me how my Marenta died?"
"She died with honor. Like a true Hellknight. Like a soldier. Like you should have — but failed — to do."
"Don't think I don't approve of you if I turn away, Seelah. It's not that. It's private."
"I think I can guess. You're remembering being a paladin? I'm not going to condemn you, just so you know."
"I can never become like you again, a paladin. Only sometimes I dream of... no. It's stupid."
"If you stopped being a paladin, that doesn't mean you became a worse person. You just had a different path."
"The crusade has toughened you up. Could you have hauled a big trunk like that before, little brother?"
"I probably would have let you carry it without even thinking. But I've grown up, and now I carry my own weight, physically and spiritually."
"You don't deserve any of this. You deserve to be happy."
"I am happy because you are with me, against all odds."
"No... no... Not again... I won't do it..."
"That dream again..."
"I've forgotten how to pray."
"But I know my brother is praying for me."
"Demons destroyed your homeland. How are you not burning with the thirst for vengeance?"
"He who burns turns to ash as well. If I catch those wretches, I'll kill 'em, of course. But if I don't, well, I've plenty of other things to do."
"You were given the chance to live a decent life. But you are acting like a feral beast."
"Yes, I am a beast. What are you? The big, bad warrior who had to be pulled out of trouble by his pathetic little brother?"
"You betray people and you're proud of it... What kind of creature are you?"

"My treachery serves a purpose, and I always know what I want. What about you? You threw your lot in with the clerics of a pathetic goddess, then with the knights in black armor, then with the demons. And it seems to me you did all that because you're weak, not because you saw an advantage in it!"
"Every time I think I can understand you and forgive you, you open your mouth again."
"I need your forgiveness like a mutt needs a fifth leg, pal! But it's not like there's much sense outta you except for mumblin' and grumblin'!"
"Don't come near me, tiefling. You stink of demon."
"What? That's my exotic and fancy cologne! Picked it up at the market, it was on tap."
"You said your name was Arueshalae, is that right? There, I've written it on my amulet. Now your bewitchery is no threat to me!"
"An amulet like that, unfortunately, won't be any help... But I wasn't planning on bewitching you, in any case!"
"I've never heard of a spirit like yours. Will you tell me about it?"
"Druids have their secrets, and shamans have theirs. Nature in its wisdom divided these two callings — so it is best we not share our knowledge."
"Is milord's high-born backside too good to get up and do something useful?"
"I'll have you know, grunt work is just as beneath the dignity of your lord's other high-born body parts."

"I'd lock you up under guard... for your own good. You're just a child, and a simple-minded one at that — war's no place for you! You'll hurt yourself, and you'll bring others to ruin along with you."
"Thank you for caring about me! I'm going to be fine — Soot won't let anything happen to me. And I'm not going to hurt other people. Not at all. I'm going to heal them."
"Tell me this: what do you live for? Surely not money alone?"
"First, you tell me: what did you wake up for this morning? Surely not to lecture me?"
"You're a tough bunch, you mongrels. We survived by the skin of our teeth, and we lived among rich fields and forests full of game. How did you manage down there underground?"
"Little by little. Mushrooms, giant centipedes... But life underground has its upsides: at least you don't ever have to worry about snow, or rain, or hurricanes."
"D'you know what we used to do with witches like you? Lock 'em up in Threshold and throw away the key."
"I wonder, do you perceive a logical connection between this deplorable custom and the subsequent demise of the country in which it was practiced?"
"A strong fighting force should be like a family, standing by each other through thick and thin. But family members don't just thrash each other for nothing!"
"Our force exterminates demons with great efficiency. Your families are gone, leaving not even ashes behind. You are in no position to instruct me in the waging of war."
"...and then I carried two full barrels of mead out of the fire on these two shoulders!"
"Too bad I wasn't there. We could have made it four barrels!"
"You were a vintner before, so I hear? You'd have been better off sticking to making sweet-tasting wine instead of poking around in people's souls."
"I tried to stay home — it was a lost cause. My conscience would not allow me to pour grape juice while others poured blood."
"Being held prisoner by the fey... must have been tough, I'll bet? I heard a story about 'em, that—"
"No stories. Not about fey. Not about anything. Better not to talk."
"Oof, stopping at last. I'm weary after today!"
"For a hundred years, all I did was sleep, and now after one day's running around, I fancy another nap."
"A clan is the only true strength there is. In a clan, everyone stands together. But what you have is no clan — it's a pack."
"Well, where is this mighty clan of yours? What about that pile of dust over there — any relation?"
"Are you telling me that you're half-oglin? Fate has played a nasty trick on you, lad."
"That's what I tell 'em! 'I'm a poor, unfortunate tiefling. For the love of Iomedae, gimme some money!' But they don't!"
"You are a powerful demon... I can sense your strength in your very movements! Oh, how sweet it would be to fight you!"
"I don't want to fight anyone in our party. I don't want to injure the people who have given me their trust."
"Tell me about the Abyss. I have heard that only demons can make their way to the top there."
"Sometimes, having the heart of a demon is enough. But that seems to be the case for finding success in Golarion too."
"I want to drink life in a single swallow, just like you. Teach me, and I will... feed you."
"Please, leave. Even if I knew how to turn you into a demon, I would never do it."
"Your belief in Desna makes you weaker, not stronger. What use is it to you?"
"You are wrong. The goddess gives me the strength to restrain my most formidable enemy — myself."
"Why do you hate your past so much? You had power, strength, status, mortal puppets at your command — what else could you want?"
"It was all an illusion. And in the end, I realized how hollow it was."
"Do you think you're better than me because you're from a noble line? You were raised in captivity, but I grew up free, able to do what I wanted!"

"Oh yes, you were able to sleep on cold rock, and now you fancied a change to this one. I, on the other hand, sadly had to endure sleeping on a bed the size of your entire encampment... I must say, your undisguised envy is really quite charming!"
"You're so sure that your beauty and softly spoken ways will always save you? The day will come when they are not enough."
"But when that day comes, the spirits of Sarkoris will come to my aid."
"So uplanders value money so much that you can even buy their respect with enough coins? And if someone takes all your money, you lose all that respect?"
"Respect? You can buy yourself love with enough coin. But not for a hideous beast like you — there's no price high enough for that."
"Rich little uplander, if you spent as long in the caves as I have, you would—"
"This endless fuss of how terribly mongrels suffer, how hard their lives are! Do you not have anything else to talk about, you tedious savage?"
"Your cooking's so terrible it even turns my stomach. And I'm used to eating mold and rats!"
"Where is your vaunted mongrel tenacity now, you beast? Just suffer this new trial — suffering is all your life has prepared you for, after all, isn't that right?"
"You live for pleasure... Come to me, golden boy, and you will be like putty in my hands and never desire another..."
"You haven't named the price of this temptation, but I suspect it's too high, even for me."
"Gods are weak, golden boy. The power they give is nothing compared to the power that demons can offer! Why do you not join them?"
"Who told you that power is what I'm after? And besides, have you seen what they do to cultists? In exchange for power, they are forced to... work! No, no no... no power in the cosmos is worth that!"
"Healthy, strong, celestial blood... There are few uplanders with whom I would be willing to breed. But you, golden boy, are on my list."
"'Breed'! You have a preternatural talent for killing off the smallest spark of desire in a man!"
"It's a pity you didn't come across us in Neathholm. I would not have let you out of the Maze so easily."
"And I would have sat underground, raising our tiny little monsters and waiting for you to bring back our supper of rats? What a frightfully perfect scene! Or a perfectly frightful one..."
"Even aasimars are no match for neathers when it comes to strength! You can produce beautiful, healthy offspring, that is your one advantage over us."
"How about this for an advantage — I shall still be capable of doing the deed that produces offspring some twenty years after you have withered from decrepitude!"
"Why do you shy away from me, golden boy? Are you afraid? Do I disgust you?"

"Do you wish me to answer honestly? I am disgusted, but not by your appearance. I find beauty and appeal in many things my countrymen would consider monstrous. No, what truly repulses me is your servility."
"Now that is clever — pretending to be an innocent child so that others lower their guard."
"I'm not pretending to be anything. But are you?"
"People call you a freak. I don't know what that's like — I was the most desirable woman in my tribe. But I do know what it's like to have to hide your rage. You don't have to pretend with me."
"They call me a freak, but they're really just scared because I'm different. How can I be angry at people who are scared?"
"What, are you planning to spend your whole immortal life living as a beggar? You could win riches, power!"
"A small amount of riches... that would be nice. I'd give it away to my friends from the River City. They could use it to build new homes after the fire."
"You managed to survive alone on the city's streets. That's like how I have lived, in some ways. You need to forge your own path!"
"But you're not on your own anymore, and you don't have to forge your path alone."
"You are the strangest out of all of us, girl. I don't know how you managed to survive this long, but I will discover your secret."
"You said, 'all of us'! So you have found friends after all."
"Other people called you beautiful before, but how can a bleating lamb be beautiful? Now you've lost that foolish meekness, you are much more beautiful!"
"Although the guise of a sweet little lamb proved highly effective at charming mortals. I am certain I will use it again and again!"
"I like your wings. In the caves they would be useless, but on the surface they give you an advantage as a warrior and a hunter."
"They give me an advantage in many other ways too. Or, at least... they open up new possibilities."
"You kill differently to the hunters of our tribe, dwarf. Teach me a few of your techniques!"
"I would, but you're one of those students who takes their final exam by slitting the teacher's throat."
"Bounty hunting... I think I could do well in that."
"To succeed, you need to develop at least a minimum level of trust. Keep your word. Is that something you're capable of? I doubt it."
"People stay at public inns, sleeping among strangers, unarmed... Don't they know what easy prey they make?"
"That's a good thing. It makes my job much simpler."
"Why do you need to earn so much gold? Can't you just take what you want by force?"

"That's not how things are done on the surface. We don't kill a tavern keeper if we want a drink. We kill some scoundrel, get paid a nice sum for it, and then make friendly conversation with the tavern keeper about the weather while sipping our pint of stout."
"The surface is a huge hunting ground. And it will all be mine!"
"I've heard that before. Those are the words of ambitious dictators who build whole empires out of nothing... but they're also the words of petty hustlers who end their days in the hangman's noose."
"Still hate me, Lann?"
"No more than anybody else in our party does. Well, there's one difference: you don't make the rest of them want to throw up."
"Now, Lann... we could slip away together, like we used to. Who wants you here, apart from me? The other women are afraid of you."
"Sweet as ever, Wendu, but I'd cut my hand off before I'd touch you."
"My father was always so kind to you, Lann. What would he say, to hear you speak to me like that?"
"What would he say if he knew you'd betrayed your own tribe? I think he'd find that more upsetting."
"Pass the salt, Lann."
"Piss off."
"Anger suits you better than silly jokes, Lann. Beast on the outside, beast on the inside... Isn't that what they call harmony?"
"You want me to become the same as you? No thanks."
"Hey, you, freak! My name is Wenduag! Wenduag! Remember my name — soon the whole world will know it!"
"When that happens, that's when I'll remember it too, mongrel girl."
"Hey, freak! You know a lot about everything. What method of torture is the simplest but also the most painful?"

"Of the methods that can be performed in field conditions — crushing fingers with a rock, and branding with a piece of wood from the campfire. I also found eating hot coals to be especially unpleasant. Alas, building a sufficient base for comparison is a grueling but necessary task."
"Your so-called work is pure nonsense! Who in the world needs these books?"
"You might change your opinion, mongrel girl, if you learned to read. But until then... you are right, they are useless to you."
"Hey, you! Want to learn something interesting? Neathers sleep like bats in their caves: they grab onto the ceiling and hang upside down."

"This is incredibly valuable information, mongrel girl. The next time we make camp in a cave, you must give me a demonstration. And if we do not find a cave, I will come to your chambers in Drezen, there is a ceiling there that is wholly suitable for experiments!"
"So, you're not a human, you're a kitsune! Ha, you deceived everyone. Well played!"

"According to the definitions I have gathered, 'deception' is the deliberate dissemination of false information with the aim of misleading one's interlocutor. I never knowingly misled anyone about my nature, and what's more — I could not have done so, given my ignorance of it. What conclusion does this bring us to? I did not deceive anyone!"
"What's the point of being a member of an order whose masters are far from here when you could simply set out on your own and deal with enemies however you want?"
"An order is a powerful alliance. It does not offer absolute freedom, it offers a purpose."
"If I joined your order, what would I get? Power? Gold? The best weapons?"
"It is possible that some in the party are worthy of admission to the order, but I would not let you within a mile of it."
"You always want to show me that you are better, stronger. Why? Am I not a superb fighter?"
"As a fighter, you are passable, but that is not enough to warrant my respect."
"You voluntarily torture yourself? You uplanders really have it too good! No one in Neathholm would do such a stupid thing! Pain finds us on its own."
"Of course such a 'stupid thing' is not done in Neathholm. If it were, I would now be speaking to a disciplined warrior, and not a fickle traitor."
"Ha, I thought gnomes were silly little moles who only knew how to enjoy themselves. I didn't know there were any worthwhile people among them."
"Your ignorance of surface people is telling."
"Don't you trust me, paladin? Are you wondering how to bring my wayward soul into the fold?"
"I'm thinking about who I would have become if I'd made the wrong choice a long time ago."

"Come on, paladin, let's see how you do against me. I want to see what you're like when you're up against a decent opponent! I want to feel the strength of our hands, to see the fire in your eyes, to see the moment when your rage takes over! It will be a good fight, I promise."
"It sounds like you're asking me out on a date."
"What do you get out of being a paladin, then? Is all that tedious praising and praying worth it? Claiming your freedom scares you, because you don't know if you'll go back to your old way of life!"
"Being a paladin gives me a purpose and my soul peace. I doubt you'll ever understand what that's like."
"You seem awfully tense when I'm around. Is that fear?"
"I'm tense because, like any normal person, I don't like it when someone looks at me like I'm a piece of meat."
"You scorn me because I bow down before the strong? But you bow down before a mighty goddess, you pray to her and beg her for mercy. Hypocrite."

"I will try to explain in language you'll understand. The same substance can be both a poison and a medicine, right? How would you react to someone who secretly slips some into your drink? And how about if they offer it to you openly when you're sick?"
"You're always muttering away at your prayers... Why doesn't your goddess make you do something more practical in exchange for her power?"
"Hm... Painting could also be seen as service to my goddess. Is that practical enough for you?"
"People come to you willingly and tell you their secrets? Who are these idiots?"
"But I swore a vow never to reveal their secrets to anyone else... Oh, I forgot, you don't understand the meaning of the word 'vow.'"
"Why are you still clinging to false hope? Your brother is long gone, nobody is going to find him. Don't be pathetic — accept it!"
"I have faith that I will find him, but I'm not forcing anyone to follow my example. This is my burden alone, you don't need to concern yourself with it."
"Why do you serve the goddess of beauty? Beauty is useless. You would be better off serving the god of war or power."
"Strength does not only lie in cruelty and inflicting pain. When you find yourself stopped in your tracks by something beautiful, or you weep at a piece of music, you will understand."
"Sosiel the do-gooder! You're so desperate for people to like you, you'll tie yourself in knots just to help!"
"It's not possible to have everyone like you. But helping even those who do not like you — that is the work of a cleric."
"How humiliating — proud crusader to demons' plaything. Tell me, did you feel like you had been used?"
"At first, I felt hatred. Then despair. But by the end, I felt nothing at all."
"I thought you would be stronger than your milksop of a brother. But underneath all those muscles, you are just as soft as Sosiel."
"For me, that is not an insult, but the highest praise."
"You're just like our chief, Sull. Only he spent years trying to destroy his tribe in his old age, but you succeeded in your youth."
"You are nothing like any member of my tribe. Except for perhaps that one hound that went rabid and had to be put down."
"Strength gives the right to life."
"If you're weak, sooner or later you will become prey."
"People who sit around hoping they'll be saved are pathetic fools!"
"And when we should be off killing demons, instead we have to go and save their useless hides!"
"Demons are far harsher and more ruthless than uplanders, that's why they're on top."
"And if the crusaders want to survive, they're going to have to learn how to be ruthless very fast."
"A world with no walls... a sky with no ceiling..."
"I liked it better in the caves, where I knew every twist and turn, and every place to expect prey or an ambush."
"I should thank Deskari — he shook up this drowsy world when he attacked Kenabres, and he changed so many destinies, including my own."
"Yes, when we kill the wretch, I will say, 'Thank you,' to his mutilated corpse."
"You have the blood of a demon in you! A powerful demon, too, since you're skilled in magic. You can share some of your power with me! I will get the demon seed, and you'll get a good time."
"Uh... you're all right, love! Thanks, but no thanks! I'm actually celibate, me! Took a vow of chastity. I'd show you my chastity belt, but well, wouldn't want to tempt you!"
"Why are you going around telling everyone I look like a spider, you horn-headed lowlife?"
"I never said you 'looked' like a spider, I said you are a spider! A nasty, carnivorous spider! Ow! That hurts!"
"Your ancestors were so weak-willed that they let demons use them. You are the proof of their disgrace."
"Not my ancestors — my old gran, it was. She got up to some wild stuff in her day, and I'm one of the less disgraceful episodes!"
"Put that knife away. If you try to stab me, boy, I'll rip off your tail strangle you with it."
"I just wanted to peel an apple! Do you ever relax?"
"You're weak! Do you know what the demons will do to you if you don't become stronger?"
"I can't do push-ups with you sittin' on my back! Well, actually, I can't do 'em at all..."

"See, I look at you and I think... maybe my old granddaddy was an incubus? Some distant relation of yours. Both our horns are similar enough, we both have dark hair, you're a succubus and I'm also as handsome as they come!"
"You're looking for similarities with demons, but I like that you look more like a human than one of us."

"And so I'm trying to get away from the guard and I come across this door, so I run in... and inside are all the thieflings! They're all pointin' at me and fallin' about laughin'. So I look down... and I've got no pants on! Well? D'you still think mortal dreams are wondrous, magical things?"

"How could I not? Without even being aware of it, you created an entire story that reflected your fears, you built a whole world that prompted you to wake up when it faded away. Only mortals are capable of such magic!"

"I still can't wrap me head around it. You can kill someone with a single pucker of the lips, you could make a big name for yourself in the Abyss easily — but you swapped it all for some dreams and so you could have a chinwag with mortal folk! Why? You're a demon! You've got power!"
"You're right. I do have power. For years and years, I was drunk on my power. It's only now that I understand how little I truly had compared to what mortals possess."
"If not for the wings, I could've set you up in the Family. Nobody would've suspected a thing!"
"I don't want to steal things. But calling someone family... that would be nice."
"I'll bet you've learned a ton of songs already, huh? Or whatever Desna likes folk to do... Give us a song, will ya?"
"I... I mean... I'm still not comfortable singing on demand like that."
"Hey, Lady Muck, you eat the last crispy wing every single time! Every time! I've seen you!"
"I eat precisely as much as is appropriate and necessary. Whereas your plebian gluttony is revolting."
"Tell me, your snootiness, that amulet of yours, medallion, whatever... is it worth a lot? I'm just askin' out of interest, y'know, makin' polite conversation."
"My amulet... is priceless. Unlike your head."
"Tell me this: how come you're so sure you're really talkin' to spirits, and not just hearin' voices in your head?"
"For the same reason I am certain that you are a lowly creature lacking in wit or decency: some things are simply self-evident."
"What would you have done in my shoes, if you'd had to survive on the streets? What, you wouldn't've took to thievin'? Yeah, right!"
"I would have survived one way or another. The spirits would have told me what to do."
"Let's say your ol' pops dies outta the blue, right? How're you gonna prove that you're his daughter, eh? Any guy off the street could show up and say he's a Gwerm, too!"
"Why are you so interested, I wonder? Are you planning some kind of scheme?"
"So you're the fella, I mean, the gentleman, who threw the party on the boats? Ha! I remember that! We had some fine fishin' that night!"

"If by that you mean that you thieflings plucked drunken aristocrats who had fallen overboard out of the water and stripped them of everything but their fillings, then I should think that was closer to seal hunting than fishing."
"Daeran, your excellency, sir, is it true what they say? That you're next in line for the throne? What'll be the first thing you do if you're crowned king?"

"I'd issue a law protecting tieflings from persecution, of course. I jest. I would have all the fountains in the land filled with wine instead of water. Don't make that face at me, I know you tieflings will enjoy that little edict too."
"Hand on heart, the first time I saw you face to face, I thought you were like all the other snobs who won't even spare two words for people lower than them. But you're all right."
"Of course I mix freely with the lower classes. It is the simplest way to enrage the stuffy gatekeepers of high society!"

"Being an aasimar, huh. Nice life if you can get it! People love 'em, people always think nice things about aasimars, about beauty and Heaven and other good things! Tieflings, well, that's another story."
"When people look at tieflings, they think of the sweetness of sin. When they look at thieflings, however, they wonder where their coin purse is."
"You love tellin' folk about your mad capers. Come on, then, what's the weirdest thing that's ever happened to you!"

"I shan't go into details, suffice it to say it involved a spinning wheel, a bear skin, the vanes from a windmill, a scroll of levitation, a wand of animate object, a bucket of blue paint, and some aromatic candles."

"You're always harpin' on about how everythin's terrible and the sufferin's only just started and all that... so why are you always smilin'? I don't want my sufferin' to start! I'd actually prefer it if I suffered as little as possible, thanks very much!"
"But what you want and how things are — they're two different things, right? Let's not wish for anything and just enjoy what we have now."
"You lived on the streets and you never once stole nothin'? Like, nothin' nothin'? Not even an apple? Get outta here!"
"But it's the truth. Why would I steal when kind people are so willing to share what they have?"
"I don't want you to go round tellin' everybody you knew me when I was a kid. They'll all laugh at me."
"But won't they laugh at you anyway? I thought you acted silly on purpose because you liked making people laugh."
"I grew up... but you haven't changed a bit. That's creepy!"
"I'm not going to change either. I'll always be your friend. Even after you die."
"I can't be your friend anymore, you got that? I don't even know how to be friends with people... it's not my thing!"
"Nobody knows how to be friends at first. And then you find some friends and you learn. Want to try again?"
"I used to think that being weird like you meant being alone. But... lots of folk like you here."
"Let's be weird together! And then you'll never be alone."

"You're just as dumb as you've always been... but I'm not embarrassed to be seen talkin' to you anymore. Actually the opposite, I'm embarrassed I turned my back on you. And now I've got this weird ache inside."
"I'm happy it hurts, that means your heart that froze from loneliness is starting to thaw."
"Can you turn into a guy? All decked out in armor, a little taller than me. Dark hair, with a little gray, but young. And with a face, all aristocratic-like..."
"What do you think I am? A toy? Get lost!"
"I liked you better before. This place has enough monsters that wanna eat me already!"
"That's right... but I am the only monster who will do it with tenderness."
"Hey, Uncle Greybor, my old pal! If anybody ever hires you to kill me, you'll give me a heads-up, won't you? Y'know, sporting like."
"Don't worry, my young friend. If I'm hired to kill you, you'll be the first to know."

"Why d'you even bother doing the jobs you're hired for? Just take the money and go to ground for a while. And if you're found, just kill 'em all. You're a scary fella, you could handle it. If I was a bounty hunter, that's what I'd do!"
"Something tells me you won't die of natural causes, friend."
"I heard you abandoned your daughter just because the road was callin' you or some such tripe. You're not all that different to my dear ol' dad."
"Number one: shut your mouth. Number two: my daughter didn't grow up to be a thief. Maybe even because I wasn't in her life."
"So you're proud of your rep. But what if you're dyin' and the only way to save yourself is to ruin your reputation — what would you do?"
"Let myself die, or live hating myself and my cowardice — that's a difficult choice. But for me the answer is obvious — I would choose my self-respect."
"If you like teachin' me so much, why don't you open a home for little thieves? You could sit there smokin' your pipe, rockin' in your chair and lecturin' all the little crooks!"

"You're not a little thief anymore, you're a grown lad, so I doubt my lectures will work on you. I'm just trying to teach you a little dignity so you don't discredit us with your petty hustler habits."

"Fine, so you ate rats and moss and things like that. Well, once when there was nothin' else to eat, my ol' gran stole a rotten fish from the market and made a soup with it! Whaddaya make of that, eh?"
"You get that this isn't a competition, right?"
"I don't get you mongrels. Why sit underground waiting and waiting, when you can just go outside and get it over with?"
"The world just isn't ready for our kind of beauty yet. I'm the first emissary of the people who are going to make the aasimars look positively homely."
"How d'you know you don't got long to live? You look healthy enough to me."
"Ah, but that's because I'm secretly coughing into a lace handkerchief that's becoming stained with blood as my condition progresses."

"Brother Lann, you're a good guy and all, but you're a little rough around the edges. You've still got that 'cave' look about you. You don't know how to act, and your jokes ain't all that either. I can give you some lessons if you want? I'm always happy to help a pal."
"Sure I do. Just as soon as I finish reading this collection of essays on 'How to Travel in a Party with a Deadbeat Liar Without Killing Him.'"
"I get it, but how could anyone get involved with a half-cat, half-spider abomination who hates everybody? Or did you think you were special?"
"Wenduag wasn't always like that. Well, she pretended not to be. You should already know this — some people are capable of doing anything to survive."

"Nenio, you've got a fast pair of legs on you. That's real compliment, comin' from me. Sometimes even I struggle to keep up with you, and I was always one of the fastest runners back with the thieflings."
"Experiments facilitate the development of this skill."
"Nenio, have you ever tested to see how many times you can change into a kitsune and back in an hour? Whaddaya say we have ourselves a little experiment once we're back in Drezen?"

"That would be interesting! But this time you'll have to sit still and keep count. After my research into the consumption of rotten apples, some of the people tried to blame me for their coin purses going missing while they were watching the experiment."
"This is ridiculous! Gimme back my file for my horns! I already look like some kind of wild demon!"

"Tiefling boy, your horns should be put into the service of science. I will give you back your file once I have recorded the maximum length they grow to when they are not filed down every day. Not a moment before."
"Are you gonna get anything outta this book of yours? If you sell it, is there a chance you could get rich off of it?"
"I have never even thought about it, tiefling boy. I am generally of the opinion that knowledge should be free."
"You want to see my shadow again? Well, I dunno, it's gonna cost ya... I normally don't show it for anything less than twenty... Fine, since it's you, I'll do it for fifteen!"

"Excellent. I will observe it for half an hour. During that time, you will have to answer my questions, and as for the money... put it on my tab. I do not know what that expression means, but I hear it said in taverns very frequently."
"How does that little old gnome manage to be so titchy and so terrifying all at once? It's the eyes, the crazy eyes and the pasty skin..."
"And the excellent hearing. Speak clearly or stop mumbling!"
"How's it work then? You're Hellknights, but you don't bow down to devils? Nice setup you got there! But then what's this got to do with Hell? I don't get it..."
"We obey the order's code to create a world in which demon spawn don't run their mouths."

"D'ya know what I like, ol' Reggie? You know that all the talk about the crusades and good deeds and true friendship ain't worth nothin'. You don't try to deceive anyone. You're a rock, grandpa Reggie, unshakeable. You have my respect."
"Take your hands off my coin pouch and keep them where I can see them."
"You've got it all worked out: you go around in spiky armor lookin' mean, and then you can do whatever you want! That's the life!"
"Astonishing. You are even more stupid than I thought, thief."

"So you think nothin' gets past you? That you notice everything, huh? I bet you won't be able to guess which cup the pea is under. Just watch: I put it under the middle one, swap 'em round and round again..."
"The first pea is in your hand, the spare is behind your ear. Judging by the engraving, you stole the cups from the Silken Thread in Kenabres."

"Keep 'em peeled, paladin. Round and round and round we go, where it stops, nobody knows. No trick, no magic, just nimble fingers! Watch closely now, we don't want no hard feelings later, one, two, one more time, and hey presto! Well? Which cup is the pea under?"
"Seriously? Out of everybody in the party, you picked me? I learned the cups and balls trick before I could talk, you little punk! Now sit down and let sister Seelah show you how it's done!"

"You became a paladin because some lady didn't wear a helmet one time? I s'pose... fine, so, you stole her helm, but come on, they're paladins. They're rich. Don't tell me there wasn't a spare helmet lyin' around someplace. And what about armorers and all that...?"
"I'm this close to forgetting that paladin code I swore to uphold, hornhead. Take the hint, will you?"

"I know you're a paladin and all, but... just hear me out. We go into a tavern, you challenge the local champion to a drinking match, and I'll work my magic on the crowd to make them all bet on him. We'll split the takings fifty-fifty. How 'bout it?"
"Drinking is fun, not work. I can't take money for that."
"I had a messed-up childhood, but sometimes I think back on it fondly. Life was so easy!"
"You were smaller, so it was easier for you to cut purses and get away without being caught. Am I right? Don't tell me, I know I'm right."

"You had this funny look on your face back in Kenabres, when you were watchin' the poor little kids whose houses had been burnt to cinders. Were you missin' the days when you weren't weighed down with armor, back when you didn't take orders from nobody?"

"I do get sad sometimes when I see little kids and remember my childhood. Not because I miss the 'freedom' of running wild in the slums, but because I remember my life before then, before I became an orphan..."
"You're tellin' me you know my tricks? I bet you won't know this one: you take a regular purse with a few coins in it, drop it in the middle of the street, some idiot comes along and picks it up—"
"And then the 'real owner' runs over yelling about how he's been robbed. You really think you thieflings came up with everything, don't you?"
"You must've got slow since you've been in your order, not as nimble, wits ain't as sharp as they were when you were a thief, right? I bet you couldn't even beat me in a race."
"Running and turning tail are different things, Woljif. When it comes to the latter, you've got everybody beat!"

"You're always sayin' brother this, brother that... but it's just a word! Big deal, you both had the same mother — that makes no difference. He don't gotta love you, and you don't gotta chase after him all over the world!"
"I've never really thought of it as an obligation. Love comes from within, it either is or it isn't. Despite all its trials, I am glad to love my brother."
"The temple of Shelyn... no doubt that's where you stash all your pretty baubles, eh? So tell me, what d'you reckon the most valuable thing is that you'd find in temples of Shelyn and nowhere else?"
"Rose petal tea, of course."

"Hey, is it true that you Shelyn clerics go around lookin' for a pretty girl and start fallin' over yourselves to worship her? And if you bring the pretty girl back to the temple, you get paid cash? So here's the deal: we catch a succubus, bring it to the temple, and split the payout... Hang on, why are you laughing?"
"I'm not, I'm not... It's just, ahem, a cough..."

"I've got an idea! Why don't you do those portraits of yours for money? There's plenty of folk who'd want to send a picture back home to the family, why not turn it into a money-spinner for us? Whaddaya reckon?"

"Painting portraits of people who cannot afford such things in their ordinary lives... people who may never see home again but who want to leave something behind... That is a wonderful idea. But I could never accept money for it."

"Everybody keeps tellin' me to change. But I like the way I live! I ain't plannin' to change! Hear that, cleric? You wouldn't give up your Shelyn just 'cause somebody told you to, would you? Well, the same goes for me."
"But you are forever complaining about your life. How are people to know that you are truly happy with your lot?"
"You're a big fella, ain't ya? You should work as hired muscle! You'd be in high demand!"
"No. I want to return to the land. Grow grapes. I don't want to fight anyone ever again."
"The way Sosiel talked you up, I thought you gotta be like an angel from Heaven. But now you're here in the flesh... and you ain't no angel."
"Am I more like a demon, then? Don't be afraid. I can take the truth."
"Ulbrig, old buddy! I always dreamed of flying on a griffon. Will you gimme a ride?"
"I let you on my back and I'll be missing half my feathers by the end of it. Not a chance, lad, keep dreaming."
"I packed up your tent, I washed out your bowl... Do I look like a servant or summat? Don't think you can scare me! I ain't scared of you!"
"When you stop shaking like a leaf and get that tail of yours to lie still, maybe I'll believe you."
"Looks like it's just you and me, cherry roll, alone at last! I've had to hide you from everybody for so long, but now I can finally enj... hey!"
"Such a tasty treat you stashed away for me, runt. Today I'm going to act like you don't exist. You're welcome."
"How come you're always pickin' on me, eh? Am I the only whipping boy around here or somethin'?"
"I just like the way it sounds when you beg for mercy in that sweet little voice of yours."
"Ha ha, cave critter, why so glum? You break a nail or somethin'?"
"No, I haven't. And I've got claws, not nails. And I'll slash your throat open if you don't shut up!"
"I know why you dumped your underground pal, the goat-lizard guy. Because if you didn't, he'd have dumped you first. Who'd want a shrew like you!"
"Lann would never have had the sense to 'dump' anyone. He was straight as an arrow, loyal as a dog, and I strung him along because I wanted to."
"Pearls of wisdom from brother Woljif!"
"Thieving's as next to frugality, because a stolen thing's much cheaper than a bought thing!"
"Pearls of wisdom from brother Woljif!"
"If you're gonna be nappin' dogs, go for the smaller ones — the smaller the pup, the bigger the ransom."
"Pearls of wisdom from brother Woljif!"

"If you're floggin' a fake treasure map, take care that all the islands are where they ought to be, or if you add some of your own devisin', at least give 'em normal-soundin' names. 'Lands of Woljif the Great' isn't a good name. It turns out."
"Pearls of wisdom from brother Woljif!"
"When you're on a job, don't go wearin' a big sweepin' cloak: when you're sneakin' about the house, you'll knock over every trinket like an idiot."
"Pearls of wisdom from brother Woljif!"
"When you eat in a tavern, you don't have to pay — just make sure to sit close to the door!"
"If my gran could see me now, I wonder what she'd say?"
"I wonder what put that in my head. Well, that's my night ruined, now I'm gonna hear that ol' hag's voice in my head all day tomorrow."
"Commander, every year mortals celebrate the day they were born, is that right? And today is your birthday, if I'm not mistaken? Well then, happy birthday, Commander!"
"A strange custom... but it seems fun! I wonder if I could have a birthday, too? And if so, when is it?"
"If memory serves, today is our leader's birthday. Many happy returns, Commander!"
"You deserve a great deal more than a humble toast by a campfire, and I hope that soon you will receive all the honors you deserve."

"Birthdays can be lovely occasions, but not if there are demons banging on the door and trying to infect everyone at your party with a magical plague. Or if the god-bothering baroness from the neighboring estate shows up unannounced with her five unmarried daughters in tow. I cannot decide which is more terrifying!"

"But your birthday, dearest Commander, puts every other birthday to shame — a cozy campfire celebration in the middle of a demon invasion! I raise my glass to you with this sincerest wish — savor every moment. Life is to be enjoyed, after all!"
"Today is the birthday of the person who brought all of us together. It's a happy day... and a sad one."
"So many people have died, but we're all still alive. That's worth celebrating."
"I heard that today is my favorite mortal's birthday. Is it true?"
"Come and see me tonight — I'll have a wonderful gift waiting for you... That is, if you are brave enough to unwrap it!"
"Commander! A little bird told me today's your birthday, is that right?"
"Well, then, happy birthday! May you have wit and wariness enough to live to see the next one!"
"Today is the birthday of my incredible friend. Without the Commander, I don't know how we could have fought back against the demons the way we have. Happy birthday!"

"It's great we've lived long enough to see this day — even though the whole Abyss was doing everything it could to see that we didn't. Let's agree to keep our guard up today, to make sure we'll still be here to celebrate your next birthday!"
"Every mortal has exactly one day a year on which their age in years can be represented by a whole number."
"According to my calculations, today is precisely that day for my irreplaceable assistant. Best wishes on this intriguing, but utterly pointless occasion."

"Traditions are the glue that binds society together. I do not advise people to blindly follow tradition in every situation, but nevertheless, I want to honor one of Golarion's most ancient customs today by wishing you a happy birthday."

"Commander, you have already earned your place in the annals of history. My only hope is that the chapters still to be written will serve as inspiration for your contemporaries and as an example for future generations. Accept nothing but excellence from yourself and your companions. And win this war!"
"Wahey! The big day is finally here! The day our fearless leader came into the world!"

"You've got a lot on your shoulders, {name}, but I hope you have a least a little bit of fun on your birthday. I raise my drink to you — may you plow through all adversity like a mastodon through a wattle fence!"
"Commander, your birthday truly is a red letter day. Happy birthday to you — and good wishes to all of us!"
"At the end of the day, without you we would never have come together and achieved all that we have. So this day is for each one of us!"
"Happy birthday, Commander."
"It's good to be among friends again. To wish someone a happy birthday again."
"Down in the caves, we don't place any special meaning on the number of gongs that have passed since birth. We had other things to worry about. Not dying — that was the best gift."
"But you, Commander. You are different. Your arrival into this world, a world destined to bow down before you, is a true cause for celebration!"

"Ah, I love any excuse for a party, me. That goes double for wartime — you need to seize every chance you can get to celebrate. Take today, for instance, it's our leader's birthday. Ain't that great? Happy birthday, chief!"

"Come to think of it — how 'bout we make today a public holiday, y'know, in honor of our leader's birthday? We can take the day off, and just sit here by the fire, drain a flask or two, tell stories, and not have to fight a single mangy demon... Pure paradise!"
"I am just a copy of the real succubus known as Arueshalae..."
"Does that mean that I am innocent? That the evil deeds that haunt me weren't my deeds at all?"
"What does one say when meeting oneself face to face?"
"Personally, I would dispense with the chitchat altogether."
"All this ruminating is unspeakably tedious — who is real, who is a copy..."
"Who fancies a drink?"
"Why don't Valmallos and Ssila'meshnik like each other? They've hurt each other so much, and there was no reason for it!"
"Why do people always act like this?"
"I am a criminal, so finding myself in prison comes as no great shock. And as prison cells go, this one is better than most."
"But that doesn't mean that I won't try to escape. As I said, I am a criminal."
"So if I'm a copy of the real Lann, then does that mean that the fate of the mongrels — that the whole crusade — isn't my concern anymore?"
"Huh. This feels weird. I'm not sure how I'll cope with all this lack of responsibility."
"All of the experiments I have conducted on myself — namely, pinching various body parts — have produced the same result: I exist, I am real."
"Then again, perhaps I am still experiencing the 'denial' stage described in treatises about the mind's response to shock?"
"Valmallos protects the world against destructive magic. His work is worthy of respect."
"It is rare that I meet an enemy deserving of respect."
"Goddess Iomedae, light of my sword, do not forsake me in this hour of darkness..."
"Will the goddess hear me in this world? Do I have the right to pray to her, seeing as how I'm not even a real person?"
"Sometimes when I paint, I think, 'What if this painting is my last?'"
"And the stranger the circumstances we find ourselves in, the greater my desire to paint better. I feel it now."
"Valmallos thinks he has locked us in here. The fool! All he has done is give us free rein to rampage across his realm."
"By the time we get out of here, this place will be nothing but rubble!"

"Well, now's the perfect time for a repeat performance. I might not be the real me, but this Woljif doesn't like being locked up any more than the other one."

"Why's that so hard to believe? I'm hauling sacks around, cutting wheat, and making the... uh... wheel thing turn. I'd like to see you do all that and not build muscle!"
"Wow, who would've thought the city is almost as big underground as it is above ground!"
"Yes, these catacombs have always been a headache for the city authorities. The vast majority are not even documented in our records!"

"I realize you're joking, young man, but knowing our city's bureaucrats the way I do, it wouldn't surprise me in the least."
"Hey, gravedigger! You still alive?"
"I'm alive, Mr. Rekarth, and I feel great! Healthy as a horse — only don't touch me!"
"If haranguing somebody could cure their wounds, then with Inai in our party, we'd be invincible."
"If clowns like you were invincible, then healers wouldn't have to waste their time on people who injure themselves through their own idiocy."
"Langrat, you heard something? Are we being pursued?"

"I bet you feel right at home in this quarter, Langrat. Tell the truth: which one of these mansions is yours?"
"Ah, if only a violinist could afford to live in a mansion... I have spent a lot of time here, it's true, but only as a guest."
"Gods, this place reeks."
"It seems to be my lot in life — if I'm not wading through blood, I'm crawling through shit."
"You think you got me trapped, you cultist scum?"
"Ha! No prison can hold Rekarth for long!"
"How about that, we've literally risen from the grave."
"This will make a great story to tell over a beer... If we don't wind up six feet under before we get the chance."
"Only a week ago, townsfolk would see me and start checking their purses. Now they're asking me for help."
"But let's say I do save them — once the demons are sent packing, we'll be right back to 'Beat it, street rat!'"
"It used to be an ordinary street, but now it's a battlefield. Full of rubble, smoke, screams..."
"Funny, I always felt out of place here before, but now it suits me right down to the ground!"
"Some folks like nothing better than creeping into some crypt, or a bear's den, or a hole bristling with spikes..."
"And yet, here I am, alive and kicking! Sometimes when you go looking for trouble, trouble goes looking for you in the wrong place, and the two of you never meet!"

"I've always been a smiley kind of person, and I haven't died once so far. Maybe my smile is my lucky charm!"
"Hey, have you heard the one about the gnome who fought off the Bleaching so well they turned into a pot of paint?"
"Oh, that's fantastic! I think I'd like that. I wonder what color I'd be? Purple, perhaps? Or a deep azure?"
"My, Bemir, you are a big fellow! I daresay you could take on a giant and win, yes?"
"Yeah right! I don't want to fight anybody. I'm a peaceful guy, you know, wouldn't hurt a fly — but what's this giant done to me, anyhow?"
"Everything's been torn apart, it's like something from a horrible nightmare. But not to worry, they'll build everything back better than before, isn't that right, Frada?"
"I doubt it. This attack will plunge Kenabres into a financial hole much deeper than the catacombs beneath the city."
"It's a pity I didn't get to see Kenabres properly before the invasion. Tell me, Brodie, what was it like here before? Beautiful, I'm sure?"
"I've lived here since I was a child and I've never had a proper look at the place neither. It's all work, work, work — when am I supposed to have had time to take in the sights?"
"Why are ordinary people suddenly turning to demon worship? Could it be a sickness? What do you think, Inai, can cultists be cured?"
"Of course they can. I'll tell you how: a crossbow bolt to the head, and a spear through the belly. Twice daily, morning and night, on an empty stomach."
"Is the violin the only instrument you play? I play the spoons, myself. And a friend of mine produces the most melodious trills on his saw — you would love it!"
"I've never had the pleasure... But if we get out of this alive, come to the theater and we'll put on a concert — your saw and spoons with my orchestra."
"It's so wonderful that it's not just snappers crawling up from the bowels of the earth, but new friends as well!"
"In what way are we friends? We only just met, and you're already getting on my nerves."
"Looking around, it makes you want to weep. All these abandoned homes... like tombstones..."
"Well, while you're weeping, there'll be plenty of scumbags rubbing their hands. To them, these houses are chests full of loot, free for the taking."
"I'm sure this place was beautiful before this calamity! I must return once it's been rebuilt."
"If they rebuild this place exactly as it was, the guards will boot us riffraff out before we can blink."
"My, my. I was so caught up in my reading, I missed the end of the world!"
"But that's nothing. Once, I was reading an engrossing book by the hearth, and didn't notice when my socks caught fire!"
"What's that smell? Bread? Burned sugar?"
"Oh no! There must be a confectioner's shop on fire nearby!"
"Come now, Sendri, get a hold of yourself! Everything will be all right, just keep your chin up!"
"You've survived mountains, forests, deserts — you're hardly going to meet your demise in a city!"
"People say succubi are the ultimate seductresses... but I look at you and think, 'She's an ordinary girl, what's all the fuss about?' I'm not saying you're ugly, far from it..."
"Thank you. No one... has ever said that to me before."
"Could it be that you're not a demon at all, but a foundling? You really don't act like others of your kind."
"Unfortunately, I am more like them than you think. I can never forget who I am."
"Hey, Cami! I like feisty girls who know their own worth. Girls like you. What do you say, think we can make a go of it?"
"I certainly do know my own worth. And it's more than you can afford, rusty."
"You know, gorgeous, I really envy your powers! I've been yammering with the spirits since I was a kid, but now... it's like I've lost all my friends."
"But you have gained abilities that could prove useful to me. I wonder how sharp a blade you could turn into..."
"Be honest, you have a crush on Queen Galfrey, right? So why don't you strike while the iron's hot and ask her to marry you? Afraid she'll turn you down?"
"Did you say, 'marry'? If by 'marry' you mean 'become king,' then I do not know which prospect I find more depressing."
"Dae! Listen, if you're ever going to a party where there'll be pretty girls, make sure to take me with you! I'm feeling a little starved of affection."
"If you can learn how to transform into something capable of pleasuring a woman, I'll take you along as a novelty."
"Sometimes I look at you, child, and I just feel like crying. I pity you, I suppose. No offense."
"You want to cry because you look at me and you see yourself. But I am nothing like you."
"Have you never wanted to go back home? Why would you stick around here in the mud and dust, surrounded by warriors?"

"I've been so distracted, I can't even remember when I last ate."
"Ah, who cares, if I don't remember, it probably doesn't matter."
"I'm surrounded by pretty girls and not one of them will even look at me!"
"Maybe they're just not looking for love right now. The crusade is a serious business."
"We'd love to have you in the Pathfinders! Your kind of talent is rare these days!"

"Why are you looking at me so closely? It's not like I have any fancy patterns on me!"
"I was thinking that many of my fellow professionals would cut off their hand to get a thing like you. You would be an exceptionally useful and versatile... partner."

"And why can't you just leave me alone? I've met bear traps less clingy than you!"

"The Abyss can pervert every good intention. In the Wound, even nature itself seems to be laughing at us."

"Hey, sneak-thief! You think I don't know what you're up to? You think nobody's watching, but I'm here!"

"I'm bein' lectured by a hunk of metal! No mouth or brains, but somehow that doesn't stop you doling out life advice! And how's your life workin' out there, pal?"
"I'm glad the Commander has found happiness — even if it's not with me."
"It hurts, but it is a wonderful pain that most demons will never know."
"Camellia, I just want to say that I bear you no grudge and that I am happy for you and the Commander. Love is a wonderful feeling. Please treasure it."
"We are simply together, which suits the two of us. Love does not come into it."

"Daeran, he's... behaving differently around the Commander. I think I can guess what it means."

"That guy — he's just a mess of contradictions, all spiky insults on the outside and a tangle of personal demons on the inside. I pity the person he falls hard for. And if anyone happens to fall for him, well, I pity Daeran, too."

"Relax, friend. Here, take a swig from this flask and think about something good."
"I just wish I too could love someone and be loved in return..."

"Thank you for the warning, my dearest Camellia. I am so delighted to have someone like you by my side — a true and compassionate friend!"

"That Dimalchio seemed so charming at first... What came over him?"

"Stop making eyes at the Commander. It's disgusting."

"Wenduag, I am sorry the Commander chose me and not you. I am sure you will find your own special someone who will love your beauty and kind heart."
"I just had a thought — if something happens to you, the Commander and I will have another chance."
"My dear Camellia, you know that I can sense veiled tension in my travel companions and interlocutors. Care to tell me who has won your favor? May I be of any assistance?"

"Praise from the connoisseur of debauchery himself? Why, Count, that means a great deal. Thank you."

"The bedchamber as a place of violence? It seems perverse to me. Would you not agree, Count?"

"So, Lann and the Commander. With complete sympathy, I am willing to wager two thousand that our scaly friend makes a complete hash of things. What say you, Greybor?"

"You're right. I hope I don't lose this tiny flame. I hope I can keep it from going out."

"I haven't the faintest idea to whom you could possibly be referring."

"Camellia, I think something has changed about the way you look at the Commander. Every time your eyes are on him, it suddenly feels warmer."

"Lann and the Commander are together, and Count Arendae owes me four thousand gold. Things are looking up, I reckon."
"I do not know which is worse — fraternization within the unit or other unit members trying to enrich themselves by betting on the outcome of the fraternization."

"Why are you glaring at me? Thinking about killing me, are you?"

"You got what you wanted. Power, influence, and... a partner you desired. I guess I underestimated you and your ambition. Forgive me."

"I cannot express how delighted I was to hear that the succubus Arueshalae was once again behind bars. But now I see she has been freed."

"The Commander's no fool. It's all part of some plan to make Wenduag think she's in control."

"She's not a succubus anymore. Trust a paladin to know — we can tell the difference between good and evil, unlike you."
"I previously noted that Cleric Vaenic was naive and frivolous, and that foolish display with the orchestra is just the latest proof."

"Don't worry about him. He's not alone. The Commander is looking after his light."

"Loving means yielding to another person sometimes, and that's where he's going to run into trouble. But I wish them all the best! I hope it works out."
"You did what? Invited her to spar with you? Lann, getting punched in the face — that's not a date."

"Keep it down! What was I supposed to do? Say, 'Let's go for a romantic stroll around the Wound! The moon's only slightly red tonight, and the creatures whose calls sound like crying babies are quieter than usual!"
"Not planning on any more training sessions with the Commander, are you? Decided to change tack and started a brawl in a tavern to get her attention?"
"I don't remember asking for your advice. But I can guess what it might be — praying to Iomedae together?"
"How could you go and get hitched just like that? And no big bash to celebrate? I would have helped."
"I don't even know how it happened. One minute everything's normal, the next I'm standing in front of an altar! And it's never too late for a party."
"I'm actually a little happy for Wenduag and the Commander. Loneliness often drives people toward evil. But having someone to be close to does the opposite."

"What you and the Commander did in the temple of Iomedae — it's insane! I don't even know how to describe it!"
"Thank you, you are too kind."
"I understand why the Commander chose you, Camellia. You are beautiful, your manners are impeccable, many people can only dream of having a lady like you on their arm."
"Thank you. I hope you also find a worthy companion, Sosiel, someone from your side of the social gulf that yawns between us."
"You must declare your feelings, Lann. I am sure she will understand everything. But getting drunk and starting fights, you will only hurt yourself and her that way."
"Are you our resident professor of love or something? Back off."
"Lann can be quite harsh, but with the Commander he's totally different, it's like magic. I wonder if he..."
"I noticed the same thing. I think you're right. He's really..."
"People say love can put even an inveterate scoundrel on the straight and narrow. What do you think? Is there a love that can reform a villain like Wenduag?"
"You're a good guy, Sosiel. You see goodness and love wherever you look. But I think Wenduag's feelings for the Commander are something different."
"The Commander may have rejected my love in the end — but I do not regret a single thing."
"It was wonderful. Every moment."
"I'm sure Lann and the Commander's wedding was beautiful, but... I also had a speech prepared, and if I'd been asked, I would have been happy to give it."
"What am I thinking? They're happy — that's what matters!"
"You need to be very careful. If you slip up, the Commander will never forgive you. I'm always forgiven, no matter what — we have a special understanding. But such mercy isn't for the likes of you."
"Go away. Don't talk to me about the power that passion can give one person over another. I know that far better than you. Don't wake the monster within me — or you could be its first victim."
"You stole a tasty morsel from me! But don't you worry, I'll get you back for this, wretch!"
"You call the Commander a 'tasty morsel'? Perhaps that's why I was chosen, and not you?"
"What a ridiculous present — flowers! They're pointless! How could anyone think this silly gesture is a promise of burning passion?"
"Don't sulk, my dear Wenduag. It was but a friendly gesture, it does not mean anything. Would you like me to give you flowers too? Something suited to your tender heart... daisies, perhaps?"
"Too bad the Commander has staked a claim on you, golden boy. Passion has turned you into a true predator!"
"A predator? There's something to that, you know. I am beginning to understand your perspective on things, Wenduag. Where there is passion, power, and freedom, there is no room for anything else."
"That soft priest is no partner for the Commander. A great military leader should have a great warrior by their side!"
"The Commander knows better than you. We've got a whole army of great warriors here, but see if you can find another comely lad like Sosiel in this crusade. The lad does bore me to tears, though."
"What's the sour look for, Sosiel? Going to start crying that the Commander chose me over you? You're such a whiner, ha ha ha!"
"What kind of a person laughs at another's heartbreak? A monster, I think, a monster who doesn't even have a heart!"
"Does that little bitch Arueshalae think I don't see her looking at the Commander? Ha, they can enjoy themselves as much as they want, they have my permission."
"But if she tries to come between us, I'll cut her pretty face so no one will ever look twice at her again. Succubus whore!"
"I can't figure you out, Arueshalae. Who in their right mind would willingly put themselves behind bars?"
"I did it for myself and for other people because I didn't want... I don't think anything I say will help you understand me."
"What's so special about Lann, eh? It's gotta be all those muscles — the chest, the shoulders... But scrawny guys deserve love too, I say!"
"Allow me to give you some advice: do not refer to yourself as 'scrawny.' Say: 'slender as a sapling,' 'lithe as a rapier,' and there you have it — I like you more already."

"They're happy, and you're sad that you're not happy too. I can hold your hand for a while if you want?"

"Hey, Sosiel! I heard you like to play cards. Wanna game?"
"You want to clean out my pockets? I know you're a cardsharp... But I suppose, why not? Let's play!"
"Hey, Camellia! I see the way you've been eyin' up the Commander! Especially when he's not looking, heh."
"Uh, Camellia? Why are you lookin' at me like that? I didn't mean nothin' by it, honest. I was just sayin'. I'll shut up now."
"Everybody condemns Nurah, I know... but deep down I understand her. She had nowhere to go, at least the demons gave her some kind of purpose in life."
"I have thought a lot about her betrayal, but I feel pity rather than hatred for her. Horrific lives lead many people to commit horrific acts."
"She is a traitor, of course, but if she wanted to come back and promised to make things right, I wouldn't execute her."
"I'm not surprised that a traitor shows compassion to a fellow traitor. Nurah Dendiwhar deserves death."
"She got caught, silly little fool. If you can't hunt stealthily, don't go after the big game."
"It's a shame the Bell of Mercy would burn me if I touched it. But I feel drawn to it like... a moth to a dame. Or is it flame? What's the expression?"
"So this here bell only hurts demons and cultists, right? I'm just worried that if we ring it, my tail will drop off or somethin'. I bet it'll happen!"
"To a flame, Arueshalae. A moth is drawn to a flame. I'm sorry — I should not have corrected you! I hope you are not offended."
"Where do all these things come from? Was Desna just clearing out some old junk in Elysium one day and thought we'd like it?"
"Uplanders rely too heavily on magical artifacts like this bell. That is why they are so easily defeated."
"To a flame, not to a dame. But I like the sound of your version! It's good to shake up these old sayings, or to even come up with your own!"

"I know it's very bold of me, but I would like to meet Queen Galfrey. I'd like to talk to her, perhaps ask her for advice... She has been fighting the chaos and evil that give rise to creatures like me for so many years. I wish I had her courage."
"There's a reason why she's our warrior queen! One look from her steels you for victory!"
"A leader willing to join the fray is an inspiration to their troops. But even better inspiration would be tangible results."

"Oh, rest assured, Arueshalae, cousin Galfrey is the worthiest, most even-handed do-gooder that has ever lived among mortals. With a single word, she can set hearts ablaze and give new meaning to life. I would be delighted to introduce you. It should be a... thrilling encounter."

"If she had won her power in battle, by killing a dozen strong rivals, then maybe even I'd welcome her advice. But she received her place through the stupid uplander right of birth. What's to admire about that?"
"I got a look at ol' Galfrey — a dame like any other, nothin' special! If you dressed me up in jewels and a crown, I'd look like a hoity-toity queen, too!"
"I never wanted to breathe this rank air again, but as soon as we arrived in Alushinyrra, my heart started racing. I have come home... But can I call this place home now?"
