"Only dogs run joyously to play in muck and offal. I always suspected you were no better than an animal."
"Everybody's just running around and shouting — how is that madness? Real madness is a nightmare that you can't escape even when you're awake."
"Did you ever consider that you might be one of those doomed souls one day and call for help? You'll be glad of people like us then."
"Now the whole fortress is ours! A huge fortress, big as a city! Now the peoples of Golarion will bow down before us..."
"Uh, you do remember who we're fighting against, right?"
"Oh look, isn't she sweet when she's happy?"
"So ignorant. This is not even the largest and best-fortified citadel in Mendev, let alone Golarion."
"I had never seen so much fire before I came to Kenabres. The smell of smoke seems to follow me everywhere now! But I cannot say that I find the smell... unpleasant."
"You could bathe, perhaps. That may help."
"You, too? So I'm not the only one who always smells smoke everywhere! It started for me after me and my father came to the city."
"I don't think that will be the last fire you'll see. Only next time, it will be the demons burning!"
"It's a cryin' shame about the town, but it was a tough place for an enterprisin' thief to find his feet. It's time to conquer new heights and all that stuff!"
"A swarm of vescavors is power incarnate, destroying everything in its path! But what is the point of such power if you're too mindless to enjoy it?"
"I am glad that even your thirst for power has its limits... Forgive me, that sounded like sarcasm, but I truly am glad."
"Exactly! How can you enjoy life if your only goal is to kill everything in your path?"
"What method will help me understand the functioning of a hive mind? Will observation from a distance be sufficient, or will I have to place the hive on my head?"
"My, my, what complex philosophical musings! You are discovering the world for yourself, how darling!"
"War on the surface is not like skirmishes among the cave tribes. But I will achieve perfection in this arena as well."
"War is both a science and an art. To master both aspects, you need a disciplined mind. Until you acquire that discipline, you will understand nothing of war."
"Right, war is nothing like a one-on-one fight where you get to look the other person in the eye. But at least here you can feel that you're not alone!"
"Chaos, blood... they are horrible, but we must wade through it all to win and see a better world."
"I do not understand why Areelu abandoned this laboratory but did not destroy it. She opened the Worldwound but did not cover her tracks!"
"Sounds sensible. Even if you fear nothing and no one, there's no reason to leave evidence at the scene of the crime."

"She did not abandon it, she simply suspended its operation, and she will one day return. A true scientist never loses their hunger for knowledge! Opened a planar rift? Then you need to open another one, to confirm the results of the first experiment!"
"She isn't you. She's interested in more than... wait — you've actually made me defend Areelu Vorlesh!"
"The laboratory appears to be abandoned. But is it truly? I doubt it."
"We should have taken Xanthir alive! I could have learned how he made the demons stronger and used that knowledge!"
"But you are already strong. You don't need other people's secrets, you are enough on your own."
"If you got what you wanted, you'd have chewed us all up by now! No, I think you should stay just the way you are."
"What need have you of greater strength? You have already conquered my heart with your gentle words and angelic nature!"
"That power would have destroyed you. Or is that what you want — self-destruction?"
"Alushinyrra... now here's a city to my taste. There is life here, there is struggle! I could be chief here!"
"You think you are on an equal footing with Shamira and Nocticula? You, the ill-kempt arachnid from the caves? I have not laughed this much in an age!"
"I reckon you could do it. If you know the right people, meaning demons, you could rise here. But you didn't hear it from me!"
"Power can corrupt even those with iron principles. What, then, will power do to you?"
"But what you need is freedom and hunting. You'll be sad sitting on a throne all day."
"That bitch Nocticula stole our victory over Baphomet! Curse that devious wretch!"
"You reckon we could've just taken him ourselves? All I want to do is thank her."

"If a reward was owed for Baphomet's head and Nocticula had claimed it, then I could understand your frustration. As it is, what she did was not very polite, but nothing more than that. We've suffered no financial loss."
"Before Nocticula became a demon lord, she killed one of them using cunning, not strength. That is how she removed Baphomet from her path. She acted as is her custom."
"Devious, but dangerous and powerful. Her strikes are so decisive, so inevitable... the thought alone is quite mesmerizing."
"Nocticula and Iomedae... They are powerful, those two arrogant shrews. But I'm sure they both have a weakness, which means they can both be defeated!"
"Summon a healer, Wenduag wishes to do battle with some goddesses. With two at once, my sweet, or are you going to be sensible and take them on one at a time?"
"Poor you, you're scared! Don't worry, they might be stronger than you, but they won't touch you."
"Please, do not even think of it. Angering the gods is too dangerous."
"Your enthusiasm is laudable, mongrel girl! Please be sure to tell me if you discover any of the gods' weaknesses. And do not forget to bequeath your body to science before you start investigating!"
"Life can change in the blink of an eye! Yesterday I was thinkin' I had it all figured out, no surprises for me, and now today I'm dragging myself someplace with a gang of... uh, strangers."
"Did you say 'gang'? I shall say this only once, thief: I do not wish to be viewed as a member of a gang!"
"What about me? I'm not a stranger, am I? I remember when you were little, you threw rocks at me like the other boys. See, we even have some shared memories."
"I understand. This whole gang thing just kinda fell on top of me. And now I'm here."
"You should be pleased. More fighting means more riches — isn't that what you're after?"

"Wardstone, Wardstone... I wouldn't mind gettin' a closer look at the thing. Maybe take a little piece... Only with the best intentions, honest! Magical stuff is my specialty, maybe I'll tinker with it to make it even better at chasin' away demons!"
"So everyone is supposed to believe that you, a known coward, want to drive off the demons, and not take the first opportunity to flee somewhere warm and safe?"

"An excellent idea, tiefling boy! I am also planning to take samples for study as soon as we get close enough to the Wardstone. I will likely need a decent pick and a wheelbarrow, no, wait, make that a wagon!"

"You dummy, it's not just an artifact, it's a divine gift. Do you know who put it here in Kenabres? The Hand of the Inheritor, that's who! The herald of Iomedae and general of the armies of Heaven. So I don't think a toerag like you can improve it."
"If I had a stash in the Gray Garrison like those guys, would I have gone there, riskin' my tail? What's worth more to me — my tail or my loot?"
"I just crawled up to the surface and I've already met a philosopher! What other universal problems are troubling you?"
"That's why thieves live short, sad lives — many of them don't put any value on life, they all think that money is more important."
"Life is worth more. As long as you're alive, you can get more gold. But you are an idiot, so you won't make money no matter how long you live."
"In structure, your tail seems to be similar to a cat's, but manual examination is not conclusive... Tell me, would you miss it if it was removed?"
"These Nahyndrian crystals are right little beauties, no mistakin' it. It's like they're beckonin' to me. They look expensive and all. I wonder how much I could get for one of 'em?"
"I will make sure that your pack and your person are thoroughly searched every day, thief."
"These crystals are like the girls who used to throw rocks at me: so pretty, but they don't know the harm they're doing."
"Those crystals would look superb in a tiara. And a tiara would look superb perched atop my golden head."

"Still, things ain't too bad in Drezen, it's almost like being in a real city! I just wish the patrols stopped draggin' me up in front of Irabeth all the time. It's like I can't walk into a store, or take an innocent peek inside a warehouse without being suspected of something!"
"It's your own fault. You're lucky they don't know half of what you got up to with those cultists!"
"Is it possible you entered the premises with dishonest intentions, but you have forgotten? I could try to hypnotize you and restore your memory!"
"Please forgive their prejudice. Everyone is on high alert, but give them time and they will get used to you and accept you."

"I know how you feel. Some people say that demons and tieflings do not belong in a fortress blessed by Iomedae. But we cannot give up. We will keep fighting on their side, and sooner or later they will come to see us as true allies."
"Now I've seen gramps, and great-grandpa Baphomet... I won't be surprised if mom and dad pop outta nowhere and try to wring my neck."
"The higher you rise in life, the more people will try to take you down, and we all have risen high. Even you, worm, have become someone of note, thanks to the Commander."

"By my preliminary evaluation, the chances of such a thing are quite low. But it is an intriguing prospect, having the chance to witness such a rare phenomenon. If it happens, congratulations in advance!"
"Baphomet is a deadly and devious demon lord, but even his blood in your veins has not made you any more intelligent or capable."

"Blood ties matter little to demons — descendants are just a resource to be exploited. Do not take it to heart, Woljif. It is best not to think of this again. And do not be fooled if any demon ever tries to lure you into a trap by appealing to family affection — I have seen such a thing more than once."
"Come on, who wants to go first? Rate Nocticula on a scale of one to ten!"
"I'd give her ten stabs in the back out of ten. No, actually, twelve out of ten."
"I cannot believe I am saying this, but I believe Iomedae is the more beautiful of the two. There is something about her sublime haughtiness that I like."
"She is strong, dangerous, imperious. She will be the one to judge when the time comes, not the other way around."

"Oh, tiefling boy, you are conducting your own experiments! I was just in the middle of working on my Universal Scale for the Measurement of Strength of (Semi-)Divine Beings. We should compare our findings!"
"That Deskari's got an ugly mug on him, doesn't he? And he thinks he's the best and the smartest, but we got one over on him. I wish I was as full of myself!"
"A typical spoiled prince who steps beyond his estate for the first time and realizes that the world could not care less who he is. I have no idea what that feels like."
"Did you know that Deskari's scythe is made from his mother's skeleton? Does that mean that he feels positively toward his mother, or the opposite?"
"Your confidence is far from lacking, never fear. I do not even know what could knock it, even. Perhaps the feeling of helplessness and slowly approaching death..."
"We are stronger than this demon. Stronger than the hunger of the Abyss itself. Ha! How sweet it is — to know that you are stronger."
"Giants are an ancient race. They had lived here for millennia before your first cities were founded."
"And what is the greatest achievement of their civilization? '1,000 Years Of Cannibalism: The Cookbook'?"
"As stars are set upon their course by fate, and gods are bound by strictures all their own"
"So destiny will always choose to wait, and claim those few who claim it as their own..."
"I can't think of anything more monstrous than a giant. They're huge, evil and ravenous... At least there's a silver lining: no giant will ever sneak up on you."
"Sure they won't! You can hear them coming from miles away — and in case you're hard of hearing, there's still their stench."
"Ugh, the stench is unbearable! How can the giants themselves stand it?"
"You'll just have to get used to it. If you were a giant, this'd be the sweet smell of home."
"Goblin songs are not devoid of interest. They have a rather unique approach to making music — I even picked up a couple of techniques from them."
"Sadly, their lyrics are not up to par. From what I have heard so far, their vocabulary consists almost entirely of synonyms for 'gobble' and 'whack.'"
"Goblins chew and goblins bite, goblins cut and goblins fight!"
"Bones be cracked, flesh be stewed, we be goblins! You be food!"
"Now this is a proper royal palace! Every single room reeks of its owner's snobbery."

"I don't know. Looks nice enough to me... What if you could conjure up a perfect dwelling for yourself? Your imagination is the limit. What would it be? A single empty room with a lonely army bunk inside?"
"Goblins are so merry and cheerful! If they weren't so bloodthirsty, they'd be decent chaps."
"Then they'd have been called gnomes."
"A curious fact: the creatures we mortals know as kytons do not actually use this name among themselves. 'Kyton' came about due to a translation error thousands of years ago."
"Know what I'd like to call those butchers? "Nonexistent." Actually, I'd rather not call them anything at all. I don't even want to think about them!"
"Can you hear him waking, up above the stairs? Can you hear him weeping, is he really there?"
"Can you say 'I'm speaking,' are you saying naught? Is it you who's weeping, is it you he's caught?"

"When I was in prison, I kept reminding myself that the world did not end there in my cell. That there's more to the world than chains and bars... And here we are, on a plane of reality where chains and bars are all there is. Thinking about it gives me the creeps."
"Better to think of Heaven, Nirvana, or Elysium. If we can get to the Shadow World alive, maybe we can get there, too."
"It's so creepy in here... I'm not sure I'll even be able to sleep tonight."
"Shut your eyes and your mouth right now! The last thing we need in battle is a sleep-deprived gnome."
"A jungle and a boreal forest a stone's throw from each other... Have you ever seen such an unusual landscape, Sendri?"

"I have seen plenty of natural wonders in my travels, but this one seems to have magical origins. I cannot tell for sure who is responsible, though. Could be demons, could be fey, could be someone else."
"Brothers far and brothers near, are you overcome with fear?"
"Soon comes your time now to be brave, for your own lives you must save!"
"I wonder how many such settlements are scattered all over the Worldwound. Besieged by demons, isolated, lost and forgotten... How hard must it be for them just to survive."
"It is a perpetual struggle indeed. I hope the knights of the new crusade find them all and rescue them!"
"It's a pity that one shard bearer can only sense the other's presence very vaguely. It might take us weeks to find him in these woods!"
"I, for one, am glad of it. Have you asked yourself what would happen if that other shard bearer set out to find us?"
"I first came to the Abyss during the Second Crusade. Now we are in the middle of the Fifth..."
"According to my calculations, it would take at least twenty-five more to stop the demons for good."
"Sharpen the blades, tighten the bowstring, check if the armor pieces fit..."
"I cannot be prepared for everything, but at least I will not be the one to blame if things go to the Abyss."
"My tavern, my sweet tavern..."
"I'll dream of you next time I'm sleeping in a frozen puddle of mud."
"What a day! The stars have circled the sky once more, and you are celebrating another birthday today, unless I've miscalculated?"
"Congratulations, warchief! You are our leader, and not during peacetime, but war. It falls to you to deal with this pain in the rear — and you're doing a fine job of it!"
"So I'm a replica of the real succubus Arueshalae?"
"Oh, how I long to meet my other self. How many insights and new experiences we could discover together..."
"Everything I remember... never happened to me. Everything happened to the other Trever, the real Trever."
"So who am I, then?"
"I can understand Valmallos. Maintaining order is important, especially when the entire world is at stake."
"But even so — I am not guilty of anything, and I refuse to be condemned to this dungeon."
"Hey-ho the derry-o... With his cheeks aflame and his trews down low..."
"This bawdy tavern song is a timeless classic. I guarantee it will be stuck in your head for days."
